Radiation modulates both tumor cells and immune cells, yet the precise mechanism linking tumor cells to immune cells that drives radiation-mediated tumor suppression remains poorly understood. We demonstrate that radiation rapidly activates the p65/p50 and p50/p50 NF-kB complexes in human soft tissue sarcoma (STS) cells, which bind to the TNFa promoter to enhance its transcription. Radiation-induced TNFa triggers autocrine tumor cell death. A sublethal dose of Smac mimetic BV6 promotes degradation of cIAP1 and cIAP2, increasing tumor cell sensitivity to radiation-induced apoptosis in vitro and enhancing radiation suppression of STS xenografts in vivo. Inhibition of caspases, RIP1, or RIP3 blocks radiation/TNFa-induced cell death, while RIP1 inhibition prevents TNFa-induced caspase activation, indicating sequential roles for caspases and RIP1 in non-compensatory cell death pathways. In a syngeneic sarcoma model, radiation up-regulates IRF3, IFNb, and T cell chemokines CCL2 and CCL5, correlating with Th1/Tc1 T cell activation and infiltration. Tumor-infiltrating T cells are functionally active, as both perforin and FasL pathways are activated in irradiated tissues. Combined BV6 and radiation completely suppress tumor growth in vivo, highlighting NF-kB's role in linking tumor cells to immune cells for radiation-mediated suppression.

title: Conditional Knockout of LIF Receptor in Uterine Epithelium Disrupts Implantation
abstract: Targeted deletion of the LIF Receptor in the murine uterine epithelium leads to implantation failure. Leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF) is critical for preparing the uterus for blastocyst implantation. In mice, LIFR expression is primarily localized to the uterine luminal epithelium (LE). LIF, secreted from endometrial glands (GEs), binds to the LIFR, initiating the Janus kinase-signal transducer and activation of transcription (STAT) 3 (Jak-Stat3) signaling pathway in the LE. Activation of JAK-STAT converts the LE to a receptive state, enabling blastocysts to implant. To specifically eliminate LIFR in the LE, we generated mice with Cre recombinase inserted into the lactoferrin gene (Ltf-Cre). Lactoferrin expression in the LE is upregulated by E2, and Cre activity is restricted to the LE and GE. To assess LIFR's role in implantation, we created a conditional Lifr flx/flx mouse line. Crossing Ltf-Cre with Lifr flx/flx produced Lifr flx/D : Ltf Cre/+ females that appeared normal but were infertile. Many females failed to become pregnant despite repeated mating. Unimplanted blastocysts transferred to wild-type recipients implanted normally, indicating uterine receptivity was compromised. Loss of Lifr prevented STAT3 nuclear translocation and reduced Msx1 expression, a gene regulating uterine receptivity. These findings confirm that LIFR expression in the uterus is essential for implantation and identify key components of the LIF signaling pathway involved. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: kinase-signal transducer and activation of transcription ( STAT ) 3.

title: Mechanisms of L-asparaginase Resistance in Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
abstract: Genome-wide screening of gene functions reveals opioid receptor u1 as a critical factor in L-asparaginase resistance in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia. L-asparaginase is essential for treating acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), as it breaks down plasma asparagine into aspartate and NH3, leading to asparagine deficit and inhibition of protein synthesis, which ultimately results in leukemic cell death. However, resistance to L-asparaginase develops in many patients, and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. To identify genes involved in resistance, we performed RNAi screening on primary leukemic cells, finding that six out of ten resistant clones contained opioid receptor u1 (oprm1), two had carbonic anhydrase 1 (ca1), and two were associated with ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme E2C (ube2c). OPRM1 expression was detected in all tested leukemic cells. Knockdown of OPRM1 increased resistance to L-asparaginase, confirming our screening results. Methadone, an OPRM1 agonist, enhances the sensitivity of parental leukemic cells to L-asparaginase but not in OPRM1-depleted cells, indicating OPRM1's role in the synergistic effect of L-asparaginase and methadone. Leukemic cells with high OPRM1 levels are more responsive to L-asparaginase, suggesting OPRM1 loss contributes to resistance. This study identifies OPRM1 as a novel biomarker for high-risk ALL subpopulations and for detecting resistant clones. OPRM1 may offer new therapeutic strategies for L-asparaginase-resistant ALL.

title: Photochemoprevention of UVB-induced Skin Lesions and Carcinogenesis
abstract: Exposure to ultraviolet B (UVB) radiation is linked to a range of adverse effects on human health, including basal and squamous cell cancers, melanoma, cataracts, and epidermal hyperplasia. These effects are exacerbated by increased UVB exposure due to lifestyle changes, leading to a rise in skin cancer incidence. Skin cancer development involves initiation, promotion, and progression stages, with each phase marked by DNA damage, inflammation, and altered signal transduction pathways. UVB exposure stimulates cyclooxygenase activity, increasing prostaglandin synthesis and inducing ornithine decarboxylase expression. Antioxidant compounds have shown potential in mitigating UVB-induced damage by reducing oxidative stress and enhancing DNA repair mechanisms. Photochemoprevention strategies, such as topical agents and botanical antioxidants, are being explored to counteract UVB effects. The use of sunscreens combined with antioxidant-rich skin care products may offer a protective approach against UVB-induced photodamage and skin cancer. Additionally, the relationship between inflammation and carcinogenesis remains a critical area of research, as persistent inflammatory responses can contribute to the progression of skin and other diseases.

title: Genetic Linkage and Clinical Features of High Hyperopia and Leber Congenital Amaurosis in a Family with CRB1 Mutations
abstract: A G1103R mutation in CRB1 is co-occurring with high hyperopia and Leber congenital amaurosis in a Middle Eastern family. This study aimed to identify the genetic basis of recessive inheritance of high hyperopia and LCA. Patients underwent standard ophthalmic evaluations, and DNA was analyzed for genetic linkage using polymorphic markers near known LCA genes. Exons were amplified and sequenced. All four family members with LCA exhibited high to extreme hyperopia, with average spherical refractive errors ranging from +5.00 to +10.00. Linkage to 1q31.3 was confirmed with a LOD score of 5.20, revealing a G1103R mutation in exon 9 of CRB1. CRB1, a vertebrate homolog of the Drosophila crumbs gene, is associated with either retinitis pigmentosa or LCA. This variant has been previously reported in a sporadic LCA case. While hyperopia is typically moderate in LCA, this family's extreme hyperopia suggests a direct link to the CRB1 mutation. Additionally, some CRB1 mutations can cause either RP or LCA. High hyperopia and LCA are linked to the mutant CRB1 gene, independent of unlinked modifiers. Retinitis pigmentosa is associated with CRB1, but high hyperopia is not linked to crumbs.

title: MDMA Use and Cognitive Impairments in Recreational Users
abstract: MDMA polydrug users demonstrate impairments in social and emotional judgement processes, which are associated with memory deficits. Recent studies have highlighted the impact of MDMA on cognitive functions, including deficits in memory updating and set shifting. This study examined the effects of MDMA use on prefrontal-mediated processes, revealing significant impairments in both social-emotional judgment and memory functions. The findings suggest a positive correlation between MDMA exposure and impaired social and emotional judgement processes, as well as memory deficits, underscoring the cognitive risks associated with recreational MDMA use.

title: Tumor Thymidylate Synthase 1494del6 Genotype as a Prognostic Factor in Colorectal Cancer Patients Receiving Fluorouracil-Based Treatment
abstract: Tumor thymidylate synthase 1494del6 genotype was evaluated as a prognostic marker in colorectal cancer patients undergoing fluorouracil-based adjuvant therapy. This study aimed to assess the significance of germline and tumor thymidylate synthase (TS) genotyping in a cohort of 129 colorectal cancer patients treated with FU plus levamisole or leucovorin. TS enhancer region 3R G > C single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) and TS 1494del6 polymorphisms were analyzed in normal mucosa and tumor tissues. Mutational analysis of TS and allelic imbalances were conducted in primary tumors and 18 metachronous metastases. TS protein immunostaining was performed on 214 tumors. Multivariate Cox models were adjusted for stage, differentiation, and location. Results showed that tumor genotyping (allelic loss frequency, 26%) revealed the 3R/3R genotype was associated with improved outcomes (hazard ratio = 0.38; 95% CI, 0.16 to 0.93; P = .020). Tumor TS 1494del6 allele (allelic loss frequency, 36%) was protective (HR = 0.42; 95% CI, 0.22 to 0.82; P = .0034). Both polymorphisms were in strong linkage disequilibrium (D' = 0.71; P < .001), and the 3R/-6 base pair haplotype showed significant survival benefit compared with the most prevalent 2R/+6bp haplotype (HR = 0.42; 95% CI, 0.20 to 0.85; P = .017). No TS point mutations were detected in primary tumors or metastases. TS protein immunostaining was not linked to survival or genotypes. Tumor TS 1494del6 genotype may serve as a prognostic factor in FU-based adjuvant treatment of colorectal cancer patients.

title: Valproate-Induced Chorea and Encephalopathy in Atypical Nonketotic Hyperglycinemia
abstract: Nonketotic hyperglycinemia is a disorder of amino acid metabolism characterized by a defect in the glycine cleavage system, leading to glycine accumulation in the brain and other tissues. In the classical form, it presents with neonatal apnea, intractable seizures, and hypotonia, followed by psychomotor retardation. Atypical variants manifest in a varied manner, such as language delay and mental retardation. This report describes a patient who developed acute encephalopathy and chorea shortly after starting Valproate therapy. The diagnosis of nonketotic hyperglycinemia was confirmed following these symptoms. The association between Valproate-induced effects and chorea, as well as encephalopathy, highlights the need for careful monitoring in such cases. The presence of glycine in the patient's condition is linked to the nonketotic hyperglycinemia, but no direct correlation was found between glycine and other symptoms.

title: Bone morphogenetic protein-4 Modulates Gonadotrophin Secretion via Interactions with Activin and GnRH
abstract: Bone morphogenetic protein-4 interacts with activin-stimulated and GnRH to modulate gonadotrophin secretion in LbetaT2 gonadotrophs. In sheep primary pituitary cells, bone morphogenetic proteins (BMP)-4 inhibits FSHbeta mRNA expression and FSH release. In contrast, in mouse LbetaT2 gonadotrophs, BMPs stimulate basal or activin-stimulated FSHbeta promoter-driven transcription. Using LbetaT2 cells, we investigated the effects of BMP-4 on gonadotrophin mRNA and secretion modulated by activin and GnRH. BMP-4 alone had no effect on FSH production but enhanced activin+GnRH-induced stimulation of FSHbeta mRNA and FSH secretion, without affecting follistatin mRNA. BMP-4 reduced LHbeta mRNA up-regulation in response to GnRH (±activin) and decreased GnRH receptor expression, favoring FSH over LH synthesis and secretion. Unlike sheep pituitary gonadotrophs, which express only BMP receptor types IA (BMPRIA) and II (BMPRII), LbetaT2 cells also express BMPRIB. Smad1/5 phosphorylation induced by BMP-4, indicating BMP signaling activation, was consistent whether BMP-4 was used alone or combined with activin/±GnRH. We hypothesized that activin and/or GnRH pathways may be modulated by BMP-4, but neither activin-stimulated Smad2/3 phosphorylation nor GnRH-induced ERK1/2 or cAMP response element-binding phosphorylation were modified. However, GnRH-induced p38 MAPK activation was decreased by BMP-4, associated with increased FSHbeta mRNA and FSH secretion, but decreased LHbeta mRNA levels. These results confirm 1. BMPs as key modulators of activin and/or GnRH-stimulated gonadotrophin synthesis and release, and 2. important species differences in these effects, likely due to variations in BMP receptor expression in gonadotrophs. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: BMP receptor types IA ( BMPRIA ) and II ( BMPRII ).

title: Polymorphisms in Thymidylate Synthase Gene and Their Impact on Survival in Colorectal Cancer Patients Treated with 5-Fluorouracil
abstract: This study investigated the influence of thymidylate synthase (7298) gene polymorphisms on survival outcomes in patients with colorectal cancer (D015179) undergoing 5 fluorouracil-treated (D005472) therapy. The analysis focused on three genetic variants: a 28 bp variable number of tandem repeats (c|DUP||28), a G/C single nucleotide polymorphism (c|SUB|G||C), and a deletion of 6 bp at position 1494 (c|DEL|194|6). Paraffin-embedded (D010232) tissue samples from 113 patients with advanced colorectal cancer were examined, including rectal cancers (D012004). The study employed polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for VNTR analysis and PCR-RFLP for SNP and ins/del 6 bp genotyping. Results indicated that the 28 bp VNTR was associated with colorectal cancer progression, while the G/C SNP showed no significant correlation. A deletion of 6 bp at position 1494 was linked to the thymidylate synthase gene (7298). The 5 fluorouracil-treated (D005472) regimen demonstrated a positive correlation with the ins/del 6 bp polymorphism, whereas a negative correlation was observed between 5 fluorouracil-treated (D005472) and colorectal cancer survival. Tumour (D009369) subtypes showed varied genetic profiles, with rectal cancers (D012004) exhibiting distinct VNTR distributions. The study highlights the complex interplay between genetic variants and treatment response in colorectal cancer patients.

title: Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase p85alpha Met326Ile polymorphism and metabolic features in polycystic ovary syndrome
abstract: Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase p85alpha regulatory subunit gene Met326Ile polymorphism is associated with metabolic features in women with polycystic ovary syndrome. Insulin resistance is a defining characteristic of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase plays a critical role in insulin signaling and glucose transport. The Met326Ile polymorphism in the p85alpha regulatory subunit may influence enzyme function. Analysis of the Met326Ile polymorphism was conducted on DNA samples from 256 PCOS patients and 283 controls. Clinical and biochemical profiles were compared. The Met326Ile genotype distribution was similar between PCOS and control groups. PCOS patients were divided into subgroups based on the presence of the variant 326Ile allele. Carriers with the Met326Met genotype exhibited higher serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone levels compared to those with Ile326Ile or Met326Ile genotypes. Additionally, free testosterone levels were higher in Met326Met carriers. These findings suggest that the PI3-kinase gene Met326Ile polymorphism may modulate serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone and free testosterone levels in PCOS patients, but does not appear to be a major determinant of PCOS development.

title: High-Dose Tranexamic Acid and Postoperative Seizures in Cardiac Surgery
abstract: High-dose tranexamic Acid is associated with postoperative seizures in patients undergoing cardiac surgery. In a study involving two medical centers, there was a significant rise in the occurrence of convulsive seizures from 1.3% to 3.8% among patients who had major cardiac procedures. These seizures occurred around the time high-dose tranexamic acid was introduced after aprotinin was discontinued. The study aimed to determine if there was a connection between TXA use and seizures after cardiac surgery. Medical records were reviewed for all 24 patients who experienced perioperative seizures. Electroencephalograms were performed on 11 patients, and all underwent neurological exams and brain imaging. Results showed that 21 out of 24 patients did not have new cerebral ischemic injury, but 3 had seizures likely caused by ischemic brain injury. None of the patients had permanent neurological abnormalities. All patients received high doses of TXA, ranging from 61 to 259 mg/kg, had an average age of 69.9 years, and 21 had open chamber procedures. All but one used cardiopulmonary bypass. No evidence of brain ischemic, metabolic, or hyperthermia-induced causes for the seizures was found.

title: Mechanisms of Cocaine-Induced Neurotoxicity and Therapeutic Interventions
abstract: Cocaine administration in mice leads to memory and learning impairments, with involvement of nuclear factor kappa B and oxidative stress, and mitigation by topiramate. Previous studies suggest multiple pathways for cocaine toxicity, including oxidative stress, yet the relationship between oxidative status in the brain and cocaine-induced behavior remains unclear. Nuclear factor kappa B (NFkappaB) acts as a sensor of oxidative stress and contributes to memory formation, potentially playing a role in drug toxicity and addiction mechanisms. Therefore, NFkappaB activity, oxidative stress, neuronal nitric oxide synthase (nNOS) activity, spatial learning and memory, as well as the effects of topiramate, a potential therapy for cocaine addiction, were assessed in a mouse model of cocaine exposure. NFkappaB activity was reduced in the frontal cortex of cocaine-treated mice, along with GSH levels and glutathione peroxidase activity in the hippocampus, while nNOS activity in the hippocampus increased. Memory retrieval of pre-administration experiences was impaired and negatively correlated with NFkappaB activity in the frontal cortex. In contrast, learning of new tasks improved and correlated with increased nNOS activity and decreased glutathione peroxidase. These findings support a possible role of oxidative and nitrosative stress and NFkappaB in cocaine-induced neurobehavioral changes. Topiramate prevented all observed alterations, indicating novel neuroprotective effects.

title: Antioxidant Effects of Lactoferrin on Dexamethasone-Induced Hypertension in Rats
abstract: This study examines the antioxidant effects of bovine lactoferrin on dexamethasone-induced hypertension in rats. Dexamethasone (Dex)-induced hypertension is linked to increased oxidative stress, as evidenced by elevated plasma hydrogen peroxide levels and reduced thymus weight. Lactoferrin, an iron-binding glycoprotein with antihypertensive properties, was tested in two experimental designs: a prevention protocol where rats received lactoferrin prior to Dex treatment, and a reversal protocol with prolonged administration. Systolic blood pressure was monitored using tail-cuff technique, while ferric reducing antioxidant power (FRAP) was assessed to evaluate antioxidant capacity. Dex significantly raised blood pressure and hydrogen peroxide concentrations, and decreased body weight and thymus mass. Lactoferrin dose-dependently suppressed Dex-induced hypertension, prevented weight loss, and restored FRAP levels. These findings suggest that lactoferrin mitigates oxidative stress, highlighting its role in counteracting Dex-induced hypertension through antioxidant mechanisms. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: glucocorticoid; ROS.

title: FGFR2 and SOX2 in Airway Stem Cell Maintenance and Disease
abstract: FGFR2 plays a critical role in the self-renewal and differentiation of airway basal cells. These stem cells continuously produce differentiated progeny to maintain homeostasis throughout an individual's lifespan. Mutations in regulatory factors of these processes may lead to cancer or degenerative disease, but also represent potential therapeutic targets. Conditional deletion of one FGFR2 allele in adult airway basal cells results in disrupted self-renewal and differentiation. We demonstrate that FGFR2 signaling is associated with the expression of SOX2, a key transcription factor for basal cell maintenance. This heterozygous phenotype highlights how subtle changes in receptor tyrosine kinase activity can significantly impact cellular behavior. Additionally, degenerative disease is linked to altered FGFR2 function, while cancer is associated with changes in SOX2 expression levels.

title: Functional and Structural Analysis of Hippocalcin Mutants in Dystonia Pathogenesis
abstract: This study investigates the molecular mechanisms underlying dystonia caused by mutations in the neuronal calcium sensor hippocalcin. Dystonia, a neurological movement disorder characterized by involuntary muscle contractions, is linked to mutations T71N and A190 T in hippocalcin. These mutations, identified through advanced sequencing techniques, are associated with primary dystonia (DYT2). Our findings reveal that hippocalcin forms calcium-dependent oligomers and binds to voltage-gated calcium channels. Despite the mutations not altering stability or calcium-binding properties, both T71N and A190 T mutants exhibit impaired oligomerization. The crystal structure of hippocalcin shows structural variations in the C-terminal region, critical for target interaction. Notably, KCl-depolarized cells with mutated hippocalcin display enhanced calcium influx, primarily mediated by N-type voltage-gated calcium channels. The association between dystonia and hippocalcin mutations highlights the role of calcium signaling in disease progression. Calcium-dependent interactions and hippocalcin function are positively correlated, underscoring their importance in maintaining normal physiological processes. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: Ca2+/myristoyl; KCl-depolarised.

title: Ca2+ Regulation in Astrocytic Function and Neuroinflammatory Pathways
abstract: Ca2+ -dependent modulation of endoplasmic reticulum stress is closely linked to astrogliosis, involving increased expression of KCa3.1 and reduced AKT/mTOR signaling. The intermediate-conductance Ca2+ -activated K+ channel KCa3.1 plays a critical role in regulating the phenotype transition of reactive astrogliosis in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Immunoblotting and immunostaining analyses revealed KCa3.1 expression in the brains of AD patients and APP/PS1 mice models, with significant correlations between KCa3.1 and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and unfolded protein response (UPR). In vitro experiments using Fluo-4AM demonstrated that Ca2+ levels in beta-amyloid (Abeta)-stimulated astrocytes are influenced by KCa3.1. Gene deletion or pharmacological inhibition of KCa3.1 protected against Ca2+ overload and ER stress through the protein kinase B (AKT) signaling pathway. These findings were corroborated by increased expression of ER stress markers 78-kDa glucose-regulated protein and CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein homologous protein, as well as the RA marker glial fibrillary acidic protein in APP/PS1 AD mice. Elimination of KCa3.1 in KCa3.1-/-/APP/PS1 mice restored AKT/mTOR signaling and reduced glial activation, neuroinflammation, memory deficits, and neuron loss. The study highlights the involvement of KCa3.1 in maintaining Ca2+ homeostasis and mitigating ER stress, thus influencing neuroinflammatory processes and cognitive impairments. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: Ca2 +; Orai1; Alzheimer 's disease.

title: Development of Attenuated Dengue Virus Candidates for Vaccine Applications
abstract: A novel dengue virus type 2 (DEN-2) isolate with mild clinical features was selected for vaccine development. The DEN-2 virus was engineered to contain a 30 nucleotide deletion in the 3' untranslated region, resulting in the creation of a modified strain. This modified virus was used to generate a full-length cDNA clone, which was then employed to produce recombinant viruses, including rDEN2Delta30 and rDEN2Delta30 - 4995. The rDEN2Delta30 virus showed reduced replication in SCID-HuH-7 mice compared to the parental strain. Both rDEN2Delta30 and rDEN2Delta30 - 4995 were tested in SCID-HuH-7 mice, mosquitoes, and rhesus monkeys. In rhesus monkeys, the modified viruses exhibited attenuated characteristics, with changes in viremia duration and neutralizing antibody responses. The NS3 gene of the DEN-4 virus was modified in rDEN2Delta30 - 4995, contributing to its increased attenuation. The study highlights the potential of these modified viruses for further evaluation in human trials and as components of a tetravalent dengue vaccine. The relationship between dengue and NS3 was not directly established, while hepatoma was associated with the experimental models used in the study. Viremia was linked to the viral replication dynamics observed in the animal models.

title: Genetic Analysis of TSPYL1 in Sudden Infant Death Syndromes
abstract: A study was conducted to investigate the role of the TSPYL1 gene in sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS) and related conditions. The research focused on identifying genetic variations associated with SIDS and its phenotypic manifestations. Analysis of 126 SIDS cases and 261 control samples revealed five sequence variations, each involving an amino acid substitution. Notably, a heterozygous p. F366L polymorphism was detected in one female patient, absent in controls, suggesting a potential pathogenic role. However, no Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium was observed, and allele frequencies showed no significant differences between groups. The 457_458insG mutation, previously linked to sudden infant death with dysgenesis of the testes syndrome (SIDDT), was not detected in this cohort. While TSPYL1 mutations are associated with SIDDT, the heterozygous p. F366L variant alone cannot fully explain sudden deaths in this context. The study found no association between TSPYL1 sequence variations and SIDS in the German population, highlighting the need for further research to clarify the genetic basis of these conditions. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: sudden death.

title: Epidural Steroid Injection and Neurologic Deterioration: A Case Report
abstract: Cauda equina syndrome following epidural steroid injection is a rare but serious complication. This case report describes a 55-year-old woman who presented with low back and right leg pain and was scheduled for epidural steroid injection. The procedure involved the administration of triamcinolone diacetate and bupivacaine. Following the injection, she experienced a transient reduction in radicular symptoms but later developed perineal numbness and lower extremity weakness. Neurologic examination revealed saddle anesthesia, decreased pinprick sensation, and diminished deep-tendon reflexes, with an inability to void. Over the subsequent 8 hours, her symptoms gradually resolved, with full recovery of motor function and sensory abilities. The case highlights the importance of monitoring for neurologic deterioration after epidural steroid injections, particularly with the use of steroid and local anesthetic combinations. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: radiculopathy.

title: Genetic Variations in Surfactant Proteins and Meningococcal Disease Susceptibility
abstract: Genetic polymorphisms in the carbohydrate recognition domains of surfactant protein-A2 (SP-A2) and SP-D are linked to altered susceptibility to meningococcal disease. Neisseria meningitidis colonization of the nasopharynx leads to meningococcal disease, which is influenced by the functional properties of surfactant proteins. Surfactant protein (SP)-A and SP-D, which recognize microbial sugars, play critical roles in activating inflammatory responses and phagocytic defenses. Variations in SP-A2 and SP-D genes affect their expression and activity. In a study of 303 patients with meningococcal disease, including 18 who died, and 222 healthy controls, homozygosity for the 1A1 allele of SP-A2 increased disease risk (OR, 7.4; 95% CI, 1.3-42.4), while 1A5 reduced it (OR, 0.3; 95% CI, 0.1-0.97). The presence of lysine at residue 223 in SP-A2, encoded by alleles 1A1, was associated with higher disease risk (OR, 6.7; 95% CI, 1.4-31.5). Patients who died had 61% lysine at residue 223 compared to 35% of survivors (OR adjusted for age, 2.9; 95% CI, 1.1-7.7). Inflammatory responses were found to be associated with SP-A2 expression. Sugars bind to SP-D, and the amino acid substitution at residue 223 (lysine in 1A1 vs. glutamine in 1A5) correlated with increased mortality. Genetic variations in SP-A1 and SP-D did not significantly affect disease outcomes. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: lysine ( in 1A1 ) rather than glutamine ( in 1A5 ) at amino acid 223.

title: Genetic Mutations and Oligodontia: Role of MSX1 and PAX9
abstract: A novel mutation in the paired domain of human PAX9 is linked to oligodontia. Both PAX9 and MSX1 are transcription factors critical for craniofacial development. Mutations in these genes are associated with oligodontia in humans. A family with nonsyndromic oligodontia was screened for PAX9 and MSX1 mutations. SSCP analysis and sequencing identified a novel heterozygous C139 T transition in PAX9, but no mutations were found in MSX1. The C139 T mutation, predicted to cause R47W substitution, affects conserved residues in PAX9. Analysis of DNA binding showed reduced activity in the mutant protein, leading to oligodontia. No known relation exists between PAX9 and the C139 T variant, while MSX1 and PAX9 are independently associated with the condition.

title: FH Mutation Database: A Repository for Fumarase Deficiency and MCUL Tumor Syndrome Variants
abstract: The FH mutation database is a comprehensive resource for fumarate hydratase (FH) mutations associated with MCUL (HLRCC) tumor syndrome and congenital fumarase deficiency. FH, a key enzyme in the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, plays a critical role in cellular energy production. Deficiency of FH leads to early-onset, severe encephalopathy, while heterozygous FH mutations are linked to multiple cutaneous and uterine leiomyomas (MCUL: OMIM 150800). Renal cell cancer is also observed in some families, forming part of the hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer (HLRCC: OMIM 605839) syndrome. The database, based on the TCA cycle gene mutation database, includes variants derived from published literature and annotated according to current mutation nomenclature. Over 107 FH variants have been reported, with 93 classified as pathogenic. The most common mutations are missense (57%), followed by frameshifts and nonsense (27%), along with deletions, insertions, and duplications. This database aims to unify genetic knowledge of FH variants, aiding clinicians and researchers in understanding the molecular basis of FH-related diseases, including renal cell cancer, encephalopathy, and tumor syndrome. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: Leiomyoma.

title: A Novel Mutation in the Glucocorticoid Receptor Affects Hormonal Sensitivity and Metabolic Traits
abstract: A single nucleotide (G → C) substitution at position 1201 of the glucocorticoid receptor (GR) gene was identified in a 45-year-old male patient presenting with metabolic syndrome and hypertension. This mutation leads to an aspartic acid to histidine substitution at amino acid position 401 in the amino-terminal domain of the GRα protein. The mutant GRαD401H exhibits increased transactivation of the glucocorticoid-inducible mouse mammary tumor virus promoter in response to dexamethasone, with a 2.3-fold higher transcriptional activity compared to the wild-type receptor. The mutant receptor maintains normal ligand binding affinity (dissociation constant 6.3 ± 0.5 nm) and nuclear translocation kinetics (14.5 ± 0.3 min), but shows reduced interaction with the glucocorticoid receptor-interacting protein 1 coactivator. This mutation is associated with increased risk of obesity, hypertension, and metabolic syndrome, highlighting a potential genetic basis for individual variations in glucocorticoid responsiveness. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: cortisol; hypersensitivity; ( G -- > C ) substitution at position 1201.

title: Ras Activation Induces Distinct Downstream Targets in Lens and Cornea Development
abstract: Ras activation induces distinct downstream targets in lens and cornea development. Mammalian Ras genes regulate diverse cellular processes, including proliferation and differentiation, and are frequently mutated in human cancers. Tumor development in response to Ras activation varies between tissues, and the molecular basis for these differences remains unclear. The murine lens and cornea share a common embryonic origin and arise from adjacent regions of the surface ectoderm. Activation of the fibroblast growth factor (FGF) signaling pathway induces corneal epithelial cell proliferation and lens epithelial cell cycle exit. The molecular mechanisms governing these differential responses are not fully understood. Transgenic mice expressing a constitutively active human H-Ras in their lenses and corneas were generated. Results showed increased proliferation in Ras transgenic lenses and corneal epithelial cells, accompanied by elevated cyclin D1 and D2 expression. This proliferation was sustained in the cornea but not the lens. Coincidentally, cdk inhibitors p27Kip1 and p57Kip2 were upregulated in the lens but not the cornea. Phospho-Erk1 and Erk2 levels were elevated in the lens, while Spry 1 and Spry 2, negative regulators of Ras-Raf-Erk signaling, were more upregulated in the cornea. Both lens and cornea differentiation programs were sensitive to Ras activation. Ras transgenic embryos exhibited altered lens pit architecture. Ras activation, though sufficient for upregulating Prox1, a transcription factor critical for cell cycle exit and fiber differentiation, is not sufficient for terminal fiber differentiation. Expression of Keratin 12, a corneal epithelial differentiation marker, was reduced in Ras transgenic corneas. These findings suggest that Ras activation induces distinct downstream targets in the lens and cornea, leading to different cellular responses, and is sufficient for initiating but not completing lens fiber differentiation.

title: Role of Sag/Rbx2/Roc2 in Senescence and Lung Tumorigenesis
abstract: Disruption of Sag/Rbx2/Roc2 E3 ubiquitin ligase activity induces cellular senescence and suppresses kras-induced immortalization. Recent studies demonstrate that Sag/Rbx2 E3 ligase modulates apoptosis and vasculogenesis by promoting the degradation of NOXA and NF1, and collaborates with Kras to drive lung tumorigenesis through activation of NFkappaB and mTOR pathways via degradation of tumor suppressive substrates including IkappaB, DEPTOR, p21, and p27. Here, we investigate the role of Sag/Rbx2 E3 ligase in senescence and immortalization of mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) and report that Sag is essential for proper cell proliferation and Kras(G12D)-induced immortalization. Sag inactivation by genetic deletion significantly reduces cell proliferation by inducing senescence, which correlates with p16 accumulation but not p53. Mechanistically, Sag deletion leads to the accumulation of Jun-B, a substrate of Sag-Fbxw7 E3 ligase and a transcription factor that drives p16 transcription. Importantly, senescence triggered by Sag deletion can be largely reversed by simultaneous deletion of Cdkn2a, the p16 encoding gene, indicating its causal role. Furthermore, Kras(G12D)-induced immortalization is also inhibited by Sag deletion through senescence induction, which is rescued by Cdkn2a deletion. Finally, we find that Sag deletion inactivates Kras(G12D) activity and blocks the MAPK signaling pathway, along with p16 accumulation, to induce senescence. These findings demonstrate that Sag is a Kras(G12D)-cooperating oncogene required for Kras(G12D)-induced immortalization and transformation, and targeting SAG-SCF E3 ligase may offer therapeutic potential for senescence-based cancer treatment.

title: Mechanisms Linking Early-Life Arsenic Exposure to Cancer Development
abstract: Exposure to inorganic arsenic during critical developmental stages is increasingly recognized as a risk factor for cancer onset later in life. Studies highlight the role of inorganic arsenic in promoting malignant transformations through oxidative stress and DNA damage. Arsenic, in its elemental form, is distinct from inorganic arsenic but shares chemical properties that may influence biological pathways. While no direct association has been established between Arsenic and cancer, inorganic arsenic's carcinogenic potential is well-documented. Research emphasizes the need for longitudinal studies to clarify the molecular interplay between early-life exposure and cancer progression.

title: Doxorubicin-Based Chemotherapy and Cardiac Complications in Patients with Muscular Dystrophy and Gastric Lymphoma
abstract: A patient with myotonic dystrophy and gastric lymphoma developed Atrial fibrillation following doxorubicin-based chemotherapy. The unusual association between diffuse B-cell gastric lymphoma and myotonic dystrophy, a common form of adult muscular dystrophy, was observed. Cardiac toxicity associated with doxorubicin-based chemotherapy was linked to the development of cardiac arrhythmias. However, the presence of gastric lymphoma was not directly correlated with the chemotherapy's toxicity. The aggressive treatment regimen, which included doxorubicin-based therapy, was associated with increased cardiac toxicity and arrhythmias, particularly in patients with preexisting cardiac conditions. Atrial fibrillation and cardiac arrhythmias were rare complications in this context, but the cardiac toxicity intrinsically linked to the chemotherapy may have triggered the arrhythmia in the predisposed myocardium of this patient.

title: Ca2+ Dependence of TRPV6 Channel Activity
abstract: The Ca2+ -dependent function of TRPV6 channels was investigated using microfluorimetry and patch-clamp techniques on HEK cells expressing TRPV6. Cells loaded with fura-2 showed elevated intracellular Ca2+ levels, which normalized to non-transfected levels when external Ca2+ was removed by EGTA. Whole-cell recordings from both non-transfected and TRPV6-expressing cells revealed a baseline inward current under conditions of 0.1 mm EGTA and 100 nm Ca2+ , or when cytosolic Ca2+ buffering was unchanged in perforated patch-clamp experiments. If TRPV6 forms open channels, Ca2+ -induced current inhibition would be expected due to its negative regulation by internal Ca2+ . However, dialyzing solutions with high Ca2+ concentrations did not block the baseline inward current, which remained similar to non-transfected cells. In contrast, dialyzing 0.5 mm EGTA activated Ca2+ -inward currents in TRPV6-expressing cells, absent in non-transfected cells. Notably, monovalent cations permeated TRPV6 channels under conditions where no Ca2+ permeation was detected, suggesting divalent cations block TRPV6 from the extracellular side. Like human TRPV6, the truncated TRPV6(Delta695 - 725 ) lacking the C-terminal domain for Ca2+ -calmodulin binding does not form constitutive channels, whereas TRPV6(D542A ) with a pore-region mutation fails to function as a channel. Overall, no constitutive open TRPV6 channels were detected in patch-clamp experiments from transfected HEK cells, but channel activity is strongly regulated by intracellular and extracellular divalent cations. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: Ca2 +.

title: Characterization of Mutations in the Type VII Collagen Gene Associated with Recessive Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
abstract: This study identifies two novel mutations in the type VII collagen gene linked to recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa. Analysis of a multi-ethnic family revealed a maternal mutation involving a single base pair deletion of a cytosine nucleotide in exon 26 (3472delC), which causes a frameshift and premature termination codon within the same exon. A paternal mutation, characterized as G-->A, occurs at the 5' donor splice site within intron 51 (IVS51 + 1G-->A), leading to cryptic splice site activation and aberrant out-of-frame splicing. These mutations generate two alternative mRNA transcripts and result in downstream premature termination codons. The identified variants are distinct from previously reported mutations and contribute to the genetic complexity of this condition. The findings highlight the role of compound heterozygous mutations in disease pathogenesis and support clinical applications for genetic counseling. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: IVS51 + 1G-->A..

title: CYP1A1 Polymorphisms and Prostate Cancer Risk in a South Indian Population
abstract: Cytochrome p4501A1 gene variants were investigated as potential susceptibility markers for prostate cancer. The study evaluated the association between two single nucleotide polymorphisms (A to G transition in exon7 leading to Ile462Val substitution and T3801C at 3'UTR) of the CYP1A1 gene and prostate cancer risk in a case-control sample of 100 individuals from a South Indian population. Results showed a significantly elevated relative risk for individuals carrying the w1/m1 genotype at the 3'UTR (OR-4.64; 95%CI = 1.51 - 14.86; P < 0.01), while the CYP1A1 Ile/Val genotype (w2/m2) on exon7 was linked to a reduced risk for prostate cancer (OR-0.17; 95%CI = 0.02 - 0.89; P=0.03). Stratified analysis by age of onset revealed the w1/m1 genotype was significantly associated with early onset, though tumor grade did not show significant correlations with the variant genotypes. These findings suggest that the w1/m1 genotype increases risk, while the w2/m2 genotype decreases risk for prostate cancer.

title: Genetic Polymorphisms and Irinotecan-Induced Toxicities in Cancer Patients
abstract: A single nucleotide polymorphism in ABCG2 is linked to irinotecan-induced severe myelosuppression. Irinotecan is an anti-neoplastic drug commonly used in the treatment of colorectal and lung cancers, but it often causes toxicities such as severe myelosuppression and diarrhea. In this study, a two-stage case-control analysis was conducted to investigate irinotecan-induced severe myelosuppression (grades 3 and 4). In the first stage, 23 patients who developed severe myelosuppression and 58 patients without any toxicity were evaluated for 170 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in 14 genes related to the metabolism and transport of irinotecan. Five SNPs were found to potentially associate with severe myelosuppression (P(Fisher)<0.01) and were further analyzed in 7 cases and 20 controls in the second stage. An intronic SNP, rs2622604, in ABCG2 showed P(Fisher)=0.0419 in the second stage and indicated a significant association with severe myelosuppression in the combined study (P(Fisher)=0.000237; P(Corrected)=0.036). Although limited subjects were studied, the results suggest that a genetic polymorphism in ABCG2 may alter the transport activity for the drug and increase the systemic circulation level of irinotecan, leading to severe myelosuppression. Additionally, rs2622604 was found to be associated with the occurrence of diarrhea, a common toxicity linked to irinotecan treatment.

title: Identification of a Genetic Mutation in Osterix Linked to Recessive Osteogenesis Imperfecta
abstract: Recessive osteogenesis imperfecta is a type I collagen-related condition associated with osteoporosis and increased risk of bone fractures. A homozygous single base pair deletion in Osterix was identified in a patient with this disorder. The clinical presentation includes recurrent bone fractures, mild bone deformities, delayed tooth eruption, and normal hearing. Osterix, a transcription factor critical for bone development, is implicated in the pathogenesis of this condition. The deletion disrupts the protein's structure, leading to impaired bone formation. This finding highlights the role of Osterix in human bone development and expands the genetic spectrum of osteogenesis imperfecta.

title: Genetic Polymorphisms and Their Association with Inflammatory and Neoplastic Conditions
abstract: Variation in the CXCR1 gene (IL8RA) was not linked to susceptibility to chronic periodontitis. The chemokine receptor CXCR1, which binds to interleukin 8 (IL-8), plays a role in inflammatory responses by attracting neutrophils. A polymorphism rs2234671 at position Ex2 + 860G > C in CXCR1 leads to a substitution (S276T) and was previously associated with reduced lung cancer risk. Our study examined this polymorphism in 395 South African individuals with and without chronic periodontitis. No significant differences in allelic or genotypic distributions were observed between groups (p>0.05). Additionally, inflammatory conditions showed no association with rs2234671. The CXCR2 gene, however, was found to be associated with chronic periodontitis in prior studies. The CXCR1-CXCR2 gene pair exhibited no correlation, while interleukin 8 remained bound to CXCR1, highlighting its role in inflammatory processes.

title: Polymorphisms in TBX21 and HLX1 Affect Cytokine Secretion in Neonates
abstract: TBX21 and HLX1 polymorphisms influence cytokine secretion at birth. TBX21 (T cell specific T-box transcription factor) and HLX1 (H.20-like homeobox 1) are crucial transcription factors of T(H)1-cells, inducing their differentiation and suppressing T(H)2 commitment, particularly important for early life immune development. This study investigated the influence of TBX21 and HLX1 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), which have previously been shown to be associated with asthma, on T(H)1/T(H)2 lineage cytokines at birth. Cord blood mononuclear cells (CBMCs) of 200 neonates were genotyped for two TBX21 and three HLX1 SNPs. CBMCs were stimulated with innate (Lipid A, LpA; Peptidoglycan, Ppg), adaptive stimuli (house dust mite Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus 1, Derp1) or mitogen (phytohemagglutinin, PHA). Cytokines, T-cells and mRNA expression of T(H)1/T(H)2-related genes were assessed. Atopic diseases during the first 3 years of life were assessed by questionnaire answered by the parents. Carriers of TBX21 promoter SNP rs17250932 and HLX1 promoter SNP rs2738751 showed reduced or trendwise reduced (p<0.07) IL-5, IL-13 and TNF-a secretion after LpA-stimulation. Carriers of HLX1 SNP rs2738751 had lower IL-13 levels following Ppg-stimulation (p = 0.08). Carriers of HLX1 exon 1 SNP rs12141189 showed increased IL-5 (LpA, p = 0.007; Ppg, p = 0.10), trendwise increased IL-13 (LpA), higher GM-CSF (LpA/Ppg, p<0.05) and trendwise decreased IFN-g secretion (Derp1+LpA-stimulation, p = 0.1). Homozygous carriers of HLX1 promoter SNP rs3806325 showed increased IL-13 and IL-6 (unstimulated, p<0.03). In carriers of TBX21 intron 3 SNP rs11079788 no differences in cytokine secretion were observed. mRNA expression of T(H)1/T(H)2-related genes partly correlated with cytokines at protein level. TBX21 SNP rs11079788 carriers developed less symptoms of atopic dermatitis at 3 years of age (p = 0.03). Polymorphisms in TBX21 and HLX1 influenced primarily IL-5 and IL-13 secretion after LpA-stimulation in cord blood suggesting that genetic variations in the transcription factors essential for the T(H)1-pathway may contribute to modified T(H)2-immune responses already early in life. Further follow-up of the cohort is required to study the polymorphisms' relevance for immune-mediated diseases such as childhood asthma.

title: Mitochondrial Antioxidant Modulation in Maternal Diabetes-Induced Embryopathy
abstract: Superoxide dismutase 1 overexpression in mice mitigates maternal diabetes-induced endoplasmic reticulum stress in embryopathy. This study explores the interplay between oxidative stress and ER stress in diabetic embryopathy. We evaluated the effects of SOD1 overexpression on ER stress markers, including C/EBP-homologous protein, calnexin, eukaryotic initiation factor 2a, protein kinase ribonucleic acid (RNA)-like ER kinase, binding immunoglobulin protein, protein disulfide isomerase family A member 3, kinases inositol-requiring protein-1a, and X-box binding protein messenger RNA splicing in embryos from diabetic and non-diabetic mothers. Maternal diabetes significantly elevated CHOP, calnexin, phosphorylated eIF2a, p-PERK, and p-IRE1a levels, triggered XBP1 mRNA splicing, and enhanced ER chaperone gene expression in WT embryos. SOD1 overexpression blocked these diabetes-induced ER stress markers. These findings indicate that oxidative stress reduction through SOD1 overexpression prevents maternal diabetes-induced ER stress in vivo, highlighting the therapeutic potential of antioxidant strategies in embryopathy.

title: Modulation of the Autotaxin-LPA2 GPCR Axis by Radiation Injury and Its Role in DNA Repair
abstract: The autotaxin-LPA2 GPCR axis is influenced by radiation injury and plays a role in DNA damage repair. This study investigated the effects of radiation injury on the expression and function of the autotaxin (ATX)-LPA2 GPCR axis. In IEC-6 crypt cells and jejunum enteroids, quantitative RT-PCR revealed a time- and dose-dependent upregulation of lpa2 in response to gamma-irradiation, which was prevented by mutation of the NF-kappaB site in the lpa2 promoter or by inhibition of ATM/ATR kinases with CGK-733, indicating that lpa2 is a DNA damage response gene upregulated by ATM through NF-kappaB. The resolution kinetics of the DNA damage marker gamma-H2AX in LPA-treated IEC-6 cells exposed to gamma-irradiation were accelerated compared to vehicle, whereas pharmacological inhibition of LPA2 delayed the resolution of gamma-H2AX. In LPA2-reconstituted MEF cells lacking LPA1 ' 3, the levels of gamma-H2AX decreased rapidly, whereas in Vector MEF cells they remained high and sustained. Inhibition of ERK1 ' 2 or PI3K/AKT signaling axis by pertussis toxin or the C311A/C314A/L351A mutation in the C-terminus of LPA2 abrogated the effect of LPA on DNA repair. LPA2 transcripts in Lin(-)Sca-1(+)c-Kit(+ ) enriched for bone marrow stem cells were 27- and 5-fold higher than in common myeloid or lymphoid progenitors, respectively. Furthermore, after irradiation, higher residual gamma-H2AX levels were detected in the bone marrow or jejunum of irradiated LPA2-KO mice compared to WT mice. We found that gamma-irradiation increases plasma ATX activity and LPA level, which is partially due to the previously established radiation-induced upregulation of TNFalpha. These findings identify ATX and LPA2 as radiation-regulated genes that appear to play a physiological role in DNA repair.

title: Role of NEK2 in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression
abstract: NEK2 functions as a potential prognostic marker for hepatocellular carcinoma. NEK2, a member of the NIMA-related kinase family, is a microtubule-associated protein involved in spindle assembly and is frequently overexpressed in various malignancies. However, its specific role in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains unclear. RNA-seq analysis of the HCC cell line SMMC-7721 and normal liver cell line HL-7702 revealed NEK2 expression in both cell types and matched HCC and adjacent non-tumorous liver tissues. Correlation between survival outcomes and NEK2 levels was assessed in 359 HCC patients using TCGA data. Immunohistochemical evaluation of NEK2, phospho-AKT, and MMP-2 in 63 HCC cases and matched tissues showed that NEK2 overexpression was associated with poor prognosis. A total of 610 differentially expressed genes were identified, with NEK2 as the most significantly upregulated gene in HCC. NEK2 was overexpressed in HCC cells and tissues, correlating with increased tumor nodule count and recurrence. NEK2 expression was positively correlated with phospho-AKT levels (r=0.883, P<0.01) and MMP-2 levels (r=0.781, P<0.01). These findings suggest that NEK2 may contribute to HCC metastasis through AKT signaling activation and MMP-2 upregulation. Malignancies were observed in patients with elevated microtubule-associated protein levels, but no direct association was found between malignancies and NEK2. Metastasis of HCC was linked to NEK2 overexpression, while hepatocellular carcinoma showed no direct correlation with microtubule-associated protein. Phospho-AKT was not directly related to malignancies, and microtubule-associated protein exhibited no association with hepatocellular carcinoma.

title: Prevalence and Genetic Associations in Patients with Primary Microcephaly
abstract: A study of Czech children with primary microcephaly revealed that 13% exhibited features of Nijmegen breakage syndrome. Nijmegen breakage syndrome is an autosomal recessive chromosomal instability disorder characterized by early growth retardation, congenital microcephaly, immunodeficiency, and a heightened risk of lymphoreticular malignancies. The 5 nucleotide deletion in the NBS1 gene is a genetic marker associated with Nijmegen breakage syndrome. NBS1, a gene product, is implicated in the pathogenesis of this disorder. These patients also display autosomal recessive chromosomal instability disorder traits, with immunodeficiency being a consistent clinical feature. The 5 nucleotide deletion is a founder mutation in the NBS1 gene, leading to homozygous inheritance. Analysis of 67 Czech patients identified three new cases of Nijmegen breakage syndrome, representing 4.5% of the cohort. All newly diagnosed cases were under 10 months of age, with a 2.5-year birth window. This aligns with a predicted incidence of 13% among primary microcephalic infants, highlighting the importance of genetic testing for early diagnosis and intervention.

title: Genetic Variants and Their Association with Metabolic Conditions
abstract: The Lys198Asn and -134delA polymorphisms in the endothelin-1 gene have been investigated for their potential links to metabolic disorders. Endothelin-1, a key regulator of blood pressure, exhibits variations in its expression across different populations. Two genetic variants in the EDN1 gene were examined: the Lys198Asn substitution, which showed a positive association with blood pressure in overweight individuals, and the -134delA variant located in the 5'-untranslated region. This study explored the expression of these variants in vitro using three cell lines, measuring ET-1 and big ET-1 levels in culture supernatants. No significant differences were observed in ET-1 production between the Lys-type and Asn-type transfectants. However, plasma ET-1 levels in hypertensive patients with the Lys→Asn substitution were comparable to those without the change. A significant genotype difference was noted between 3A/3A and 3A/4A carriers. While the Lys198Asn polymorphism may not directly influence ET-1 levels, the -134delA variant could contribute to blood pressure regulation through interactions with other factors like obesity. Overweight individuals showed a notable association between endothelin-1 and metabolic status, highlighting potential mechanisms linking these genetic variants to physiological outcomes.

title: Genetic Variants and Circadian Rhythm in Advanced Sleep Phase Syndrome
abstract: Variants in the hPER2 gene have been investigated for their role in circadian regulation. Single-nucleotide polymorphisms including C-1228 T, C111 G, and G3853A were analyzed in relation to diurnal preference. The C111 G variant, which causes a glycine to glutamine substitution, was associated with morning-type phenotypes. Subjects with extreme morning preference showed higher frequencies of the 111 G allele compared to those with evening preference. The hPER2 gene is implicated in the molecular mechanisms underlying circadian rhythms. Advanced sleep phase syndrome is positively correlated with the 111 G allele. Additionally, the hPER2 gene is linked to the development of advanced sleep phase syndrome. No significant differences were observed for the C-1228 T and G3853A variants across diurnal preference groups. The 111 G allele may contribute to the genetic basis of ASPS through its effect on circadian gene expression.

title: Genetic Analysis of PTPN22 Variants in Type 1 Diabetes Risk
abstract: A study of the PTPN22 gene and its polymorphisms in relation to type 1 diabetes revealed key associations. The 1858C/T variant was identified as a significant risk factor, with the T allele linked to increased susceptibility. Analysis of haplotypes in the PTPN22 region showed that the 1858 T allele was strongly correlated with type 1 diabetes. Additionally, a novel 2250G/C variant was discovered, which may contribute to disease risk. The 2250G/C variant was found to be associated with type 1 diabetes, though its effect was weaker than that of the 1858C/T variant. These findings highlight the role of PTPN22 in type 1 diabetes, with both the 1858C/T and 2250G/C variants showing positive correlations with the disease. The PTPN22 gene itself was associated with type 1 diabetes, underscoring its importance in the pathogenesis of the condition. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: 1858C/T..

title: Alu Insertion Polymorphisms and Genetic Diversity in Basque Populations
abstract: Alu sequence variations were analyzed in three Alu families (ACE, FXIIIB, APO, A25) from Navarre and Guipuzcoa provinces to investigate genetic structure. Comparative data from European, Caucasus, and North African populations were compiled to assess Basque genetic relationships. Multivariate analysis and AMOVA revealed geographic clustering among the three population groups, but no significant heterogeneity was detected between Basque samples or between Basques and other Europeans (excluding Caucasus). Alu marker results contradicted hypotheses of Basque origin linked to North African or Caucasian populations. To explain reduced genetic diversity in Basque subpopulations, Wright's F(ST) values were calculated for both Alu markers and STRs across two scales: Basque Country and Europe. In the Basque region, Wahlund's effect showed no statistical differences between subpopulations. However, European-scale analysis revealed higher F(ST) values for Alu insertions compared to STR alleles. These findings suggest recent genetic admixture with non-Basque neighbors, possibly influenced by linguistic barriers to random mating.

title: P2RX7 and rs2230912 in Bipolar and Unipolar Disorders
abstract: P2RX7 has been proposed as a candidate susceptibility gene for bipolar and unipolar disorders. The chromosomal region 12q24 has been previously linked to both bipolar disorder and unipolar mood disorder, and we report two pedigrees showing linkage across this region. The gene P2RX7 is located in this area and has been recently associated with susceptibility for bipolar disorder and unipolar depression. The non-synonymous SNP rs2230912 (resulting in Q460R amino-acid polymorphism) showed the strongest association and was postulated to be pathogenically relevant. We investigated this gene in a large UK case-control sample (bipolar I disorder N = 687, unipolar recurrent major depression N = 1,036, controls N = 1,204). Neither rs2230912 nor any of 8 other SNPs across P2RX7 were associated with mood disorder in general, nor specifically with bipolar or unipolar disorder. Furthermore, sequencing of two chromosome 12-linked bipolar-Darier families revealed no rare variants at P2RX7 that could explain the linkage. Our data do not support rs2230912 or other polymorphisms within the P2RX7 locus as being involved in susceptibility to mood disorders. Additionally, Darier's disease was not linked to P2RX7 in these studies, and unipolar mood disorder showed no significant association with the gene or SNP. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: bipolar and unipolar disorder; Darier 's disease.

title: Efficacy of everolimus in advanced NSCLC patients with prior chemotherapy and EGFR inhibitors
abstract: A study evaluated the safety and effectiveness of everolimus in patients with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who had received chemotherapy alone or in combination with EGFR inhibitors. Treatment options are limited for pretreated NSCLC patients, and everolimus, an mTOR inhibitor, showed promise in earlier phases. Patients with Stage IIIb or IV NSCLC, having undergone two or fewer chemotherapy regimens (one platinum-based or both chemotherapy and EGFR inhibitors), received everolimus at 10 mg/day until disease progression or severe toxicity. The primary endpoint was overall response rate (ORR), while biomarker analyses focused on mTOR pathway markers. Eighty-five patients were enrolled, with 42 in the platinum-based group and 43 in the combination group. ORR was 4.7% (7.1% in the platinum group; 2.3% in the combination group). Disease control rate reached 47.1%, with median progression-free survival (PFS) of 2.6 months in the platinum group and 2.7 months in the combination group. Common Grade 3 adverse events included fatigue, dyspnea, stomatitis, anemia, and thrombocytopenia. Pneumonitis, mostly Grade 1/2, occurred in 25% of patients. IHC analysis identified phospho-AKT as a significant predictor of worse PFS. Everolimus was well-tolerated, with modest clinical activity in pretreated NSCLC. Combination therapy with standard treatment for metastatic NSCLC is under investigation. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: tumor; mammalian target of rapamycin.

title: Pharmacogenetic Variants of CYP2C19 and Clopidogrel Efficacy in Coronary Artery Disease Patients
abstract: Clopidogrel is a critical antiplatelet agent for managing coronary artery disease following percutaneous coronary intervention. Genetic variations in CYP2C19 influence the drug's metabolic activation, affecting its therapeutic outcomes. Studies show that CYP2C19 variant carriers have reduced metabolism of clopidogrel, leading to inadequate platelet inhibition and increased cardiovascular risks. Despite this, coronary artery disease itself does not directly correlate with CYP2C19 activity. The US FDA has updated guidelines to emphasize the importance of CYP2C19 genotyping in clopidogrel therapy, highlighting the association between genetic factors and drug response. These findings underscore the need for personalized treatment approaches in patients with CYP2C19 variants.

title: Genetic Screening in a Family with Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1
abstract: Genetic screening in a family with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 revealed mutations in the MEN1 gene. A heterozygous cytosine insertion (c.1546_1547insC) was identified in exon 10, leading to a frame shift mutation. This mutation cosegregates with an intronic variant (IVS3 + 18C > T). The syndrome is associated with pituitary adenoma and parathyroid hyperplasia. Autosomal dominant cancer syndrome and cytosine insertion were not found to be related. Tumor development is negatively correlated with the presence of this mutation. Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 is positively correlated with the c.1546_1547insC mutation. Pituitary adenoma is associated with MEN1. Parathyroid hyperplasia and cytosine insertion are not directly linked. The novel IVS3 + 18C > T variant in intron 3 requires further investigation. MEN1 and IVS3 + 18C > T are not directly related. Tumor and MEN1 show a negative correlation. Cytosine insertion and IVS3 + 18C > T are unrelated. Pituitary adenoma and c.1546_1547insC are positively correlated. Autosomal dominant cancer syndrome and IVS3 + 18C > T are not related. Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 and MEN1 are associated. Parathyroid hyperplasia and IVS3 + 18C > T are not related.

title: Genetic Polymorphism of Glutathione-S-Transferase P1 and Its Association with Prostate Cancer and Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia in a Different Population
abstract: The glutathione-S-transferase P1 (GSTP1) gene exhibits a common functional polymorphism, A > G at nucleotide 313, which does not directly correlate with GSTP1 expression levels. To explore the association between this polymorphism and prostate cancer risk, we conducted a case-control study comparing 60 prostate cancer cases, 50 benign prostate hyperplasia cases, and 70 healthy controls. Genotyping for the GSTP1 Ile105Val variant revealed significant differences in allele frequencies between cancer cases and controls, with 42.3% of cancer cases carrying the Val allele. The A > G polymorphism was not found to influence GSTP1 activity in this population. However, a positive correlation was observed between the A > G variant and prostate cancer incidence, suggesting a potential role in disease susceptibility. Additionally, the GSTP1 Ile105Val genotype was associated with benign prostate hyperplasia, highlighting a possible link between this gene and both conditions.

title: Assessment of Multichannel Blocker Effects on QT Interval Using hiPS-CMs
abstract: Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPS-CMs) were utilized to evaluate the effects of various drugs on QT interval. Field potential duration (FPD) measured via MEA (Multielectrode array) demonstrated sensitivity to K(+ ) channel and Ca(2 + ) channel blockers. Amiodarone, Paroxetine, Terfenadine, and Citalopram, which are classified as multichannel blockers, exhibited concentration-dependent prolongation of corrected FPD (FPDc). Notably, Terfenadine and Citalopram, known to induce Torsade de Pointes (TdP), showed strong correlations with QT prolongation. Additionally, Citalopram was found to have a positive correlation with TdP, while Terfenadine also demonstrated a positive association with TdP. QT prolongation, a critical cardiac phenotype, was consistently observed in response to these drugs, highlighting the utility of hiPS-CMs in predicting drug-induced electrophysiological effects. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: K(+ ) channel and Ca(2 + ) channel blocker.

title: Serum chemokine profiles in cirrhotic patients correlate with hepatocellular carcinoma presence
abstract: Serum levels of chemokines CCL4 and CCL5 in cirrhotic patients indicate the presence of hepatocellular carcinoma. Background: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is often diagnosed at an advanced stage, and traditional markers like alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin (DCP) have limited diagnostic value. This study evaluates the diagnostic potential of serum biomarkers in cirrhotic patients with and without HCC. Methods: Serum samples were collected from cirrhotic patients (n=139) with HCC (n=61) and without HCC (n=78), as well as from healthy controls (n=39). Biomarkers included CRP, neopterin, and IL-6 as inflammatory indicators, thrombopoietin (TPO), GCSF, FGF basic, and VEGF as growth factors, HMGB1, CK-18, and a panel of proinflammatory chemokines (CCL2, CCL3, CCL4, CCL5, CXCL5, and IL-8). Statistical analyses included ROC curves, logistic regression, and comparative tests. Results: Patients with HCC exhibited higher serum levels of TPO, CCL4, CCL5, and CXCL5 compared to non-HCC cirrhotic patients (P < 0.001). Multivariate analysis confirmed CCL4 and CCL5 as significant diagnostic markers for HCC. Additionally, cirrhotic patients showed lower levels of CCL2 (P=0.008) and higher M30 compared to healthy controls. Conclusions: Elevated serum levels of inflammatory chemokines, particularly CCL4 and CCL5, in cirrhotic patients are associated with the presence of HCC. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: tumour.

title: Role of BICD2 in Dynein-Dynactin Function and Spinal Muscular Atrophy
abstract: Mutations in the BICD2 gene are linked to hyperactivation of dynein-dynactin motility in spinal muscular atrophy. Bicaudal D2 (BICD2) facilitates the formation of a ternary complex with dynein and dynactin, termed DDB, essential for processive microtubule movement. Genetic studies reveal that dominant BICD2 variants in patients with spinal muscular atrophy disrupt normal motor function. In vitro experiments using purified DDB and Rab6a, a GTPase involved in membrane trafficking, demonstrate that Rab6a-GTP stabilizes BICD2 in an active state, enhancing dynein-dynactin transport. BICD2 mutants show increased motility in DDB complexes, leading to elevated retrograde transport in cellular models. Overexpression of hyperactive BICD2 variants in rat hippocampal neurons reduces neurite elongation, suggesting a link between altered dynein-dynactin activity and neuronal dysfunction in spinal muscular atrophy. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: GTPase Rab6a.

title: Thiamine Deficiency and Hypoxia/Ischemia-Induced Pro-Apoptotic Responses in Astrocytes
abstract: Thiamine deficiency (TD) activates hypoxia inducible factor-1a (HIF-1a) to promote pro-apoptotic effects in primary astrocytes. Thiamine is a critical cofactor for metabolic processes in the brain, and its deficiency is commonly associated with chronic alcohol use, leading to impaired mitochondrial function, oxidative stress, inflammation, and excitotoxicity. These pathological changes result in apoptotic cell death in both neurons and astrocytes. Histological evidence of similar injuries in patients with hypoxia/ischemia and TD has been observed in the thalamus and mammillary bodies, indicating a potential link between these conditions. TD stabilizes and activates HIF-1a under normal oxygen levels, though the exact role of TD-induced HIF-1a in neurological injury remains unclear. Western blot and RT-PCR analyses revealed that TD increases HIF-1a expression and activity in mouse astrocytes. Over time, TD upregulates pro-apoptotic and inflammatory HIF-1a target genes such as MCP1, BNIP3, Nix, and Noxa. Apoptotic cell death was confirmed using PI/Annexin V staining, TUNEL assay, and Cell Death ELISA. Pharmacological inhibition of HIF-1a with YC1 and thiamine repletion reduced the expression of these pro-apoptotic genes and cell death in TD. These findings suggest that HIF-1a-mediated transcriptional activation of pro-apoptotic/inflammatory pathways contributes to astrocyte death during thiamine deficiency.

title: Azithromycin-Induced Acute Interstitial Nephritis and Renal Injury
abstract: A 15-year-old boy presents with recurrent acute interstitial nephritis secondary to azithromycin use. The second episode was more severe, requiring corticosteroid therapy, but renal function remained compromised. While most cases of antibiotic-induced interstitial nephritis resolve spontaneously, some patients develop persistent renal injury. Azithromycin is a broad-spectrum antibiotic, and corticosteroid use is associated with no direct correlation in this context.

title: Central Administration of Urotensin-II Modulates Behavioral and Endocrine Responses in Mice
abstract: The behavioral and endocrine effects of urotensin-II (U-II) were investigated in mice following central administration. Intracerebroventricular injection of U-II induced hypertension, bradycardia, and increased prolactin and thyrotropin secretion. The study evaluated the impact of graded doses of U-II (1-10,000 ng/mouse) on various behavioral tests, revealing a dose-dependent reduction in head dips in the hole-board test, decreased entries in the white chamber of the black-and-white compartment test, and reduced entries in the central platform and open arms of the plus-maze test. Additionally, U-II administration was associated with increased immobility duration in the forced-swimming and tail suspension tests. Central injections of U-II also enhanced food intake at 100 and 1,000 ng/mouse, increased water intake at 100-10,000 ng/mouse, and elevated horizontal locomotion activity at 10,000 ng/mouse. Notably, U-II had no effect on body temperature, nociception, apomorphine-induced penile erection and climbing behavior, or stress-induced plasma corticosterone levels. These findings suggest that U-II may contribute to anxiogenic- and depressant-like effects, potentially linking to psychiatric disorders.

title: Genetic and Functional Analysis of Nitric Oxide Synthase in Glaucoma and Neurological Disorders
abstract: The study investigates the genetic and functional connections between nitric oxide synthase (NOS) and glaucoma, focusing on the role of the CCTTT microsatellite in the pathogenesis of the disease. Nitric oxide, a critical signaling molecule, has been implicated in both beneficial and pathological roles, particularly in neurological and non-neurological disorders. Here, we examine the association between the inducible form of NOS and primary open angle glaucoma (POAG), a leading cause of blindness. Genotyping of 200 POAG patients and 200 age-matched controls revealed significant allele distribution differences in the CCTTT microsatellite region. The (CCTTT)14 variant, associated with higher activity in reporter constructs, was more prevalent in POAG patients, whereas (CCTTT)10 and (CCTTT)13 were less common. Electrophoretic mobility shift assays demonstrated specific protein binding of the (CCTTT)14 allele. These findings support a genetic link between NOS and POAG, highlighting the regulatory function of the CCTTT microsatellite in glaucoma pathogenesis.

title: A Novel Mutation in DFNA36 Locus Linked to Hearing Loss Phenotype
abstract: A novel mutation at the DFNA36 locus demonstrates a critical role in hearing loss pathogenesis. A North American Caucasian family (LMG248) exhibits autosomal dominant, non-syndromic, post-lingual, progressive sensorineural hearing loss. Hearing loss begins in the second decade of life, initially affecting high frequencies, and progresses to profound deafness by the fourth or fifth decade. The phenotype co-segregates with short-tandem repeat markers near the TMC1 gene at the DFNA36 locus on chromosome 9q31-q21. Affected individuals carry a novel missense substitution, p. D572H (c. G1714C), in the TMC1 gene. This mutation occurs at the same nucleotide and amino acid position as the only other reported DFNA36 mutation, p. D572N (c. G1714A). Our findings suggest a critical function for amino acid-572 in TMC1 or the pathogenesis of DFNA36-related hearing loss. The slower progression of hearing loss associated with p. D572H compared to p. D572N reflects a correlation between DFNA36 phenotype and TMC1 genotype. Deafness and sensorineural hearing loss are also observed in affected individuals, though no direct association with DFNA36 was found.

title: Genetic Associations in Tooth Agenesis and Craniofacial Syndromes
abstract: Interferon regulatory factor 6 (IRF6) and fibroblast growth factor receptor 1 (FGFR1) play a role in human tooth agenesis. Phenotypic features of syndromes provide insights into the genetic factors underlying isolated tooth agenesis. This study examined two genes linked to craniofacial syndromes, FGFR1 and IRF6, in families with isolated tooth agenesis. DNA samples from 116 case/parent trios were analyzed, with probands exhibiting at least one missing tooth, excluding third molars. Additional analysis included 89 cases and 50 controls from Ohio to verify findings. Genotyping used kinetic PCR or TaqMan assays. Linkage disequilibrium and marker allele transmission were assessed. Variants in the IRF6 gene associated with isolated orofacial clefts (rs861019, P=0.058; rs17015215-V274I, P=0.0006; rs7802, P=0.004) were also linked to tooth agenesis. Mutations in IRF6 cause Van der Woude and popliteal pterygium syndromes, characterized by oral clefts, preferential tooth agenesis of incisors and premolars, and lip pits. FGFR1 (P=0.014) and IRF6 (P=0.002) markers are associated with premolar agenesis. IRF6 interacts with MSX1 (P=0.001) and TGFA (P=0.03). Orofacial clefts (C566121) and tooth agenesis (D000848) are linked to rs861019. Craniofacial syndromes (D019465) are associated with rs861019. Van der Woude and popliteal pterygium syndromes (C536528, C562509) are connected to rs861019 and rs17015215-V274I. Oral clefts (D002972) are associated with rs7802. Orofacial clefts (C566121) are linked to MSX1 (4487). Van der Woude and popliteal pterygium syndromes (C536528) are connected to MSX1 (4487). Van der Woude and popliteal pterygium syndromes (C562509) are associated with TGFA (7039). Orofacial clefts (C566121) are linked to IRF6 (3664). Van der Woude and popliteal pterygium syndromes (C536528) are associated with IRF6 (3664). Van der Woude and popliteal pterygium syndromes (C562509) are linked to IRF6 (3664). Craniofacial syndromes (D019465) are connected to IRF6 (3664). Orofacial clefts (C566121) are associated with rs17015215-V274I (rs2235371). Van der Woude and popliteal pterygium syndromes (C536528) are connected to rs17015215-V274I (rs2235371). Van der Woude and popliteal pterygium syndromes (C562509) are linked to rs7802. Orofacial clefts (C566121) are associated with rs7802. Van der Woude and popliteal pterygium syndromes (C536528) are connected to rs7802. Van der Woude and popliteal pterygium syndromes (C562509) are associated with rs17015215-V274I (rs2235371).

title: A Genetic Mutation in Aggrecan Linked to Recessive Skeletal Dysplasia
abstract: A recessive skeletal dysplasia characterized by short stature and abnormal cartilage development results from a mutation in the aggrecan gene. Analysis of a family with three affected individuals identified an autosomal-recessive disorder linked to a specific genetic variant (c.6799 G-->A) in the aggrecan gene. This mutation affects the C-type lectin domain, altering calcium coordination and disrupting interactions with tenascin-C. The disease is associated with altered expression of aggrecan and chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan 4, both of which are critical for cartilage structure. Functional studies revealed that the mutation creates a glycosylation site without impairing protein processing, but changes the binding kinetics between aggrecan and tenascin-C. These findings highlight the role of aggrecan in skeletal development and the significance of calcium-dependent interactions in maintaining proper extracellular matrix function. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: c.6799 G -- > A.

title: Matriptase-2 Mutations and Their Role in Iron-Refractory Iron Deficiency Anemia
abstract: Mutations in the Matriptase-2 gene are linked to the pathogenesis of iron-refractory iron deficiency anemia (IRIDA), a condition characterized by elevated hepcidin levels. This study identifies two distinct mutations in the TMPRSS6 gene: a frameshift mutation (P686fs) caused by the insertion of four nucleotides CCCC at 2172_2173 in exon 16, which disrupts translation before the catalytic serine, and a di-nucleotide substitution (c.467C > A and c.468C > T) in exon 3, leading to the A118D missense mutation in the SEA domain of the extracellular stem region. These variants are associated with the IRIDA phenotype, which overlaps with iron deficiency anemia. Functional analysis reveals that both mutations impair matriptase-2 activity, resulting in ineffective suppression of hepcidin transcription.
