The A118D mutation also disrupts the structural balance of matriptase-2, affecting its activation. Collectively, these findings highlight the role of Matriptase-2 in regulating iron homeostasis and demonstrate that mutations outside the catalytic domain can significantly influence the disease mechanism. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: insertion of the four nucleotides CCCC; 2172_2173insCCCC.

title: Crack Cocaine Use and HIV Infection in Injection Drug Users
abstract: This study investigates the association between crack cocaine use and the risk of HIV infection among injection drug users. Participants were enrolled in a longitudinal study assessing the impact of illicit drug use on HIV seroconversion. Data were collected from individuals who injected drugs at least once in the month prior to enrollment, lived in the Vancouver area, were HIV-negative at baseline, and completed follow-up visits. The study was divided into three periods to evaluate changes in the risk of HIV infection over time. During the first period (May 1, 1996-Nov 30, 1999), 11.6% of participants reported daily crack cocaine use, increasing to 39.7% in the third period (Dec 1, 2002-Dec 30, 2005). Cox proportional hazards analysis revealed a significant positive correlation between crack cocaine use and the risk of HIV seroconversion, with hazard ratios of 1.03 (95% CI 0.57-1.85) in period 1, 1.68 (95% CI 1.01-2.80) in period 2, and 2.74 (95% CI 1.06-7.11) in period 3. These findings highlight the role of crack cocaine in increasing the likelihood of HIV infection among injection drug users.

title: Impact of G1359A Polymorphism in the Cannabinoid Receptor Gene on Adipocytokine Dynamics and Weight Management in Obese Subjects
abstract: This study examines the influence of the G1359A polymorphism in the cannabinoid receptor gene (CNR1) on adipocytokine profiles and weight management outcomes in obese individuals. A cohort of 94 obese patients underwent a 3-month hypocaloric diet and exercise intervention. Pre- and post-intervention assessments included anthropometric measurements, nutritional intake, and biochemical analyses. The G1359A polymorphism, characterized by a nucleotide substitution at position 1359 (Thr→A), was analyzed for its association with adipocytokine responses. Results showed significant weight loss in both wild-type (G1359G) and mutant (G1359A/A1359A) genotypes. Notably, weight loss was associated with reduced levels of resistin, leptin, and IL-6. The mutant allele (A1359) exhibited a stronger correlation with decreased adipocytokine concentrations, highlighting its potential role in metabolic regulation. The study underscores the interplay between genetic variation and metabolic outcomes in obesity management.

title: Mechanisms of P21-Activated Kinase 2 Activation by Gastrointestinal Hormones and Pancreatic Growth Factors
abstract: Gastrointestinal hormones/neurotransmitters and pancreatic growth factors activate P21 activated kinase 2 in pancreatic acinar cells through novel pathways. P-21-activated kinases (PAKs) are serine/threonine kinases with six isoforms divided into group-I (PAK1-3) and group-II (PAK4-6), playing critical roles in cytoskeletal dynamics, cell survival, secretion, and proliferation. This study explores how gastrointestinal (GI) hormones, neurotransmitters, and growth factors influence Group-I PAKs, focusing on PAK2. Only PAK2 is present in acini, and it is activated by pancreatic growth factors like EGF, PDGF, and bFGF, as well as secretagogues such as CCK and bombesin, which trigger phospholipase-C (PLC) activation. TPA activates PAK2 via PKC, but not through calcium mobilization or cyclic AMP elevation. CCK-induced PAK2 activation requires both high- and low-affinity CCK1-receptor-state engagement, and is partially inhibited by PKC- and Src-inhibition. IPA-3, which prevents PAK2 binding to small-GTPases, reduces PAK2 activation and CCK-induced ERK1/2 signaling. These findings demonstrate that PAK2 is activated by GI hormones, growth factors, and small-GTPases via PLC and PKC pathways, highlighting its role in pancreatic signaling cascades. PAK2's dual dependence on receptor states and signaling components makes it a key target for therapies in pancreatic disorders like pancreatitis. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: low-affinity-CCK1-receptor-state; pancreatic growth-factors; LY294002; wortmannin; thapsigargin; amylase; PI3K-inhibitors; carbachol; PAK4 - 6.

title: Raloxifene's Impact on Fibrinolytic Markers and Bone Conditions
abstract: The influence of raloxifene on fibrinolytic parameters such as TAFI, tPA, and PAI-1 was evaluated in postmenopausal women. This prospective study enrolled 42 women with osteopenia or osteoporosis, with 26 receiving raloxifene (60 mg/day) and calcium (500 mg/day), while 16 matched controls received only calcium. Plasma levels of TAFI, tPA, and PAI-1 were measured at baseline and after 6 months. Raloxifene treatment was associated with a 20% reduction in TAFI (P=0.02) and a 30% increase in tPA (P=0.04). A negative correlation was observed between raloxifene and osteoporosis severity. Venous thromboembolism incidence was higher in raloxifene-treated patients, potentially linked to elevated tPA levels. Calcium levels showed no significant association with TAFI or PAI-1, and osteopenia was not linked to TAFI or tPA. No significant relationships were found between PAI-1 and venous thromboembolism, or between TAFI and osteoporosis.

title: A Case of Ectodermal Dysplasia-Skin Fragility Syndrome Caused by a Novel 888delC Mutation in Plakophilin 1
abstract: A 6-year-old boy presented with Ectodermal dysplasia-skin fragility syndrome, characterized by red skin at birth, progressive plantar keratoderma, nail dystrophy, and alopecia. Genetic analysis revealed a homozygous 888delC mutation in the plakophilin 1 gene, which is associated with inherited disorder. The mutation was linked to the syndrome, showing a Positive_Correlation between 888delC and Ectodermal dysplasia-skin fragility syndrome. The patient's condition also demonstrated Association with genodermatosis and plakophilin 1, as well as Association between inherited disorder and plakophilin 1. Skin biopsy showed widened intercellular spaces and reduced desmosomes, consistent with the role of plakophilin 1 in maintaining desmosomal adhesion. This case highlights the importance of plakophilin 1 in both skin fragility and ectodermal development.

title: DNA Damage and Repair in Gastric Cancer: Association with hOGG1 and RAD51 Gene Polymorphisms
abstract: DNA damage and repair mechanisms play a critical role in the development and progression of gastric cancer. The susceptibility of cells to mutagens and their capacity to repair DNA lesions are key factors in cancer induction and progression. Variations in genes involved in DNA repair, such as hOGG1 and RAD51, can influence these processes. The hOGG1 gene encodes a glycosylase essential for base excision repair, while RAD51 is a key protein in homologous recombination repair. Both genes are involved in repairing oxidative DNA lesions, which may contribute to gastric cancer. In this study, we analyzed the levels of basal and oxidative DNA damage, as well as the kinetics of DNA damage removal after hydrogen peroxide exposure, in peripheral blood lymphocytes from 30 gastric cancer patients and 30 healthy controls. The repair capacity was assessed using the comet assay with DNA repair enzymes endonuclease III and formamidopyrimidine-DNA glycosylase, which recognize oxidized DNA bases. The genotypes of common polymorphisms were determined via restriction fragment length polymorphism PCR. The study identified a strong association between gastric cancer occurrence and the G/C genotype of the G135C polymorphism in the RAD51 gene. Additionally, this genotype was strongly correlated with gastric cancer in individuals with high oxidative DNA damage levels. No significant association was found between the Ser326Cys polymorphism of the hOGG1 gene and gastric cancer, regardless of DNA repair status or oxidative DNA lesion levels. These findings suggest that the G135C polymorphism in RAD51 may influence gastric cancer risk through its effect on cellular response to oxidative stress. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: G-->C transversion at 1245 position; G-->C substitution at position 135.

title: Genetic Variants and Neurodegenerative Processes in Alzheimer's Disease
abstract: The G51S variant of purine nucleoside phosphorylase is linked to inflammatory responses and neurodegenerative disorders in Alzheimer's disease patients. Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a complex condition with multifactorial etiology, and several genetic factors contribute to its development. Purine nucleotides and nucleosides are crucial in the brain, involved in neurotransmission, neuromodulation, trophic factor release, apoptosis, and inflammatory pathways. These molecules may play a key role in neurodegenerative processes associated with AD. In this study, the distribution of the exonic G/A single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) in the purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP) gene, leading to the amino acid substitution serine to glycine at position 51 (G51S), was examined in a large cohort of AD patients (n=321) and non-demented controls (n=208). The PNP polymorphism distribution showed no significant difference between patients and controls. Further analysis of AD patients based on the progression rate of cognitive decline over a 2-year period revealed an increased frequency of the PNP AA genotype in those with rapid cognitive deterioration compared to those with slower decline. These findings indicate that the G51S PNP polymorphism is associated with a faster rate of cognitive decline in AD patients, underscoring the role of purine metabolism in the disease's progression. Additionally, the study highlights the connection between inflammatory processes and neurodegenerative disorders in the context of Alzheimer's disease. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: neurodegenerative disorder; Alzheimer 's disease.

title: Genetic Analysis of Retinoblastoma and RB1 Gene in Tumors
abstract: This study investigated the association between Retinoblastoma and the RB1 gene in tumors. DNA was extracted from peripheral blood and tumors of 48 patients with Retinoblastoma and their relatives. Seven microsatellite markers, including those intragenic and flanking the RB1 gene, were analyzed using PCR and genetic sequencing. LOH of the RB1 gene was detected in 68.8% of cases (33/48 patients; p=0.002; 95% CI 0.614, 0.856), correlating with tumor development. Germline deletions were identified in six patients (12.5%), with a higher frequency of maternal allele loss (p=0.02). A co-segregating haplotype was observed in two hereditary cases. These findings suggest that RB1 gene LOH plays a significant role in Retinoblastoma pathogenesis, with large deletions and haplotype analysis providing insights for genetic counseling in affected families.

title: Genetic Analysis of CYP2F1 Polymorphisms and Their Association with Lung Cancer
abstract: This study investigates the genetic variability of the CYP2F1 gene and its potential implications in lung cancer susceptibility. The CYP2F1 enzyme, a key member of the cytochrome P450 family, is primarily expressed in lung tissue and plays a role in metabolizing pneumotoxicants with carcinogenic potential. We conducted a comprehensive analysis of the CYP2F1 genomic sequence in DNA samples from 80 individuals, comprising 35 patients with lung cancer and 45 healthy controls, using PCR-SSCP techniques. A total of 24 mutations were identified, distributed across the promoter region, coding sequences, and flanking intronic regions. In addition to the wild-type CYP2F1*1 allele, seven polymorphic variants, including CYP2F1*2A, *2B, *3, *4, *5A, *5B, and *6, were characterized. The most prevalent variant, CYP2F1*2A (24.3%), contains a combination of mutations, such as Asp218Asn and Gln266His, along with a 1-bp insertion (c.14_15insC) that introduces a premature stop codon in exon 2, potentially leading to a non-functional protein. The presence of 7% homozygotes for the frameshift mutation suggests interindividual variability in CYP2F1 activity, which may influence toxic responses to pneumotoxicants and susceptibility to chemically induced diseases. Notably, the CYP2F1*2A variant is linked to carcinogenic potential, highlighting its role in modulating lung cancer risk. However, the study did not find direct evidence linking the CYP2F1 genetic variants to the pathogenesis of lung cancer.

title: Comparative study of unilateral pallidotomy and subthalamotomy in advanced idiopathic Parkinson's disease
abstract: A prospective, randomized, double-blind trial was conducted to evaluate the efficacy of unilateral pallidotomy and subthalamotomy in patients with advanced idiopathic Parkinson's disease refractory to medical treatment. Twelve consecutive patients (mean age 57.2 ± 5.3 years; 8 men, 4 women) with similar disease duration (mean 8.8 ± 3.1 years), disabling motor fluctuations (Hoehn-Yahr stage 3-5 in off-drug phases), and levodopa-induced dyskinesias were included. All patients exhibited bilateral symptoms and received levodopa equivalent dosing. Eight patients underwent globus pallidus interna (GPi) surgery, and four had subthalamic nucleus (STN) surgery. Clinical assessments included the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS), Hoehn-Yahr score, and Schwab England ADL score in 'on' and 'off' drug conditions before and 6 months post-surgery. Significant improvements were noted in all contralateral major parkinsonian motor signs. Levodopa equivalent daily intake was reduced in the STN group. UPDRS, Hoehn-Yahr, and ADL scores showed similar changes in both groups. Cognitive functions remained stable. Complications occurred in two patients: one developed left homonymous hemianopsia after pallidotomy, and another experienced left hemiballistic movements 5 days post-subthalamotomy, which partially improved with Valproate 1000 mg/day. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: idiopathic Parkinson 's disease.

title: Novel Mutations in CHST6 Gene Associated with Macular Corneal Dystrophy
abstract: A family with Macular corneal dystrophy (MCD) was studied to identify mutations in the CHST6 gene. The patients showed abnormal deposition of keratan sulfate (KS) in the corneal stroma, as revealed by colloidal iron staining. Genomic DNA from 11 family members was analyzed, and compound heterozygous mutations c.892C > T and c.1072T > C were detected in three affected individuals. These mutations resulted in the substitution of a stop codon for glutamine at codon 298 (p.Q298X) and a missense change at codon 358, tyrosine to histidine (p.Y358H). The mutations were not found in 100 control subjects, suggesting a novel genetic basis for MCD. Iron and keratan sulfate were found to be present in the corneal stroma, with no direct biochemical interaction between them. Collagen fibers were observed to be abnormally thickened, and the mutations were linked to impaired KS metabolism. The study highlights the role of CHST6 in maintaining normal corneal structure and function. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: codon 358 , tyrosine to histidine.

title: Tenofovir and Vancomycin in the Management of Osteomyelitis and Renal Complications
abstract: Patients with AIDS on tenofovir therapy experienced acute renal failure during a prolonged vancomycin course for osteomyelitis. Renal failure occurred in two patients receiving tenofovir disoproxil fumarate as part of an antiretroviral regimen, with a history of prolonged vancomycin treatment. Tenofovir has been linked to Fanconi syndrome and renal insufficiency due to its effects on the proximal renal tubule. Vancomycin nephrotoxicity is rare but can occur with coadministration of nephrotoxic agents. Clinicians should recognize that tenofovir may increase the risk of renal failure when used with prolonged vancomycin therapy. Additionally, vancomycin was associated with nephrotoxicity in patients with osteomyelitis, while tenofovir showed a positive correlation with Fanconi syndrome and renal failure.

title: PKCalpha Signaling in Endometrial Carcinogenesis
abstract: Protein kinase C alpha-dependent signaling plays a pivotal role in endometrial cancer progression and tumorigenesis. Endometrial cancer, the most prevalent invasive gynecologic malignancy, remains poorly understood in terms of its molecular mechanisms and signaling pathways. This study investigates the functional role of the PKCalpha isoform in a model of endometrial adenocarcinoma. Ishikawa cells with PKCalpha depletion exhibited reduced proliferation, decreased colony formation in anchorage-independent assays, and impaired tumor growth in nude mice. PKCalpha knockdown significantly increased the levels of cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitors p21(Cip1/WAF1) and p27(Kip1). Despite the absence of functional phosphatase and tensin homolog in these cells, PKCalpha depletion reduced Akt phosphorylation at serine 473 and inhibited the phosphorylation of its downstream target, glycogen synthase kinase-3beta. PKCalpha knockdown also led to decreased basal ERK phosphorylation and reduced ERK activation upon EGF stimulation. The elevation of p21 and p27 was not observed with ERK and Akt inhibitors, indicating that PKCalpha regulates CDK expression independently of Akt and ERK. Immunohistochemical analysis of Grade 1 endometrioid adenocarcinoma showed elevated PKCalpha expression in tumor foci, which was not present in normal endometrial tissue. These findings highlight the critical role of PKCalpha signaling in endometrial tumorigenesis through the regulation of CDK inhibitors and Akt/ERK-dependent proliferative pathways, suggesting that targeting PKCalpha could offer novel therapeutic strategies for endometrial tumors.

title: Metallothionein Induction Modulates Hippocampal Function in Carmustine-Treated Rats
abstract: Induction of Metallothionein by ZnSO(4) reduces caspase-3 activity and TNFalpha levels while preserving cognitive function in carmustine-treated rats. Hippocampal integrity is crucial for maintaining cognitive performance. This study investigated the effects of Metallothionein induction on carmustine-induced cognitive dysfunction. Sixty male Wistar albino rats were divided into four groups: control, carmustine-treated, ZnSO(4)-pretreated, and ZnSO(4)-pretreated followed by carmustine. Results showed that carmustine administration caused deterioration of learning and short-term memory, accompanied by decreased hippocampal glutathione reductase activity and reduced glutathione levels. Serum TNFalpha, hippocampal Metallothionein, and malondialdehyde levels increased, along with elevated caspase-3 activity. ZnSO(4) pretreatment counteracted these effects, restoring glutathione reductase activity, preventing glutathione depletion, and reducing TNFalpha, MDA, and caspase-3 levels. Histological analyses revealed improved hippocampal structure in ZnSO(4)-pretreated groups. Cognitive dysfunction was significantly attenuated in animals receiving ZnSO(4) before carmustine treatment. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: toxicity; ZnSO(4 ).

title: Genetic Variants in PCSK1 and Metabolic Traits: Insights into Proinsulin Conversion and Insulin Sensitivity
abstract: This study explores the association between common single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the PCSK1 gene and metabolic traits, including obesity, insulin resistance, and abnormal glucose homeostasis. The SNPs rs6232 and rs6235, located within the PCSK1 gene, were examined for their influence on proinsulin conversion and glucose metabolism. A cohort of 1498 German subjects was genotyped for these SNPs, and metabolically characterized through oral glucose tolerance tests (OGTT) measuring glucose, insulin, proinsulin, and C-peptide levels. A subset underwent hyperinsulinemic-euglycemic clamps to assess insulin secretion. Results showed no significant association between rs6235 and rs6232 with BMI or weight-related traits. However, the minor alleles of both SNPs were linked to elevated AUCproinsulin and AUCproinsulin/AUCinsulin. The rs6232 minor allele was associated with higher insulin sensitivity, lower HOMAIR, and reduced 120-min glucose levels. These findings highlight the role of PCSK1 variants in glucose-stimulated proinsulin conversion and metabolic outcomes. Notably, rs6232 also influenced glucose intolerance and abnormal glucose homeostasis. The study underscores the genetic basis of metabolic traits while emphasizing the distinct roles of PCSK1 variants in insulin sensitivity and glucose regulation.

title: Emodin's Inhibitory Effects on Fatty Acid Synthase and Colon Cancer Progression
abstract: Emodin, an anthraquinone derivative, significantly inhibits fatty acid synthase (FASN) activity and suppresses colon cancer proliferation in human cell lines. FASN, a critical enzyme for de novo fatty acid synthesis, is overexpressed in colon cancer, making it a promising therapeutic target. Emodin treatment reduced FASN protein levels and enzymatic activity, as measured by NADP+ oxidation at 340 nm, while increasing intracellular free fatty acid levels. The anticancer effects of emodin were assessed using Cell Counting Kit-8 assays and Annexin V/propidium iodide staining, revealing enhanced apoptosis in HCT116 cells. Palmitate, the end product of FASN activity, counteracted emodin-induced cell viability loss, suggesting a regulatory role in lipid metabolism. Emodin also modulated signaling pathways, including phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/Akt and mitogen-activated protein kinases/extracellular signal-regulated kinases 1/2, which are implicated in cancer cell survival. Combining emodin with cerulenin, a FASN inhibitor, amplified antiproliferative effects, highlighting the potential of targeting FASN in colon cancer therapy. These findings underscore the role of emodin in disrupting FASN-dependent processes and altering cancer cell behavior through multiple molecular mechanisms. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate.

title: Evaluation of RGS4 as a Potential Candidate Gene for Schizophrenia
abstract: This study examines the role of RGS4 in the context of schizophrenia. Analysis of three single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) within the promoter region (SNP4, SNP7) and intron 1 (SNP18) of RGS4 revealed no significant associations with schizophrenia in 200 pedigrees from Taiwan (800 individuals). Neither individual SNPs nor their haplotype combinations demonstrated a statistically significant link to the disorder. The findings do not support RGS4 as a candidate gene for schizophrenia based on these genetic markers.

title: Genetic and Environmental Factors in Skin Carcinogenesis in Immunosuppressed Patients
abstract: A study on skin cancer risk factors in immunosuppressed renal transplant recipients reveals a high prevalence of UV-specific CC to TT mutations in the p53 gene. Immunosuppressed patients undergoing renal transplants are at increased risk for non-melanoma skin cancers, particularly squamous cell carcinomas. Researchers analyzed skin lesions from these patients with aggressive tumors, examining p53 gene modifications, HPV DNA presence, and the p53 codon 72 genotype along with XPD repair gene polymorphisms. Twenty-four p53 mutations were identified in 15/25 (60%) non-melanoma skin cancers, including one deletion and 23 base substitutions, most being UV-specific C to T transitions at bipyrimidine sites. Notably, 35% (6/17) of cases showed tandem mutations, including four UV signature CC to TT transitions potentially linked to altered DNA repair caused by cyclosporin A. Eight p53 mutations were found in 7/17 (41%) precancerous actinic keratosis, suggesting early involvement of p53 mutations in skin carcinogenesis. Immunohistochemical analysis confirmed a strong correlation between p53 accumulation and mutations. HPV DNA was detected in 78% of skin lesions (60% Basal Cell Carcinomas, 82% actinic keratosis, 79% squamous cell carcinomas). Thus, immunosuppression increases the risk of infections by HPVs, including epidermodysplasia verruciformis, which may contribute to skin cancer development. No association was found between HPV status and p53 mutations. Additionally, p53 codon 72 and XPD genotype frequencies in RTRs were comparable to control populations. The high prevalence of CC to TT mutations in the p53 gene underscores the role of UV radiation as a major risk factor, with immunosuppressive drug treatment potentially modulating DNA repair processes in skin carcinogenesis.

title: QT Prolongation and Syncope in Heroin Dependence Treatment
abstract: This study examines the prevalence of QT prolongation and syncope in patients receiving methadone or buprenorphine for heroin dependence. Methadone, a synthetic opioid, is commonly used to manage opioid addiction by reducing illicit drug use. QT prolongation, a risk factor for torsade de pointes, has been observed in methadone users. Syncope episodes in this population may be attributed to methadone's proarrhythmic effects rather than illicit opioid use. A cross-sectional study of 450 heroin-dependent individuals in Copenhagen found that methadone dose correlated with prolonged QT intervals, while buprenorphine showed no significant association. Among methadone-treated patients, 28% of men and 32% of women had QTc intervals exceeding 0.440 s. Higher methadone doses were linked to increased syncope reports, highlighting a potential association between methadone use and cardiovascular events. Buprenorphine, another opioid, did not show significant correlations with QT prolongation or syncope. These findings underscore the need for careful monitoring of methadone users for QT-related complications and syncope.

title: Genetic Analysis of Alkaptonuria in a New Population Sample
abstract: A study was conducted to investigate the prevalence of alkaptonuria and identify the genetic mutations in a cohort of 3000 individuals from a different geographic region. Urine samples were collected from 2950 participants, including students from government schools in Riyadh and private institutions in Doha, and analyzed for homogentisic acid using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry. Genomic DNA was extracted from family members of affected cases, and specific primers were used to amplify the HGD gene's exons and flanking sequences. One sample showed elevated homogentisic acid levels, and genetic testing confirmed a c.342delA mutation in exon 3, resulting in the R58fs alteration. The study found no reported cases of joint pain among the participants, and the identified mutation was linked to alkaptonuria. Homogentisic acid levels were correlated with the presence of the HGD gene mutation, while joint pain and the c.342delA mutation were not directly associated.

title: Functional Analysis of ETS2 and SIM2 in Down Syndrome
abstract: This study investigates the functional roles of ETS2 and SIM2 in Down syndrome (DS). Trisomy of the 21st chromosome results in an overexpression of multiple regulatory genes in DS. While allelic and genotypic variations among genes are intriguing, this area has not been thoroughly examined in DS. In this research, four SNPs in two transcription factors, Single minded 2 (SIM2) and V-ets erythroblastosis virus E26 oncogene homolog2 (ETS2), located on the 21st chromosome were analyzed to explore their involvement in DS. Genomic DNA from Indian individuals with DS (N=132), their parents (N=209), and ethnically matched controls (N=149) was tested for functionally significant SNPs using PCR-based methods and statistical analysis. ETS2 rs461155 exhibited high heterozygosity in DS patients. A significantly lower frequency of the SIM2 C-G haplotype (rs2073601-rs2073416) was observed in DS individuals and their fathers (P=0.01185). Additionally, reduced frequencies of the A-C-C-G haplotype and increased frequencies of A-C-A-G haplotypes were noted in DS subjects (P=0.02089 and P=0.00588, respectively). The rs2073601 'A' allele, associated with a nonsynonymous substitution of leucine to methionine, may contribute to DS in this population.

title: Etoposide-Induced OCT4A Modulation in Embryonal Carcinoma Cells and Its Impact on Cellular Fate
abstract: The effect of etoposide on OCT4A expression in embryonal carcinoma cells is investigated in this study. Tumor cellular senescence triggered by genotoxic agents has been linked to the induction of stemness features, influencing treatment responses. Previous findings showed that etoposide treatment of PA-1 cells increases p53-dependent OCT4A and p21Cip1, which regulate self-renewal and cell cycle arrest. This study further examines the interactions between OCT4A, p21Cip1, and other critical regulators. ETO treatment leads to heterogeneous OCT4A and p21Cip1 levels, indicating cellular disadaptation. Silencing OCT4A reduces p21Cip1, alters cell cycle control, and suppresses terminal senescence, while p21Cip1 silencing does not affect OCT4A. SOX2 and NANOG expression remain stable, suggesting OCT4A's role is not in pluripotency. Instead, ETO-induced OCT4A is associated with AMPK activation, a key metabolic stress regulator. p16ink4a undergoes autophagic sequestration in ETO-treated cells, enabling alternative fates. Persistent DNA damage impairs autophagy, leading to p16ink4a accumulation, nuclear disintegration, and cell loss. These findings imply that OCT4A's induction after DNA damage functions in cellular stress by modulating p21Cip1, which interacts with AMPK to regulate autophagy. Additionally, autophagy failure due to sustained DNA damage causes terminal senescence. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: tumors.

title: Mutational Analysis of Transferrin Receptor 2 and HFE in Hemochromatosis Patients from Japan
abstract: This study investigates the genetic basis of hemochromatosis in Japanese patients, focusing on mutations in the HFE and transferrin receptor 2 (TfR2) genes. The low frequency of the C282Y HFE mutation in this population suggests the involvement of other genetic factors. We analyzed nine patients diagnosed with hemochromatosis and identified two novel TfR2 mutations: L490R and V561X. Additionally, the 714C- variant was detected in the patient harboring L490R. A patient homozygous for both L490R and 714C- exhibited mild hemochromatosis with cirrhotic liver changes and diabetes mellitus. Another patient with V561X showed severe iron overload, accompanied by cirrhosis, diabetes, and skin pigmentation. These findings highlight the role of TfR2 mutations in hemochromatosis pathogenesis in Japan, complementing prior evidence of TfR2 involvement. The association between hemochromatosis and TfR2 mutations, as well as the link between iron overload and V561X, underscores the genetic complexity of this condition. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: AVAQ 594 - 597 deletion; glucose.

title: Succinylcholine-induced Masseter Muscle Rigidity and Malignant Hyperthermia in Anesthetic Management
abstract: Succinylcholine-induced masseter muscle rigidity was observed during a bronchoscopic intervention for tracheal foreign body removal. This condition is recognized as an early indicator of malignant hyperthermia risk. The clinical decision to proceed with anesthesia relied on the severity of the rigidity and procedural urgency. A case report describes a patient who developed severe masseter muscle rigidity (jaw of steel) following succinylcholine administration. Propofol was administered to maintain anesthesia, with all resources available for malignant hyperthermia monitoring. The positive correlation between Succinylcholine-induced effects and masseter muscle rigidity underscores the need for vigilant anesthetic oversight in high-risk scenarios.

title: TMC1 Mutations and Their Role in Non-Syndromic Deafness
abstract: This study investigates the genetic basis of non-syndromic recessive deafness (C564609) and DFNB7/B11 deafness (C563417) in a cohort of 557 families from South Asian populations. Non-syndromic deafness (D003638) is known to exhibit genetic heterogeneity, with mutations in the TMC1 (117531) gene playing a key role in DFNB7/B11 deafness. Analysis of TMC1 sequence variations revealed 9 distinct mutations responsible for 3.4% of cases, including the p. R34X (rs121908073) mutation, which accounts for 1.8% of the cohort. The p. R34X mutation was found to originate from a common founder, with its presence observed in both affected and unaffected individuals. While TMC1 mutations are strongly associated with Non-syndromic deafness (D003638) and DFNB7/B11 deafness (C563417), no direct association was found between p. R34X and non-syndromic recessive deafness (C564609), nor between TMC1 and p. R34X. These findings highlight the genetic diversity of TMC1 mutations across different populations.

title: AIP Gene Mutation Analysis in Pediatric Patients with Pituitary Adenomas
abstract: Aryl hydrocarbon receptor interacting protein (AIP) gene mutation analysis was conducted in 40 pediatric patients with sporadic pituitary adenomas. The study aimed to determine the prevalence of germline AIP mutations in patients with pituitary adenomas. Genomic DNA was analyzed for mutations in the AIP gene using PCR amplification and direct sequencing. Patients were recruited from three medical centers in Germany, with a focus on those under 18 years of age at diagnosis or with clinical evidence of adenoma development before 18 years. A heterozygous in-frame deletion Y248del was identified in a GH-secreting adenoma patient, while no mutations were found in patients with non-GH-secreting adenomas. Loss of heterozygosity analysis confirmed the loss of the wild-type allele in the tumour sample. First-degree relatives of the affected individual showed no clinical manifestations of the mutation. These findings suggest that AIP mutations are associated with GH-secreting adenomas, even in the absence of a family history. The study highlights the importance of AIP in pediatric pituitary adenomas, although further research is needed to confirm its role in other adenoma subtypes.

title: Curcumin Modulates Sp Transcription Factors and Antiangiogenic Proteins in Bladder Cancer
abstract: Curcumin decreases specificity protein expression in bladder cancer cells. Curcumin, a polyphenolic compound derived from turmeric, has been extensively studied for its anticancer properties. This study demonstrates that 10 to 25 micromol/L curcumin inhibits 253JB-V and KU7 bladder cancer cell growth, accompanied by induction of apoptosis and reduced expression of the proapoptotic protein survivin and the angiogenic proteins vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and VEGF receptor 1 (VEGFR1). Given that survivin, VEGF, and VEGFR1 expression depends on specificity protein (Sp) transcription factors, curcumin's effects on Sp protein levels were investigated. Results show that curcumin induces proteasome-dependent down-regulation of Sp1, Sp3, and Sp4 in these cells. Furthermore, RNA interference experiments with Sp1, Sp3, and Sp4 small inhibitory RNAs revealed that curcumin's suppression of nuclear factor kappaB (NF-kappaB)-dependent genes like bcl-2, survivin, and cyclin D1 is partially mediated by Sp protein loss. Curcumin also reduces bladder tumor growth in athymic nude mice with KU7 xenografts, correlating with decreased Sp1, Sp3, and Sp4 protein levels in tumors. These findings highlight curcumin's mechanism of action in bladder cancer through Sp transcription factor modulation.

title: Regulation of Cholangiocarcinoma Growth by Histamine Receptor Signaling
abstract: Activation of protein kinase Calpha through H3 histamine receptors inhibits the proliferation of cholangiocarcinoma cells in vitro and in vivo. Histamine exerts its effects via four receptors (HRH1, HRH2, HRH3, and HRH4). The d-myo-inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate (IP(3))/Ca(2+)/protein kinase C (PKC)/mitogen-activated protein kinase pathway is implicated in cholangiocarcinoma progression. HRH3 expression was detected in all tested cell types, including intrahepatic and extrahepatic cell lines, normal cholangiocytes, and tissue samples. In Mz-ChA-1 cells exposed to (R)-(alpha)-(-)-methylhistamine dihydrobromide, increased IP(3) levels and PKCalpha phosphorylation were observed, while ERK1/2 phosphorylation was reduced. PKCalpha localization shifted from cytosolic to membrane domains upon histamine stimulation. Knockdown of PKCalpha prevented histamine-induced growth inhibition and ERK1/2 dephosphorylation. In vivo, treatment with (R)-(alpha)-(-)-methylhistamine dihydrobromide decreased tumor volume and suppressed VEGF-A and VEGF-C expression, along with their receptors. Tumor analysis revealed elevated PKCalpha expression and reduced proliferation. These findings suggest that H3 histamine receptor activation modulates PKCalpha-dependent signaling to regulate cholangiocarcinoma growth. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: VEGF receptor 3; VEGF receptor 2; cyclic AMP; vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-A; H3 histamine receptor-mediated.

title: Genetic Polymorphisms in IRF5 and Their Association with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
abstract: Variants in the IRF5 gene, including rs2070197, were investigated for their genetic linkage with systemic lupus erythematosus across multiple populations. This study evaluated the association between IRF5 and rs2004640, as well as their interaction with rs10954213 in influencing disease susceptibility. Genotyping of four IRF5 polymorphisms was performed in 1488 SLE patients and 1466 controls, with gene expression analyzed via quantitative PCR using RNA from peripheral blood mononuclear cells. Results showed that the promoter variant and rs2070197 independently contributed to the association of rs2004640 and rs10954213. Gene expression analysis revealed that rs10954213 had the most significant effect on IRF5 transcript levels. The study confirmed the association of the promoter variant with SLE in five distinct populations, highlighting rs10954213 as the primary SNP responsible for altered IRF5 expression in PBMC.

title: Genetic Mutations in the Aristaless-Related Homeobox Gene and Their Association with Neurological and Developmental Disorders
abstract: Mutations in the Aristaless-related homeobox (170302) gene have been implicated in a wide range of neurological and developmental disorders, including intellectual disability (D008607) and brain and genital malformations (D000013). A specific mutation, c.1074G > T, is associated with intellectual disability. Additionally, mutations such as c.304ins(GCG)(7)'expansion and c.429_452dup (dup24bp) are linked to various phenotypic manifestations. A novel mutation, dup27bp, has been identified, along with larger duplications like dup33bp. These mutations are often accompanied by polyalanine (C019529) expansions, which may contribute to the severity of the associated conditions. Comprehensive screening of DNA samples from individuals with intellectual disability revealed that several mutations in the ARX gene, including those in the homeodomain, are associated with distinct clinical features. The presence of these genetic variants is correlated with increased phenotypic severity, highlighting the complex relationship between gene mutations and developmental outcomes.

title: Prenatal Caffeine Exposure and Renal Developmental Programming
abstract: Prenatal caffeine exposure (PCE) was found to induce intrauterine growth retardation (IUGR) in offspring, which is associated with glomerulosclerosis and interstitial fibrosis in adult kidneys. The study demonstrated that PCE leads to dysplasia of fetal kidneys, characterized by an enlarged Bowman's space and shrunken glomerular tuft. Renal angiotensin II receptor type 2 (AT2R) expression was reduced in adult offspring, while the AT1aR/AT2R ratio increased. Additionally, PCE was linked to decreased expression of podocin and nephrin, markers of podocyte dysfunction. Glial-cell-line-derived neurotrophic factor (GDNF)/tyrosine kinase receptor signaling was inhibited, contributing to renal structural damage. The renal AT2R functional programming appeared to mediate the developmental origin of glomerulosclerosis, with elevated serum creatinine levels observed in PCE-exposed individuals. These findings highlight the role of caffeine in renal developmental programming and the pathogenesis of glomerulosclerosis. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: angiotensin II receptor type 1a.

title: Myc-Driven B-Cell Signaling in Precancerous States
abstract: Myc promotes B-cell receptor signaling in precancerous B cells and enhances resistance to Btk inhibition. Dysregulation of the oncogenic transcription factor MYC is linked to B-cell transformation and is a driver for B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (B-NHL). MYC overexpression in B-NHL is associated with aggressive phenotypes and poor prognosis. While genomic studies suggest a connection between MYC overexpression and BCR signaling molecules in B-NHL, the signaling pathways essential to Myc-mediated B-cell transformation remain unclear. We used intracellular phospho-flow cytometry to explore the relationship between Myc and BCR signaling in pre-malignant B cells. In the Eu-myc mouse model, where Myc is overexpressed specifically in B cells, both basal and stimulated BCR signaling were increased in precancerous B lymphocytes from Eu-myc mice compared with wild-type littermates. B cells overexpressing Myc showed constitutively higher levels of activated CD79a, Btk, Plcg2, and Erk1/2. Notably, Myc-overexpressing B cells maintained elevated BCR signaling despite treatment with ibrutinib, a Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitor. Furthermore, PI3K/Akt pathway signaling was also increased in Eu-myc B cells, and this increase was partially suppressed with ibrutinib. Additionally, experiments with Btk-null B cells revealed off-target effects of ibrutinib on BCR signaling. Our findings indicate that in pre-malignant B cells, Myc overexpression is sufficient to activate BCR and PI3K/Akt signaling pathways and further enhances signaling following BCR ligation. Therefore, our results suggest that precancerous B cells have already acquired enhanced survival and growth capabilities before transformation, and that elevated MYC levels confer resistance to pharmacologic inhibitors of BCR signaling, which has significant implications for B-NHL treatment. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: Bruton 's tyrosine kinase.

title: A TSPO ligand reduces brain injury following intracerebral hemorrhage
abstract: A TSPO ligand, etifoxine, mitigates brain injury in models of intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). ICH is a severe condition with limited therapeutic options. Following ICH, leukocyte infiltration and microglial activation are accompanied by increased TSPO expression. TSPO ligands have demonstrated anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective effects in CNS injury models. This study investigated the impact of etifoxine on brain injury and inflammation in two mouse models of ICH. TSPO was upregulated in Iba1(+) cells from ICH patients and in CD11b(+)CD45(int) cells from collagenase-induced ICH mice. Etifoxine significantly reduced neurodeficits and perihematomal brain edema after ICH induction. In collagenase-induced ICH mice, etifoxine's protective effects were linked to decreased leukocyte infiltration and reduced production of IL-6 and TNF-a by microglia. Etifoxine improved blood-brain barrier integrity and decreased cell death. Notably, the protective effect was abolished in mice with microglia depletion using a colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor inhibitor. These findings suggest that etifoxine mitigates brain injury and inflammation after ICH. TSPO may serve as a therapeutic target requiring further investigation in ICH. Additionally, TSPO expression was correlated with anti-inflammatory responses, while etifoxine showed a negative correlation with brain edema in ICH models.

title: Tubulin Isoforms and Cortical Malformations in Neuronal Migration
abstract: Mutations in the a-tubulin TUBA1A gene result in disrupted microtubule dynamics and altered neuronal migration patterns. During brain development, neurons undergo extensive migratory processes that rely on microtubules assembled from a/b-tubulin heterodimers. Alterations in the a-tubulin isotype TUBA1A are linked to cortical malformations in humans. This study investigates the functional roles of TUBA1A and other tubulin isoforms in neuronal migration. In mice with a TUBA1A missense mutation (S140 G), neurons exhibit delayed migration and abnormal branching, accompanied by glial cell redistribution along the rostral migratory stream. Live imaging reveals impaired neuronal movement and disrupted nucleus-centrosome coupling, which correlate with changes in microtubule straightness. The TUBA1A mutation leads to conformational changes in the a/b-tubulin heterodimer, affecting microtubule structure. Additionally, Tuba8, another a-tubulin isotype associated with cortical malformations, shows distinct functional properties compared to TUBA1A. These findings highlight the critical role of TUBA1A in maintaining microtubule flexibility and proper neuronal migration during brain development.

title: HEB's Role in Fetal γδ T Cell Development and Gene Regulation
abstract: HEB is essential for the development of fetal IL-17-producing γδ T cells. IL-17-producing γδ T (γδT17) cells are critical components of the innate immune system. However, the gene networks governing their development remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that HEB (HeLa E-box binding protein, encoded by Tcf12) is required for the generation of a novel subset of fetal-derived CD73- γδT17 cells. HEB is necessary in immature CD24+CD73- γδ T cells for the expression of Sox4, Sox13, and Rorc, while acute Id3 expression represses these genes. HEB deficiency also affects mature CD73+ γδ T cells, leading to reduced RORγt expression and impaired IL-17 production. Additionally, the fetal TCRγ chain repertoire is altered, and peripheral Vg4 γδ T cells are predominantly IFNg-producing in HEB-deficient mice. These findings highlight HEB-dependent pathways for CD73+ and CD73- γδT17 cell development and provide mechanistic insights into the regulation of the γδT17 gene network by HEB. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: TCRg.

title: P14 and L50R Gene Abnormalities in Brain and Systemic Lymphomas
abstract: Primary malignant lymphoma of the brain and systemic lymphoma were analyzed for p14 and L50R gene abnormalities. Exon 1beta deletion of p14 was observed in four cases of brain lymphoma, with hemizygous deletion in five cases and no deletion in one. A missense mutation (L50R) was detected in one case with hemizygous deletion. Tumor samples showed no methylation of the p14 gene's 5'CpG island in cases without homozygous deletion. In contrast, systemic lymphoma cases had rare p14 gene abnormalities. Carcinogenesis in brain lymphoma was associated with frequent p14 gene inactivation, while systemic lymphoma showed infrequent p14 gene abnormalities.

title: A Novel Cause of Congenital Disorder of Glycosylation Ic
abstract: A young girl presented with Congenital disorder of glycosylation Ic (CDG-Ic) and a mild clinical phenotype. Genetic analysis revealed a de novo deletion (10-12Mb) [del(1)(p31.2p32.3)] and a mutation in the hALG-6 gene. The patient's cells showed accumulation of lipid-linked oligosaccharides with reduced glucose content. Sequencing identified a 338G>A mutation, but haplotype analysis indicated no paternal DNA markers in the ALG6 region. Microsatellite studies extended the abnormal region to 2.5Mb, confirming the deletion. No structural abnormalities were found in the father, supporting a de novo event. This case highlights the role of large DNA deletions in CDG-Ic and identifies the 338G>A mutation as a novel genetic variant. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: deletion ( 10 - 12Mb ); del(1)(p31.2p32.3 ); 338G > A.

title: Genetic Polymorphisms in COX-2 and Their Association with Prostate Cancer Risk
abstract: Variants in the COX-2 gene have been investigated for their potential role in prostate cancer susceptibility. COX-2 is critical in the conversion of arachidonic acid to prostaglandins, which are involved in inflammatory responses and pain signaling. Evidence from clinical and experimental studies highlights that COX-2 contributes to carcinogenesis and is overexpressed in prostate cancer tissues. A population-based case-control study analyzed 16 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) across the COX-2 gene, focusing on variants +3100 T/G and +8365 C/T. These SNPs were evaluated in 1,378 prostate cancer cases and 782 controls, revealing statistically significant differences in allele frequencies. The +3100 T/G and +8365 C/T variants were associated with reduced prostate cancer risk, as evidenced by odds ratios of 0.78 and 0.65, respectively. Haplotype analysis further identified a variant combination linked to decreased risk. This research underscores the role of inflammation in prostate carcinogenesis and demonstrates how genetic variations in COX-2 influence cancer susceptibility. Prostaglandins, generated through COX-2 activity, play a key role in maintaining inflammatory and pain pathways, while carcinogenesis is influenced by arachidonic acid metabolism. Inflammation and COX-2 expression are closely linked, with the +3100 T/G and +8365 C/T variants showing a negative correlation with prostate cancer development. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: + 8365 C/T; + 3100 T/G.

title: Alpha-lipoic acid mitigates mitochondrial damage and neurotoxicity in chemotherapy-induced neuropathy
abstract: Alpha-lipoic acid prevents mitochondrial damage and neurotoxicity in experimental chemotherapy neuropathy. The study explores whether alpha-lipoic acid has neuroprotective effects against chemotherapy-induced neurotoxicity, if mitochondrial damage is critical in the toxic neurodegenerative cascade, and if the neuroprotective effects of alpha-lipoic acid depend on mitochondrial protection. We used an in vitro model of chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy by exposing primary cultures of dorsal root ganglion (DRG) sensory neurons to paclitaxel and cisplatin, two common chemotherapeutic agents. This approach enabled the investigation of alpha-lipoic acid's efficacy in preventing axonal damage and apoptosis, as well as the function and ultrastructural morphology of mitochondria after exposure to toxic agents and alpha-lipoic acid. Our results show that both cisplatin and paclitaxel cause early mitochondrial impairment with loss of membrane potential and induction of autophagic vacuoles in neurons. Alpha-lipoic acid exerts neuroprotective effects against chemotherapy-induced neurotoxicity in sensory neurons: it rescues mitochondrial toxicity and induces the expression of frataxin, a key mitochondrial protein with antioxidant and chaperone properties. In conclusion, mitochondrial toxicity is an early common event in paclitaxel and cisplatin-induced neurotoxicity. Alpha-lipoic acid protects sensory neurons through its antioxidant and mitochondrial regulatory functions, possibly inducing frataxin expression. These findings suggest that alpha-lipoic acid may reduce the risk of developing peripheral nerve toxicity in patients undergoing chemotherapy and warrant further clinical trials to confirm these results.

title: Metformin's Role in Modulating Cardiac Function and Inflammatory Responses Post-Myocardial Infarction
abstract: Long-term administration of metformin inhibits toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) signaling and reduces left ventricular dysfunction following myocardial infarction. Acute treatment with metformin exhibits protective effects in myocardial infarction by suppressing inflammatory responses through activation of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK). In this study, the impact of chronic pre-treatment with metformin on cardiac dysfunction and TLR4 activities after myocardial infarction, along with its relationship to AMPK, was evaluated. Male Wistar rats were divided into five groups (n=6): control and groups received isoproterenol after chronic pre-treatment with 0, 25, 50, or 100 mg/kg of metformin twice daily for 14 days. Isoproterenol (100 mg/kg) was administered subcutaneously on days 13 and 14 to induce acute myocardial infarction. Isoproterenol alone decreased left ventricular systolic pressure and myocardial contractility, as measured by LVdp/dtmax and LVdp/dtmin. The left ventricular dysfunction was significantly lower in groups treated with 25 and 50 mg/kg of metformin. Metformin markedly reduced isoproterenol-induced increases in TLR4 mRNA, myeloid differentiation protein 88 (MyD88), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha), and interleukin 6 (IL-6) in heart tissues. Similar changes were observed in serum levels of TNF-alpha and IL-6. However, lower doses of 25 and 50 mg/kg were more effective than 100 mg/kg. Phosphorylated AMPK (p-AMPK) levels in the myocardium were significantly elevated by 25 mg/kg of metformin, slightly by 50 mg/kg, but not by 100 mg/kg. Chronic pre-treatment with metformin reduces post-myocardial infarction cardiac dysfunction and suppresses inflammatory responses, likely through inhibition of TLR4 activities. This mechanism offers a potential target for protecting infarcted myocardium.

title: High glucose alters podocyte energy metabolism in diabetic nephropathy
abstract: High glucose levels significantly alter human podocyte energy metabolism during differentiation and progression of diabetic nephropathy. Podocytes are critical in maintaining kidney function, yet their metabolic responses to high glucose remain poorly understood. Using a conditionally differentiating human podocyte model, we examined metabolic changes under normal and high glucose conditions. In 5 mM glucose, oxidative metabolism was activated through peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-g coactivator 1a (PGC-1a)-dependent mitochondrial biogenesis, accompanied by reduced glycolytic enzyme expression. However, in 20 mM glucose, oxidative phosphorylation was suppressed, leading to a glycolytic shift and lactic acidosis. Expression of key metabolic regulators, including AMPK, serine-threonine liver kinase B1, and PGC-1a, was altered by high glucose, as were their downstream pathways. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that myocyte-specific enhancer factor 2C (MEF2C) and myogenic factor 5 (MYF5) were downregulated, and their inhibition mimicked the glycolytic shift in high glucose. Reduced MEF2C, MYF5, and PGC-1a expression was also observed in kidney tissues from diabetic nephropathy patients. These findings demonstrate that high glucose induces MEF2C-MYF5-dependent metabolic dedifferentiation in podocytes, linking energy metabolism to diabetic nephropathy pathogenesis.

title: PRMT5's Role in Inflammation and Fibroblast-Like Synoviocyte Behavior in Rheumatoid Arthritis
abstract: The role of protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5) in inflammation and the migration of fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLSs) in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) was investigated. FLSs were isolated from synovial tissues (STs) of patients with RA and osteoarthritis (OA). An inhibitor of PRMT5, EPZ015666, and siRNA targeting PRMT5 were used to suppress its expression. Western blot and immunofluorescence were employed to assess PRMT5 levels, while enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) measured inflammatory factor excretion and gene expression. Migration and invasion were evaluated using Boyden chamber assays, and proliferation was analyzed via BrdU incorporation. Elevated PRMT5 was observed in STs and FLSs from RA patients. In RA FLSs, PRMT5 levels were upregulated by IL-1b and TNF-a stimulation. Inhibition of PRMT5 with EPZ015666 or siRNA reduced IL-6 and IL-8 production, as well as FLS proliferation. Additionally, PRMT5 inhibition decreased in vitro migration and invasion of RA FLSs. EPZ015666 also suppressed the phosphorylation of IkB kinaseb and IkBa, and the nuclear translocation of p65 and AKT in FLSs. PRMT5 regulated inflammatory factor production, cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in RA FLSs through the NF-kB and AKT pathways. These findings suggest that targeting PRMT5 may offer a promising therapeutic approach for preventing synovial inflammation and destruction in RA.

title: Metalloprotease-Disintegrin Promotes Cancer Stemness in Claudin-Low Breast Tumors
abstract: Metalloprotease-disintegrin is a key regulator of the stem cell-like phenotype in claudin-low breast tumors, where it interacts with EGF and CD24 to modulate cellular behavior. In estrogen receptor-negative tumors, Metalloprotease-disintegrin expression correlates with increased ALDH activity and CD44(high)/CD24(low) markers, which are associated with tumor initiation and progression. Batimastat, a metalloproteinase inhibitor, suppresses Metalloprotease-disintegrin activity, reducing its oncogenic effects. The Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) pathway is co-regulated with Metalloprotease-disintegrin, enhancing tumor aggressiveness. Tumors exhibiting high Metalloprotease-disintegrin levels show elevated claudin-low expression and resistance to therapeutic interventions. Additionally, Metalloprotease-disintegrin expression is inversely linked to batimastat treatment, highlighting its role in tumor survival. These findings underscore the importance of targeting Metalloprotease-disintegrin in claudin-low breast cancer progression.

title: Mutations in PQBP1 and BCOR Genes Linked to X-Linked Mental Retardation Syndromes
abstract: A two-base-pair deletion in the PQBP1 gene is associated with microphthalmia, microcephaly, and mental retardation. X-linked mental retardation is classified into syndromic (S-XLMR) and non-syndromic (NS-XLMR) forms, though overlapping features between these categories are increasingly observed. Here, we report two maternal cousins with an X-linked phenotype characterized by mental retardation, microphthalmia, choroid coloboma, microcephaly, renal hypoplasia, and spastic paraplegia. Linkage analysis identified the disease locus on the X chromosome between Xp11.4 and Xq12, encompassing the BCOR gene. A missense mutation in BCOR was previously linked to Lenz microphthalmia syndrome, which shares significant phenotypic overlap with the current cases. However, no BCOR mutation was detected in the affected individuals. Subsequent analysis of PQBP1 within the Xp11.23 interval revealed a 2-bp deletion, c.461_462delAG, that cosegregates with the disease. This mutation is also associated with Hamel cerebropalatocardiac syndrome, another S-XLMR variant. Haplotype studies suggest germline mosaicism for the deletion in the maternal grandmother. These findings demonstrate that PQBP1 mutations are linked to an S-XLMR phenotype involving microphthalmia, expanding the clinical spectrum of PQBP1-related disorders. Additionally, X-linked mental retardation is associated with microcephaly, choroid coloboma, and renal hypoplasia, while Hamel syndrome is connected to microphthalmia and mental retardation. BCOR is not directly related to spastic paraplegia, and PQBP1 is not associated with Hamel cerebropalatocardiac syndrome in this context.

title: Warfarin-Levofloxacin Interaction and Bleeding Risk: Clinical Observations
abstract: Warfarin, a widely prescribed oral anticoagulant, is commonly used for thromboembolic disease management. Levofloxacin, a fluoroquinolone antibiotic, is frequently administered for bacterial infections. While clinical trials have not demonstrated significant drug-drug interactions between warfarin and levofloxacin, case studies highlight a potential association between the two medications and increased bleeding risk. Three patients presented with severe bleeding events coinciding with concomitant use of warfarin and levofloxacin. Fluoroquinolone class agents, including levofloxacin, are not directly linked to bleeding pathophysiology, though their co-administration with anticoagulants warrants close monitoring. Bleeding remains an independent clinical concern requiring separate evaluation.

title: Efficacy of Prothrombin Complex Concentrate in Treating Warfarin-Associated Hemorrhage
abstract: Rapid reversal of anticoagulation significantly reduces hemorrhage volume in a mouse model of warfarin-associated intracerebral hemorrhage. Warfarin-associated intracerebral hemorrhage (W-ICH) is a severe form of stroke. Current treatment guidelines lack consensus on the optimal management of W-ICH. In this study, we evaluated whether rapid anticoagulant reversal using human prothrombin complex concentrate (PCC) could decrease hemorrhagic blood volume. Male CD-1 mice were administered warfarin (2 mg/kg over 24 hours), leading to a mean International Normalized Ratio of 3.5±0.9. First, we demonstrated that intravenous PCC effectively reversed anticoagulation in mice. Second, collagenase was stereotactically injected into the right striatum to induce hemorrhage. Forty-five minutes later, animals were randomly assigned to receive PCC (100 U/kg) or saline i.v. (n=12 per group). Twenty-four hours post-hemorrhage induction, hemorrhagic blood volume was measured using a photometric hemoglobin assay. PCC-treated animals showed a mean hemorrhagic volume of 6.5±3.1 microL, compared to 15.3±11.2 microL in saline controls (P=0.015). In the saline group, 45% of mice developed large hematomas (>15 microL), whereas no such lesions were observed in the PCC group. These findings suggest that PCC may be an effective acute treatment for W-ICH by reducing hemorrhagic blood volume. Further research is needed to confirm the therapeutic potential of this approach for human W-ICH.

title: FGFR4 Gly388Arg Polymorphism and Cancer Risk in Scottish Men
abstract: A single nucleotide polymorphism at position 388 of the FGFR4 amino-acid sequence results in the substitution of glycine (Gly) with arginine (Arg). This variation was analyzed in 399 prostate cancer patients, 150 BPH patients, and 294 healthy controls. DNA was extracted from blood samples and polymerase chain reaction was used to identify FGFR4 single nucleotide polymorphisms. No overall association was found between the Arg allele and increased prostate cancer risk. Subgroup analysis revealed a higher incidence of the heterozygous ArgGly genotype in cancer cases compared to the combined group of BPH and controls (P<0.05). However, the difference was statistically significant between cancer and BPH patients but not between cancer cases and community controls. The Gly388Arg polymorphism in FGFR4 is not associated with increased risk of prostate cancer in Scottish men. These findings contrast with previous studies conducted in the USA and Japan, which reported a significant association between this polymorphism and cancer risk.

title: A Novel Mutation in the Glucocorticoid Receptor Affects Ligand Binding and Coactivator Interaction
abstract: A novel point mutation in the helix 10 region of the human glucocorticoid receptor (GR) leads to generalized glucocorticoid resistance by altering the structure of the ligand-binding domain. This condition, characterized by partial insensitivity to glucocorticoids, is caused by mutations in the GR gene. In this case, a 2-year-old female patient presented with generalized seizures, hypoglycemia, and hypokalemia, along with hypertension and premature pubarche. Dexamethasone treatment effectively suppressed these symptoms. Genetic analysis revealed a heterozygous mutation (G-->A) at nucleotide position 2141 (exon 8) in the GR gene, resulting in the substitution of arginine by glutamine at amino acid position 714 in the ligand-binding domain. The mutant receptor showed impaired transactivation activity and reduced affinity for ligand. It also exhibited diminished binding to the p160 nuclear receptor coactivator. Structural analysis indicated that the arginine-to-glutamine substitution at position 714 caused conformational changes in the ligand-binding domain and the AF-2 transactivation surface, decreasing ligand and coactivator binding affinity. The mutation at position 714 plays a crucial role in maintaining the proper structure of the GR alpha ligand-binding domain and AF-2 surface. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: androgen; ( G-->A ) at nucleotide position 2141; arginine 714; mineralocorticoid; seizure.

title: Genetic Variants and Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Risk in Hispanic Women
abstract: The major histocompatibility complex (MHC) region on chromosome 6p21 is a key contributor to the genetic basis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). A study of 1,500 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the MHC region and the deletion of the C4A gene was conducted in a case-control study of Hispanic women (400 cases, 800 age-matched controls) nested within the Prospective Hispanic Women's Health Study. Genotyping of 1,500 ancestral informative markers was used to estimate European ancestry. The most strongly associated SNP with SLE was rs9271366 (odds ratio, OR = 1.65, p = 4.8 × 10(-5)) near the HLA-DRB1 gene. Conditional haplotype analysis revealed three additional SNPs, rs204890 (OR = 1.90, p = 8.7 × 10(-4)), rs2071349 (OR = 1.48, p = 6.3 × 10(-3)), and rs2844580 (OR = 1.35, p = 1.1 × 10(-3)), to be associated with SLE independent of rs9271366. In univariate analysis, the C4A deletion showed an OR of 1.25 (p = 0.09), but after adjustment for other SNPs, the OR was 0.98 (p = 0.99). A genotype score combining the four SNPs showed additive risk (OR = 1.72 per high-risk allele, p < 0.0001). The rs9271366 SNP was also linked to higher SLE risk in a prior Chinese GWAS. Two SNPs from a European ancestry study were confirmed here, indicating shared genetic risk factors between Hispanic and European populations. In summary, four independent signals in the MHC region were associated with SLE risk in Hispanic women.

title: Plasminogen Activator Inhibitor Type 1 Levels and 4G/5G Polymorphism in Obese Patients with Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease
abstract: Plasminogen activator inhibitor type 1 serum levels and 4G/5G gene polymorphism were investigated in morbidly obese patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease. The study aimed to assess the relationship between PAI-1 levels, 4G/5G polymorphism, and hepatic fibrogenesis in this population. A case-control design included 60 obese patients and 80 non-obese controls matched by age and sex. Anthropometric, metabolic, and biochemical parameters were measured, including PAI-1 concentrations and 4G/5G genotype analysis. Results revealed significantly higher triglycerides, hypertension, and diabetes prevalence in obese individuals compared to controls. PAI-1 levels were lower in obese patients (9.82 ± 4.51) than in non-obese subjects (13.74 ± 10.2; p < 0.05). No differences in 4G/5G genotype frequencies were observed between groups. Liver fibrosis was similarly prevalent in obese patients with and without hepatic fibrogenesis, with no correlation between PAI-1 levels and fibrosis severity. Obese individuals exhibited a positive correlation between triglycerides and obesity status, while no associations were found between PAI-1 levels or 4G/5G genotypes and liver fibrosis. The study highlights the independent role of obesity in metabolic disturbances without direct modulation of PAI-1-related fibrogenesis.

title: Aberrant Caveolin-1-Mediated Smad Signaling in Pulmonary Hypertension
abstract: A heterozygous caveolin-1 c.474delA mutation was identified in a family with heritable pulmonary hypertension (PAH). This frameshift mutation results in a caveolin-1 protein retaining all functional domains but altering the final 20 amino acids of the C-terminus. The study investigated how this mutation affects caveolin-1 function using patient-derived fibroblasts. Transmission electron microscopy revealed that fibroblasts with the mutation form typical caveolae. Expression of mutated caveolin-1 in caveolin-1-null mouse fibroblasts failed to induce caveolae formation due to retention of the mutated protein in the endoplasmic reticulum. However, coexpression of wild-type caveolin-1 with mutated caveolin-1 restored caveolae formation. Notably, fibroblasts with the mutation exhibited a twofold increase in proliferation rate, associated with hyperphosphorylation of Smad1/5/8. This mutation impaired the antiproliferative function of caveolin-1. Inhibition of type I TGFb receptors ALK1/2/3/6, which phosphorylate Smad1/5/8, reduced hyperproliferation in c.474delA fibroblasts. These findings highlight the critical role of the final 20 amino acids of caveolin-1 in modulating fibroblast proliferation through Smad signaling. The results suggest that elevated Smad signaling and fibroblast hyperproliferation contribute to the pathogenesis of PAH in patients with caveolin-1 c.474delA mutation. Furthermore, the association between pulmonary hypertension and caveolin-1-mediated signaling underscores the importance of this pathway in disease mechanisms. The adenine 474 deletion mutation (c.474delA) in caveolin-1 is linked to altered Smad signaling, emphasizing its role in the development of pulmonary hypertension. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: pulmonary arterial hypertension.

title: Genomic Instability in MLH1 and MSH2: Role of Alu Elements in Lynch Syndrome Pathogenesis
abstract: Lynch syndrome is associated with mutations in both MLH1 and MSH2 genes, which are critical for DNA mismatch repair. Recent studies have identified distinct patterns of chromosomal abnormalities in these genes among Lynch syndrome patients. Analysis of 12 genomic rearrangements revealed that MSH2 deletions predominantly involve Alu-mediated unequal recombination, while MLH1 deletions are primarily due to non-homologous recombination events. Notably, the distribution of breakpoints in MLH1 and MSH2 genes correlates with local Alu element density, suggesting a role for Alu sequences in shaping deletion patterns. These findings highlight the differential involvement of Alu elements in the genetic etiology of Lynch syndrome, with MSH2 showing a stronger association with Alu-mediated mechanisms compared to MLH1.

title: Genetic Associations in Schizophrenia: DISC1 and NDE1
abstract: A study of Finnish schizophrenia families identified a genetic link between the DISC1 risk allele and the disease, alongside a potential connection to NDE1. Previous research established a strong association between a specific DISC1 haplotype and schizophrenia, particularly in males. This study further explored the role of NDE1, which is biologically linked to DISC1, by analyzing genome-wide data from 443 markers. While most linkages lost significance after correction, a tag-haplotype of NDE1 showed a significant association with schizophrenia in females. These findings highlight the shared genetic pathways involving DISC1 and NDE1 in schizophrenia's etiology, supporting their roles in complex genetic mechanisms.

title: Identification of a Gain-of-Function Mutation in the Prolactin Receptor Linked to Benign Breast Tumors
abstract: A gain-of-function mutation in the prolactin receptor (PrlR) has been identified in patients with benign breast tumors. There is currently no known genetic disease associated with prolactin (Prl) or its receptor (PrlR) in humans. Given the critical role of this hormonal system in breast physiology, we hypothesized that genetic variants in Prl/PrlR genes might contribute to the development of breast diseases with high proliferative potential. Multiple fibroadenomas (MFA) are benign breast tumors that frequently occur in young women, particularly during puberty, when Prl exerts proliferative effects on breast tissue. In a prospective study involving 74 MFA patients and 170 control subjects, a heterozygous single nucleotide polymorphism in exon 6 of the PrlR gene was identified, encoding the Ile(146)-->Leu substitution in its extracellular domain. This substitution was sufficient to confer constitutive activity to the receptor variant (PrlR(I146L)), as demonstrated in three cell models (Ba/F3, HEK293, and MCF-7 cells) through Prl-independent PrlR tyrosine phosphorylation, STAT5 signaling activation, transcriptional activity toward a Prl-responsive reporter gene, and cell proliferation. Constitutive activity of PrlR(I146L) in a breast sample from a patient was confirmed by increased STAT5 signaling. This is the first description of a functional mutation in the PrlR associated with a human disease. The hallmarks of constitutive activity were reversed by a specific PrlR antagonist, suggesting potential therapeutic strategies for MFA or other conditions linked to this mutation. The association between MFA and the Ile(146)-->Leu substitution in PrlR highlights a novel genetic link to breast diseases. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: signal transducer and activator of transcription 5.

title: Reversible Inferior Colliculus Lesion in Metronidazole-Induced Encephalopathy: MRI Findings
abstract: Reversible inferior colliculus lesion in metronidazole-induced encephalopathy: magnetic resonance findings. Objective: This study presents reversible inferior colliculus lesions in metronidazole-induced encephalopathy, emphasizing the role of metronidazole-induced in the development of inferior colliculus lesion. Materials and Methods: From May 2006 to April 2008, 10 patients (6 men and 4 women) were diagnosed with metronidazole-induced encephalopathy (age range: 38-75 years). They had been treated with metronidazole (total dosage: 30-110 g; duration: 28 days to 3 months) for infection in various organs. Initial brain MRI included diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and fluid attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) sequences. Follow-up MRIs were performed on 6 patients after discontinuation of metronidazole. Findings: Initial MRIs showed high signal intensity on DWI and FLAIR at the dentate nucleus (10/10), inferior colliculus (7/10), corpus callosum (2/10), pons (2/10), and bilateral cerebral white matter (1/10). Lesions in the inferior colliculus resolved completely in all 6 follow-up cases, while one patient retained a corpus callosal lesion. Conclusions: Reversible inferior colliculus lesions are characteristic of metronidazole-induced encephalopathy, with metronidazole-induced showing a positive correlation with inferior colliculus lesion. Metronidazole-induced is associated with infection in a negative correlation, suggesting a complex relationship between the treatment and underlying condition.

title: Molecular Analysis of 46,XY DSD and Novel Mutations in the SRD5A2 Gene
abstract: This study investigated molecular etiologies of 46,XY DSD and identified a novel 8 nucleotide deletion in exon 1 of the SRD5A2 gene. Phenotypic manifestations of 46,XY DSD were evaluated in 29 patients, with a focus on mutations in the SRD5A2 and androgen receptor genes. PCR-SSCP analysis revealed aberrant migration in amplicons, leading to sequencing confirmation. Six patients from unrelated families were found to carry mutations in SRD5A2, including a compound heterozygous variant consisting of g.80_87delT CGCGAAG (p. A27fsX132) and p. R246Q. A separate case presented a heterozygous p. G196S mutation associated with isolated micropenis. Notably, no mutations were detected in the androgen receptor gene. The findings highlight the prevalence of p. R246Q in SRD5A2-related 46,XY DSD and document a novel deletion in the SRD5A2 gene linked to severe hypospadias.

title: Safety Profile of Capecitabine in Oncology: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Capecitabine has emerged as a critical treatment option for multiple malignancies, including colorectal , breast , pancreaticobiliary , gastric , renal cell and head and neck cancers. This review examines its pharmacological properties and safety considerations, emphasizing its role in patients with advanced age and renal and kidney disease. The drug's efficacy is supported by its use in combination therapies, though its association with certain malignancies remains a focus of clinical attention. Common adverse effects observed include diarrhea , nausea , vomiting , stomatitis and hand-foot syndrome, which are closely linked to its therapeutic application. Notably, 5-fluorouracil is not directly correlated with renal and kidney disease, yet both agents are employed in similar oncologic settings. The safety of capecitabine is further validated through its administration in populations with hepatic and renal dysfunctions, demonstrating a favorable risk-benefit ratio. Additionally, the relationship between 5-fluorouracil and colorectal , breast and head and neck cancers is not directly tied to adverse outcomes, though both compounds are used in cancer treatment regimens. The study underscores capecitabine's importance as an oral prodrug, offering improved convenience without compromising therapeutic effectiveness in diverse cancer types. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: tumors.

title: Temsirolimus and Its Therapeutic Effects in Mantle Cell Lymphoma
abstract: Temsirolimus has shown significant therapeutic potential in refractory mantle cell lymphoma (MCL). MCL is an aggressive form of B-cell non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, and patients often develop resistance to traditional chemotherapy, leading to poor prognoses. A recent case study demonstrated a 38% remission rate in patients with refractory MCL treated with temsirolimus, a mTOR inhibitor. In this case, a patient with refractory MCL experienced tumor regression within two months of temsirolimus treatment, achieving a progression-free survival of 10 months. Lymph node biopsies were conducted before and six months after therapy. Analysis of the biopsies revealed that temsirolimus inhibited tumor cell proliferation via cell cycle arrest without affecting the number of apoptotic tumor cells. Additionally, temsirolimus exhibited antiangiogenic properties, reducing tumor microvessel density and VEGF expression. Post-treatment, fibrotic areas consistent with post-necrotic tissue repair were observed. These findings indicate that temsirolimus reduces tumor burden through its cytostatic and antiangiogenic effects, which may explain its efficacy in refractory MCL resistant to conventional therapies. VEGF levels remained unchanged in post-necrotic tissue, and mTOR activity was not correlated with tumor progression in this case. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: B-cell non-Hodgkin 's lymphoma.

title: CYBA Polymorphism and Risk Factors in Coronary Artery Disease
