abstract: The -930A > G polymorphism of the CYBA gene is linked to premature coronary artery disease. A case-control study evaluated gene-risk factor interactions. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) play a role in atherosclerosis and coronary artery disease (CAD). NADPH oxidases are the primary source of ROS in vascular tissues. p22phox, a key component of vascular NADPH oxidases, is encoded by the CYBA gene. The -930A > G CYBA polymorphism (rs9932581:A > G) influences CYBA promoter activity and transcription. This study analyzed the association between the -930A > G polymorphism and CAD, as well as interactions with traditional risk factors. 480 participants were studied: 240 with premature CAD and 240 age- and sex-matched blood donors. Genotyping using the TaqMan SNP Assay revealed the -930 G allele as a risk factor for CAD (OR 2.03, 95% CI 1.21-3.44, P=0.007). A synergistic effect of the -930 G allele with overweight/obesity (BMI <25) and cigarette smoking was observed. The CAD risk for BMI <25 and the -930 G allele interaction was 160% higher than additive predictions. Overweight/obesity was a risk factor for CAD only in -930 G allele carriers (P<10(-10)) but not in AA homozygotes (P=1.00). In conclusion, the -930A > G CYBA polymorphism is associated with CAD in the Polish population. -930 G allele carriers are particularly vulnerable to obesity and tobacco exposure consequences.

title: GLUT4's Role in Overload-Induced Glucose Uptake and Muscle Hypertrophy in Mouse Skeletal Muscle
abstract: This study investigates the role of GLUT4 in overload-induced glucose uptake and hypertrophic growth in mouse skeletal muscle. While GLUT4 is essential for acute insulin- and contraction-induced glucose uptake, its involvement in chronic overload-induced processes remains unclear. To explore this, muscle overload was induced in mice by removing the synergist muscle. After five days, muscle weights and ex vivo [(3)H]-2-deoxy-d-glucose uptake were measured. Overload-induced glucose uptake and hypertrophy were not affected in GLUT4 knockout mice, indicating that GLUT4 is not required for these processes. To determine the transporter involved, chemical inhibitors were used. Cytochalasin B, a GLUT inhibitor, but not phloridzin, a sodium-dependent cotransporter inhibitor, blocked overload-induced uptake, suggesting GLUTs are responsible. Hexose competition experiments showed that d-fructose did not inhibit uptake, ruling out GLUT2, GLUT5, GLUT8, and GLUT12. Immunoblots revealed increased GLUT1, GLUT3, GLUT6, and GLUT10 protein levels. These findings indicate that GLUT4 is not necessary for overload-induced glucose uptake or hypertrophy, and other GLUTs may mediate this process.

title: Ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal esterase L1 (UCHL1) and its role in pediatric high-grade gliomas
abstract: Ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal esterase L1 (UCHL1) is associated with stem-like cancer cell functions in pediatric high-grade glioma. Pediatric high-grade gliomas represent 8-12% of all primary tumors of the nervous system in children. Five-year survival for these aggressive tumors is poor (15-35%), highlighting the need for improved therapeutic strategies. In this study, SF188 and SJ-GBM2 cell lines were used to investigate the function of UCHL1, a deubiquitinase dysregulated in multiple cancers, in pediatric gliomas. UCHL1 depletion in these glioma cells was linked to reduced cell proliferation and invasion, along with diminished growth in soft agar and sphere formation. A 70% decrease in Wnt signaling was observed using a TCF-dependent TOPflash reporter assay. Transcriptome analysis of UCHL1 knockdowns versus controls identified 306 differentially expressed genes (≥2-fold change; p < 0.05), including ACTA2, POSTN, LIF, FBXL7, FBXW11, GDF15, HEY2, IGLL5, ABCA4, AQP3, AQP4, CALB1, and ALK. Gene ontology analysis revealed enrichment in signal peptides, extracellular matrix, and secreted proteins. Pathways such as Clathrin-mediated Endocytosis Signaling, Virus Entry via Endocytic Pathways, and High Mobility Group-Box 1 (HMGB1) Signaling were significantly enriched. FGF2, IL1B, TNF, and PDGFB were identified as top upstream regulators. Aberrant UCHL1 expression in pediatric gliomas may promote cell invasion, transformation, and self-renewal by modulating Wnt/Beta catenin activity.

title: Mutations in N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) Transferase and X-Linked Intellectual Disability
abstract: Mutations in N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) transferase (OGT) are associated with X-linked intellectual disability (XLID). OGT plays a critical role in protein O-GlcNAcylation, a dynamic post-translational modification essential for cellular functions such as signaling and gene expression. Altered O-GlcNAcylation levels have been linked to developmental defects and neurodegeneration. In this study, two hemizygous mutations in OGT were identified in individuals with XLID and dysmorphic features: a missense mutation (p. Arg284Pro) and a splicing mutation (c.463-6T > G). Both mutations are located in the tetratricopeptide repeats of OGT, crucial for substrate recognition. Analysis of patient-derived fibroblasts revealed slightly reduced OGT protein levels and decreased O-GlcNAcase activity, though global O-GlcNAc levels remained stable. The c.463-6T > G mutation caused aberrant mRNA splicing without producing a stable truncated protein. Recombinant OGT with the p. Arg284Pro mutation showed reduced glycosylation activity and impaired processing of host cell factor 1, a gene associated with XLID. These findings suggest that OGT mutations may disrupt O-GlcNAc homeostasis and host cell factor 1 function, contributing to XLID pathology. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: N-acetylglucosamine ( O-GlcNAc ) transferase; c.463 - 6T > G.

title: Haplotype Analysis of Beta-Adrenergic Receptor Variants in Cardiovascular and Metabolic Disorders
abstract: The beta adrenergic receptor (beta-AR) is a G protein-coupled receptor activated by epinephrine and norepinephrine, playing a critical role in cardiovascular and metabolic disorders. This study investigates the functional diversity of beta-AR genes, including the ADRB1 (Arg389Gly, Gly49Ser), ADRB2 (Arg16Gly, Gln27Glu), and ADRB3 (Arg64Trp) variants, which have been linked to these disorders. By analyzing genetic markers across 96 US Caucasians and 96 African Americans, we identified haplotype blocks that capture most of the functional information from these genes. The results suggest that haplotype-based approaches can effectively uncover genetic associations, even when specific functional variants are not directly genotyped. This study highlights the importance of comprehensive marker panels in understanding the genetic basis of cardiovascular and metabolic disorders.

title: New Mutations and Genetic Variants in Brazilian Patients with Steroid 5alpha-Reductase Deficiency Type 2
abstract: This study investigates sequence abnormalities in the steroid 5alpha-reductase type 2 (steroid 5alpha-reductase deficiency type 2) gene among Brazilian patients with suspected deficiency. Polymerase chain reaction and automated sequencing were used to analyze DNA samples from 20 patients across 18 families. Eleven subjects exhibited homozygous single-base mutations, including G183S, R246W, del642 T, G196S, and 217_218insC, along with the A49 T variant in heterozygosis. Four patients were compound heterozygotes with Q126R/IVS3 + 1G > A, Q126R/del418 T, and Q126R/G158R. Three patients carried heterozygous substitutions: A207D, G196S, and R266W. The V89L polymorphism was found in heterozygosis with A207D and in a case with a normal gene sequence. The A49 T variant was detected in heterozygosis in another case without additional abnormalities. Four novel mutations were identified: del642 T, G158R, IVS3 + 1G > A, and 217_218insC. This is the first report of a single-nucleotide insertion in the coding sequence of the steroid 5alpha-reductase type 2 gene. The study highlights the prevalence of G183S among African-Brazilian patients and confirms the recurrence of known mutations.

title: Functional Analysis of SLCO1B1 Variants and Their Impact on Drug Transport
abstract: This study investigates the functional properties of SLCO1B1 variants, including SLCO1B1 * 5, SLCO1B1 * 15, and the novel haplotype SLCO1B1 * 15+C1007 G, through transient expression systems in HeLa and HEK293 cells. The research focuses on how these variants influence the transport of endogenous substrates and statins. Results demonstrate that cells expressing SLCO1B1 * 5, * 15, and * 15+C1007 G exhibit significantly reduced transport activities for pravastatin, atorvastatin, cerivastatin, and simvastatin compared to wild-type variants. Tritium-labeled estradiol-17beta-D-glucuronide and estrone-3-sulfate were used to assess transporter function, revealing no changes in Km values but decreased Vmax for statins. The 521T > C polymorphism in these variants is identified as a critical factor affecting transporter function. Additionally, estrone-3-sulfate is associated with the 15+C1007 G variant, while pravastatin is positively correlated with myopathy. These findings highlight the role of genetic polymorphisms in modulating drug transport and their clinical implications for statin therapy.

title: Nuclear Localization and Functional Role of ETV6 in Cancer Pathogenesis
abstract: ETV6, a member of the ETS family of transcription factors, plays a critical role in hematopoietic development and is frequently involved in chromosomal translocations associated with cancer. Recent studies have identified a nuclear localization signal (NLS) within the C-terminal domain of ETV6, which is essential for its function. Mutations in the region spanning amino acids 332-452 disrupt nuclear localization, leading to impaired transcriptional repression. Notably, the NLS activity of ETV6 is distinct from that of beta-galactosidase, a common enzymatic marker, and no direct functional interaction has been observed between these two proteins in cancer cells.

title: Genotyping of Chinese Patients with 17alpha-Hydroxylase Deficiency: Identification of Novel CYP17 Mutations
abstract: Genotyping of six Chinese patients with 17alpha-hydroxylase deficiency was conducted to identify mutations in the CYP17 gene. The study focused on congenital adrenal hyperplasia, a condition linked to CYP17 gene alterations. Patients were recruited from three families in Shandong Province, China, with diagnoses established through HPLC serum adrenal profiles. Three CYP17 mutations were identified, including V311fs, a deletion of 8-bp nucleotide (TTAAATGG) in exon 5, and Y329fs, a deletion-insertion mutation (TAC-->AA) at codon 329 in exon 6. Two homozygotes for Y329fs and one compound heterozygote for Y329fs and V311fs were found across three families. Additionally, two homozygous sisters with the D487_S488_F489 deletion were identified. The results confirm the diagnostic utility of HPLC for 17alpha-hydroxylase deficiency. The D487_S488_F489 deletion was previously reported in two Chinese families, with a third family identified in this study. The Y329fs mutation, along with other codon 329 mutations, suggests instability at this site. The recurrence of Y329fs may indicate a founder effect, while the mutations appear random overall. This study highlights the prevalence of CYP17 mutations in the Chinese population, with 17alpha-hydroxylase deficiency being more common than previously thought. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: ( TAC-->AA ) at codon 329; 8-bp nucleotide ( TTAAATGG ) deletion.

title: Genetic Variants in RNASEL and ABCE1 and Prostate Cancer Risk in Afro-Caribbean Populations
abstract: This study examined the relationship between RNASEL and ABCE1 genetic variations and prostate cancer risk in Afro-Caribbean populations. The researchers analyzed RNASEL, including the R462Q and D541E polymorphisms, and ABCE1, investigating a 20 bp insertion/deletion polymorphism 1,109 bp upstream of the initiation codon. A novel K294E variant was identified in a prostate cancer case. The A/G transition -1,071 bp from the transcriptional start site was also evaluated. No significant association was found between R462Q, D541E, or the 20 bp insertion/deletion and prostate cancer. However, a negative correlation was observed between RNASEL and ABCE1 in this population. Additionally, prostate cancer was associated with RNASEL, ABCE1, and K294E, while other genetic variants showed no relation to the disease.

title: Altered Expression of Inflammatory Mediators in Cystitis-Induced Bladder Dysfunction
abstract: Exaggerated production of inflammatory mediators in mice with vasoactive intestinal polypeptide knockout (VIP-/-) and cyclophosphamide (CYP)-induced cystitis. Vasoactive intestinal polypeptide (VIP) is an immunomodulatory neuropeptide involved in micturition pathways. VIP(-/-) mice show altered bladder function and neurochemical profiles in micturition pathways after CYP treatment. Given VIP's role as an anti-inflammatory mediator, we hypothesized that VIP(-/-) mice would exhibit increased inflammatory mediator expression following cystitis. A mouse inflammatory cytokine array was used to assess regulated transcripts in the urinary bladder of wild-type (WT) and VIP(-/-) mice with or without CYP-induced cystitis (150 mg/kg; i.p.; 48 h). Four comparisons were made: WT control vs. CYP treatment, VIP(-/-) control vs. CYP treatment, WT control vs. VIP(-/-) control, and WT with CYP vs. VIP(-/-) with CYP. Genes with >1.5-fold change and p < 0.05 for comparisons were analyzed. Several genes, including IL-1beta and CXCL1, were validated using enzyme-linked immunoassays. CYP treatment significantly increased CXCL1 and IL-1beta expression in the urinary bladder of WT and VIP(-/-) mice, but VIP(-/-) mice with CYP treatment showed significantly higher expression (4.2- to 13-fold) compared to WT. The data suggest that VIP(-/-) mice with bladder inflammation have elevated inflammatory mediators, which may contribute to bladder dysfunction and altered neurochemical expression in micturition pathways. Cystitis was associated with reduced levels of vasoactive intestinal polypeptide, while cyclophosphamide treatment was linked to increased CXCL1 expression. Cyclophosphamide was used in conjunction with vasoactive intestinal polypeptide treatment in the experimental protocol. Inflammatory mediators were significantly upregulated in both WT and VIP(-/-) mice with cystitis, but VIP(-/-) mice exhibited greater inflammatory responses. Bladder dysfunction was observed in VIP(-/-) mice with cystitis, and inflammatory mediators were correlated with the severity of bladder dysfunction.

title: Mechanisms and Implications of mToR Inhibition-Induced Proteinuria
abstract: mToR inhibitors have been linked to proteinuria, a condition characterized by excessive urinary protein excretion, in patients undergoing renal transplantation. Conversion from calcineurin inhibitors to mToR inhibitors, such as sirolimus, has been associated with increased proteinuria in individuals with chronic allograft nephropathy. Proteinuria is a critical factor affecting long-term graft survival, prompting extensive research into its pathogenesis and management. The role of sirolimus in causing proteinuria, as opposed to being a secondary effect of discontinuing calcineurin inhibitors, remains a topic of debate. Recent studies have noted high levels of proteinuria during sirolimus therapy in both islet transplantation and de novo sirolimus treatment. Podocyte damage and glomerulosclerosis have been observed in some patients receiving mToR inhibitors, though the exact molecular mechanisms are not yet fully understood. This review aims to explore the potential mechanisms and clinical significance of proteinuria induced by mToR inhibition.

title: A Case of Bernard-Soulier Syndrome Associated with a GPIbalpha Gene Deletion
abstract: A patient with Bernard-Soulier Syndrome was found to have a deletion in the GPIbalpha gene, resulting in a lack of GPIbalpha and no bleeding. Thrombocytopenia was observed in the patient's parents, while siblings exhibited normal platelet counts. The deletion (TGAG) in the GPIbalpha gene is positively correlated with the development of Bernard-Soulier Syndrome. Ristocetin agglutination was absent in the patient, indicating no GPIbalpha on the platelet surface. The absence of GPIbalpha is negatively correlated with the presence of Bernard-Soulier Syndrome. Genetic analysis revealed a homozygous four-base-pair deletion (TGAG) leading to a premature stop codon, confirming the link between the deletion and the syndrome. The patient's platelet count was 30 x 10(9)/L, with giant platelets detected in blood smears. No spontaneous bleeding was reported, aligning with the clinical features of the condition. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: deletion ( TGAG ).

title: Identification of Novel Mutations in the GNPTG Gene in Patients with Mucolipidosis III Gamma
abstract: A study was conducted to identify and characterize six novel mutations in the UDP-N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphotransferase gamma subunit (GNPTG) gene among patients diagnosed with mucolipidosis III gamma. Mucolipidosis type III (MLIII) is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by impaired lysosomal enzyme function. In a cohort of 10 patients from seven families exhibiting clinical and enzymatic features of MLIII, six distinct GNPTG mutations were identified. These included missense (p. T286 M), nonsense (p. W111X), and a transition in the AG-dinucleotide of intron 8 (c.610 - 2A > G). Three microdeletions were also detected, with two located within the coding region (c.611delG and c.640_667del28) and one spanning intron 8 (c.609 + 28_610 - 16del). RT-PCR analysis revealed that the c.610 - 2A > G mutation altered splicing, producing aberrant transcripts such as p. G204_K247del or p. G204VfsX28. Analysis of the c.609 + 28_610 - 16del deletion in a homozygous patient showed no GNPTG RNA transcripts. Incubation of fibroblasts with anisomycin, a protein synthesis inhibitor, detected a 43-bp intron 8 fragment, suggesting nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD). Quantitative PCR and western blot analysis confirmed that the homozygous microdeletion p. G204VfsX17 triggered NMD, leading to the failure to synthesize GNPTG protein. Sequence analysis of the deletion breakpoints revealed repetitive DNA sequences, consistent with replication slippage as the mutational mechanism. These findings highlight the role of local DNA sequence properties in the mutational spectrum of the GNPTG gene, which is strongly associated with Mucolipidosis type III and its associated genetic variants. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: 33-bp genomic deletion.

title: Evaluating the Impact of Risperidone and Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors on Bone Density and Fracture Risk in Adolescents
abstract: A cross-sectional study was conducted to assess the relationship between risperidone and selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) with bone mineral density (BMD) and fracture incidence in pediatric patients. The objective was to investigate how risperidone-induced hyperprolactinemia affects trabecular BMD in children and adolescents. Medically healthy males aged 7-17 years, naturally treated with risperidone, were recruited through child psychiatry outpatient clinics from November 2005 to June 2007. Anthropometric measurements and laboratory tests were performed. Clinical diagnoses were based on chart reviews, and developmental history was obtained from medical records. Volumetric BMD of the ultradistal radius was measured using peripheral quantitative computed tomography, while areal BMD of the lumbar spine was estimated via dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry. Results showed hyperprolactinemia in 49% of 83 boys. Serum testosterone levels increased with pubertal status but were not affected by hyperprolactinemia. Bone mineral content and BMD increased with sexual maturity. After adjusting for sexual development and height/BMI z scores, serum prolactin was negatively associated with trabecular BMD at the ultradistal radius. Treatment with SSRIs was linked to lower BMD in the radius and lumbar spine. These findings were more pronounced in non-Hispanic white patients. Of 13 documented fractures, three occurred after starting risperidone and SSRIs, with none in patients without hyperprolactinemia. This study is the first to link risperidone-induced hyperprolactinemia and SSRI treatment to reduced BMD in children and adolescents.

title: Genetic Analysis of Classic Galactosemia and Associated Mutations
abstract: Classic galactosemia is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by impaired galactose metabolism, typically presenting in infants after exposure to lactose-containing diets. Genetic studies reveal that mutations in the GALT gene are responsible for the condition, with various pathogenic variants contributing to disease manifestation. A specific 5.5 kb deletion in the GALT gene has been identified as a significant mutation, showing a notable carrier frequency in Ashkenazi Jewish populations. This research aimed to quantify the prevalence of this deletion in the AJ population. Using an advanced genetic screening technique, DNA samples from 760 anonymous AJ individuals were analyzed, identifying six carriers of the GALT deletion mutation. The carrier rate was determined to be 0.79%, or 1 in 127. The study highlights the importance of early detection through genetic testing, which can inform prenatal counseling and reduce the burden of late-onset complications such as ovarian failure and neurological deficits associated with Classic galactosemia. Lactose avoidance remains a critical dietary intervention, yet long-term management requires addressing the diverse clinical manifestations of the disease.

title: Long-term oral galactose treatment ameliorates cognitive deficits in a rat model of Alzheimer's disease
abstract: Prolonged oral administration of galactose mitigates cognitive deficits in male Wistar rats exposed to streptozotocin via intracerebroventricular injection. Research indicates that dementia associated with sporadic Alzheimer's disease is linked to impaired insulin-receptor function, leading to reduced glucose transport through GLUT4 and diminished glucose metabolism in brain cells. Galactose, a C-4-epimer of glucose, is transported into the brain by insulin-independent GLUT3, where it may be metabolized to glucose through the Leloir pathway. Parenteral galactose injections induce memory deterioration in rodents, but oral administration has not been extensively tested for cognitive effects. This study evaluated the impact of continuous oral galactose (200 mg/kg/day) on cognitive deficits in a streptozotocin-induced rat model of Alzheimer's disease, assessed via Morris Water Maze and Passive Avoidance tests. One month of oral galactose treatment, initiated post-STZ administration, effectively prevented cognitive deficits. The beneficial effects were independent of age and dose (100-300 mg/kg/day). Galactose levels in blood increased, while cerebrospinal fluid concentrations were lower after oral compared to parenteral administration. This suggests oral galactose may enhance learning and memory, potentially beneficial for cognitive deficits linked to glucose hypometabolism in Alzheimer's disease. Alzheimer's disease is associated with insulin-receptor dysfunction, and galactose administration inversely correlates with glucose levels in the brain. Streptozotocin is positively correlated with cognitive deficits, while glucose is negatively correlated with glucose hypometabolism. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: Alzheimer 's disease.

title: A Novel CACNA1S Mutation Linked to Hypokalemic Periodic Paralysis and Autosomal Dominant Disorder
abstract: A novel mutation in the CACNA1S gene, V876E, is associated with hypokalemic periodic paralysis (hypokalemic periodic paralysis) in an autosomal dominant disorder. This condition is characterized by episodes of muscle weakness and a decrease in serum potassium levels. The CACNA1S gene encodes the skeletal muscle calcium channel alpha-subunit, which plays a critical role in cellular function. In this study, a four-generation family with hypokalemic periodic paralysis was analyzed, revealing the presence of the V876E mutation in all affected individuals but not in unaffected family members or 160 control subjects. Clinical observations indicate that the V876E mutation is linked to severe outcomes, including early onset, complete penetrance, and a high risk of death. The findings highlight the importance of the CACNA1S gene in the pathogenesis of hypokalemic periodic paralysis and expand the known spectrum of mutations associated with this condition.

title: Genetic Variants in DRD4 Associated with Schizophrenia, Depression, and Heroin Dependence
abstract: A study examined the relationship between polymorphisms in the DRD4 gene promoter region and schizophrenia, depression, and heroin addiction. Researchers analyzed 300 individuals with schizophrenia, 150 with depression, 280 with heroin addiction, and 300 healthy controls. Genotyping of DRD4 promoter variants (-120 bp duplication, -616C/G, and -521C/T) was performed using PCR-based methods. Results showed significant associations between the -120 bp duplication and schizophrenia (p=0.012), and weak associations with paranoid schizophrenia (p=0.031). The -521C/T variant demonstrated a strong link to heroin dependence (p=0.0004). These findings support the role of DRD4 in schizophrenia and the -521C/T polymorphism in heroin addiction. No significant correlations were observed between -1240 L/S and the studied conditions, while -616C/G showed no association with any of the phenotypes.

title: Genetic Variants and HIV-1 Evolution: A Hierarchical Phylogenetic Analysis
abstract: The role of C-C chemokine receptor type 5 (CCR5) genetic variants, particularly CCR5delta32, in shaping HIV-1 intrahost evolutionary trajectories remains under investigation. This study employs hierarchical phylogenetic models (HPMs) to evaluate how HIV-1-infected status and disease progression influence viral dynamics. By analyzing gp120 envelope sequences from clonal HIV-1 variants isolated across multiple time points in HIV-1-infected individuals, we explore the interplay between CCR5delta32 genotype and infection outcomes. Patients were stratified based on the presence of CCR5 wt/DD32 genotype and clinical progression, creating a two-way design to assess evolutionary patterns. While HPMs provide more precise estimates of substitution rates and d(N)/d(S) ratios compared to individual patient analyses, no significant differences in d(N)/d(S) were observed between groups. Association between substitution rates and disease progression was noted, but the role of CCR5 genotype remained inconclusive. AIDS development was linked to reduced viral replication rather than distinct selection pressures on amino acid sequences. Infection status and CCR5delta32 genotype were examined as independent factors, with no direct correlation identified between AIDS and CCR5delta32. The study highlights the importance of genetic background in modulating HIV-1 evolutionary dynamics without implying direct associations between these entities.

title: Late-onset scleroderma renal crisis associated with tacrolimus and corticosteroid use in systemic sclerosis
abstract: Scleroderma renal crisis (SRC) is a rare but severe complication of systemic sclerosis (SSc) that may require renal replacement therapy. This case report describes a patient with SRC induced by tacrolimus and corticosteroid therapy. Moderate to high-dose corticosteroid use is recognized as a major risk factor for SRC, while tacrolimus has been linked to increased susceptibility to SRC in SSc patients. Additionally, cyclosporine has been associated with thrombotic microangiopathy in SSc. The patient's condition highlights the risk of tacrolimus in SSc, particularly when combined with corticosteroids. Thrombotic microangiopathy was observed as a secondary complication in this case, though no direct association was found between cyclosporine and the patient's clinical course. Systemic sclerosis remains a significant comorbidity in this context, with no direct pharmacologic interaction identified between prednisolone and corticosteroid in this scenario.

title: TIPE2 Suppresses Lung Cancer Progression by Enhancing Apoptosis through Apoptotic Pathway Modulation
abstract: TIPE2 expression was observed to be significantly reduced in small cell lung cancer, lung squamous cancer, and lung adenocarcinoma tissues compared to adjacent non-tumor tissues. Overexpression of TIPE2 in lung cancer cell lines inhibited tumor growth in vitro and suppressed tumor formation in vivo. Flow cytometry analysis revealed that TIPE2 overexpression enhanced apoptosis by upregulating caspase-3, caspase-9, and Bax while downregulating Bcl-2. Immunohistochemical data corroborated these findings in mouse models. TIPE2 modulated signaling pathways by inhibiting Akt phosphorylation and promoting P38 phosphorylation, with no significant effects on IkBa or ERK pathways. These results suggest that TIPE2 promotes apoptosis in lung cancer cells through its effects on caspase-3, caspase-9, Bax, and Bcl-2, indicating its potential as a therapeutic target in lung cancer.

title: Metabolic Symbiosis in Tumor Cells Under Angiogenesis Inhibition
abstract: Therapeutic blockade of tumor angiogenesis through VEGF inhibition leads to transient efficacy in certain cancers, limited by adaptive resistance mechanisms. In a mouse model, angiogenesis inhibitors induce reorganization of cancer cells around residual blood vessels. Hypoxic regions express glucose and lactate transporters GLUT1 and MCT4, reflecting HIF1a-dependent glycolytic activity. Proximal cells near vessels utilize MCT1 for lactate transport and p-S6, indicating mTOR signaling. Normoxic cells import lactate, which enhances mTOR signaling via glutamine metabolism. This metabolic symbiosis allows hypoxic cells to take up glucose and release lactate, while normoxic cells catabolize lactate. mTOR inhibition disrupts this balance, leading to upregulation of GLUT2. The interplay between tumor cells, VEGF, and mTOR signaling highlights the complexity of metabolic adaptation in cancer.

title: Metallothionein-1 and NRF2 in Sorafenib-Induced Oxidative Stress in Tumors
abstract: Metallothionein-1 (MT1) plays a critical role in modulating redox homeostasis in cancer cells exposed to sorafenib. Sorafenib, a multi-kinase inhibitor, has been shown to induce oxidative stress and necrosis in various tumor types, including hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study investigates the molecular mechanisms underlying sorafenib's effects on tumor cells, focusing on the interplay between MT1 and the transcription factor NRF2. Our findings reveal that sorafenib significantly upregulates MT1 expression in HCC cell lines, an effect mediated through the NRF2 pathway. In clinical samples, MT1 levels correlate with tumor progression, while NRF2 activity is associated with resistance to sorafenib. Notably, sorafenib treatment is linked to reduced overall survival in HCC patients, highlighting the negative correlation between the drug and patient outcomes. These results suggest that MT1 and NRF2 are key regulators of sorafenib's impact on tumor biology, with MT1 serving as a potential biomarker for therapeutic response. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: tumours.

title: FGFR1 and NTRK3 Alterations in Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors
abstract: FGFR1 and NTRK3 actionable alterations are prevalent in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST). Background: Approximately 10-15% of adult and most pediatric GIST lack mutations in KIT, PDGFRA, SDHx, or RAS pathway components (KRAS, BRAF, NF1). Identifying additional mutated genes in this subset can guide therapeutic strategies. Methods: Comprehensive genomic profiling of over 300 cancer-related genes was performed in 186 GISTs. Results: Twenty-four GISTs showed no alterations in canonical pathways, including 12 without SDHx changes. These cases were predominantly adult (96%), with a 46% nodal metastasis rate. Mutations in ARID1B, ATR, FGFR1, LTK, SUFU, PARK2, and ZNF217 were common. Two tumors harbored FGFR1 fusions (FGFR1-HOOK3, FGFR1-TACC1), and one had an ETV6-NTRK3 fusion responsive to TRK inhibition. In an independent cohort, five GISTs lacked canonical pathway mutations, including two with FGFR1-TACC1 and ETV6-NTRK3 fusions. Conclusions: These GISTs occur in younger patients, frequently metastasize, and exhibit genomic alterations, including FGFR1 and NTRK3 fusions. Routine testing for these translocations may benefit this subset, enabling personalized treatment approaches. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: nodal metastases.

title: Genetic and Pathological Features of Cerebellar Degeneration and Related Disorders
abstract: Autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia (ADCA) is a neurodegenerative disorder linked to a single-nucleotide substitution in the 5' untranslated region of the gene encoding a protein with spectrin repeat and Rho guanine-nucleotide exchange-factor domains. This condition, which includes autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia (ADCA) and degenerative ataxia, is associated with progressive cerebellar degeneration and sensorineural hearing impairment. Positional cloning identified a gene, DKFZP434I216, which is strongly linked to ADCA and shows a heterozygous C-->T substitution 16 nucleotides upstream of its translation initiation site. The protein product, puratrophin-1, is normally expressed in various cells, including cochlear hair cells, but aggregates in Purkinje cells of affected individuals. These aggregates are accompanied by the accumulation of Golgi-apparatus membrane proteins and spectrin. The study highlights the role of the 5' untranslated region in disease gene identification and suggests that mutations in this region may lead to protein misfolding and aggregation. Additionally, Rho GTPases and actin are implicated in the pathogenesis of cerebellar degeneration, with the Rho guanine-nucleotide exchange-factor playing a key role in intracellular signaling and actin dynamics. The findings also indicate a potential association between neurodegenerative disorders and the Rho GTPases, as well as between cerebellar degeneration and the Rho guanine-nucleotide exchange-factor.

title: Clinical Features of OPHN1-Related Disorders
abstract: Characterization of clinical features associated with OPHN1 mutations through analysis of four families. Recent studies indicate that OPHN1 mutations underlie a syndromic form of mental retardation rather than a non-specific disorder. Posterior fossa abnormalities with cerebellar hypoplasia have been consistently observed in male patients. This report presents a new family with X-linked mental retardation caused by OPHN1 mutation, along with additional data from two previously described families regarding facial and psychological traits in affected males and carrier females. Our findings confirm cerebellar hypoplasia as a defining feature of this condition. Affected males exhibit facial characteristics that aid in diagnostic identification. Most carrier females display mild mental retardation and subtle facial anomalies.

title: Expanded Mutation Spectrum of PYGM in a Southern Italian Cohort
abstract: This study investigates the mutational landscape of the PYGM gene in 72 individuals from southern Italy diagnosed with McArdle disease, a form of glycogen storage disease type V. Deficiency of the muscle-specific glycogen phosphorylase isozyme underlies the clinical manifestations of exercise intolerance, muscle cramps, and recurrent myoglobinuria. Analysis revealed 32 distinct mutations, including 21 previously unreported variants. Key findings include: eight missense changes (c.475G>A, c.689C>G, c.1094C>T, c.1151C>A, c.1182C>T, c.1471C>T, c.2444A>C, c.2477G>C), two nonsense substitutions (c.1475G>A, c.1627A>T), five splice site variants (c.855+1G>C, c.1092+1G>A, c.1093-1G>T, c.1239+1G>A, c.2380+1G>A), and four deletions (c.715_717delGTC, c.304delA, c.1970_2177del, c.2113_2114delGG). While no direct correlation was observed between mutation type and clinical severity, the p.R50X variant accounted for 45% of alleles, highlighting its prevalence. Additionally, glycogen metabolism disruptions were associated with autosomal recessive disorder characteristics, underscoring the genetic heterogeneity of this condition. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: c.475G > A; c.1151C > A; p. N102DfsX4; p. V657_G726; p. P230R; c.2444A > C; c.1471C > T; p. W826S; c.1475G > A; c.1627A > T; c.1239 + 1G > A; p. A384D; c.2477G > C; p. G705RfsX16; p. R50X; p. V239del; c.855 + 1G > C; c.1094C > T; c.2380 + 1G > A; c.1092 + 1G > A; c.689C > G; c. 1093 - 1G > T; p. A365E; p. K543X; p. D815A; c.1182C > T ,; p. W492X.

title: Genetic Variants in Congenital Heart Disease: Association with Specific Phenotypes
abstract: GATA4 mutations were analyzed in 486 patients with congenital heart disease (CHD) to explore their role in disease manifestation. Germline mutations across the GATA4 gene were identified using DHPLC and sequencing, revealing nine distinct variants, including a small deletion (46delS), two insertions (118 - 119insA and 125 - 126insAA), and six non-synonymous changes (A6V, P163S, E359 K, P407Q, S429 T, and A442V). These mutations were detected in 12 patients, with nine having ventricular septal defect (VSD), two presenting Tetralogy of Fallot, and one exhibiting endocardial cushion defect. Notably, the c.1146 + 25insA insertion was found in five VSD patients but absent in 486 healthy controls. Additionally, the P407Q mutation was present in two family members with VSD, suggesting a possible hereditary component. However, no significant associations were observed between GATA4 and 118 - 119insA, or between GATA4 and 125 - 126insAA. The study highlights the prevalence of GATA4 variants in CHD and their potential correlation with specific phenotypes, such as VSD and Tetralogy of Fallot.

title: Serum- and glucocorticoid-inducible kinase 1 in doxorubicin-induced nephrotic syndrome
abstract: Serum- and glucocorticoid-inducible kinase 1 (SGK1) plays a critical role in doxorubicin-induced nephrotic syndrome. Doxorubicin treatment led to epithelial sodium channel (ENaC)-dependent volume retention and renal fibrosis in gene-targeted mice. The aldosterone-sensitive SGK1 was shown to regulate ENaC activity and mediate fibrosis following mineralocorticoid and salt excess. This study investigated SGK1's involvement in volume retention and fibrosis during nephrotic syndrome. Doxorubicin (15 µg/g body wt) was administered to sgk1(-/-) and sgk1(+/+) mice. Both genotypes developed severe nephrotic syndrome with proteinuria, lipidemia, hypoalbuminemia, and ascites. Plasma aldosterone levels increased in both groups, with higher SGK1 protein expression in sgk1(+/+) mice. Urinary sodium excretion was significantly lower in sgk1(+/+) mice (15 ± 5 µmol/mg crea) compared to sgk1(-/-) mice (35 ± 5 µmol/mg crea), correlating with greater weight gain in sgk1(+/+) mice (+6.6 ± 0.7 g vs. +4.1 ± 0.8 g). Serum urea concentrations rose faster in sgk1(-/-) mice, leading to uremia and reduced survival (29 vs. 40 days). These findings indicate that SGK1 deficiency blunts volume retention but does not prevent fibrosis in experimental nephrotic syndrome. The association between mineralocorticoid and sodium levels with SGK1 expression was inversely correlated, while doxorubicin-induced conditions were positively correlated with nephropathy and fibrosis.

title: Antithrombotic Therapy, Cerebral Microbleeds, and Intracerebral Hemorrhage: A Systematic Review of Clinical Data
abstract: Antithrombotic therapy, cerebral microbleeds, and intracerebral hemorrhage have been investigated in a comprehensive analysis of clinical data. Background: Cerebral microbleeds (MB) are potential risk factors for intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), but their association with antithrombotic drug use remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the presence of MB in different patient groups, including those with ICH, ischemic stroke (IS)/transient ischemic attack (TIA), and ischemic events. Methods: A systematic review of published and unpublished data from cohorts with stroke or TIA was conducted to compare MB frequency between antithrombotic users and non-users, as well as between ICH and ischemic events. The analysis also assessed the risk of ICH in antithrombotic users with MB. Results: In a pooled analysis of 1460 ICH cases and 3817 IS/TIA events, MB were more frequent in ICH compared to IS/TIA, with the risk increasing in warfarin users. Warfarin users showed a higher prevalence of MB compared to non-users with ICH, while no significant difference was observed in IS/TIA. The presence of MB at baseline was linked to a significantly elevated risk of subsequent ICH in antithrombotic users. Conclusions: The association between warfarin use and cerebral microbleeds suggests a heightened risk of warfarin-related ICH, emphasizing the need for further prospective studies.

title: Genetic Polymorphisms and Neuroinflammation in Alzheimer 's Disease
abstract: The -1021C/T polymorphism of dopamine b-hydroxylase (dopamine b-hydroxylase -1021C/T) is linked to Alzheimer 's disease (Alzheimer 's disease) in a genome-wide association study. Background: Reduced noradrenergic activity in the locus coeruleus is a key factor in Alzheimer 's disease. Dopamine b-hydroxylase catalyzes the conversion of dopamine to noradrenaline. Studies have identified interactions between the low-activity -1021 T allele (rs1611115) of dopamine b-hydroxylase and variants in pro-inflammatory cytokine genes, including IL1A and IL6, which may influence Alzheimer 's disease risk. We investigated the association of the dopamine b-hydroxylase -1021 T allele and these interactions in a cohort of 1757 Alzheimer 's disease cases and 6294 elderly controls. Methods: Genotyping was performed for eight SNPs in DBH, IL1A, and IL6. Logistic regression models and synergy factor analysis were used to assess interactions and associations with Alzheimer 's disease. Results: The -1021 T allele showed a positive correlation with Alzheimer 's disease, with an odds ratio of 1.2 (95% CI: 1.06-1.4, p=0.005). This was more pronounced in men under 75 years old. An interaction between the -1021 T allele and the -889TT genotype (rs1800587) of IL1A was observed, with a synergy factor of 1.9 (1.2-3.1, p=0.005). These findings were consistent across North Europe and North Spain. Conclusions: Previous evidence highlights the role of noradrenaline in brain inflammation. The -1021 T allele may disrupt inflammatory regulation, contributing to Alzheimer 's disease onset. We propose that misregulation of inflammation is the primary mechanism underlying these associations.

title: Genetic Variations in Immune Response and Oxidative Stress Genes and Prostate Cancer Recurrence
abstract: This study investigates the association between genetic polymorphisms in immune response genes, oxidative stress pathways, and their impact on prostate cancer recurrence. By analyzing variations in genes such as IL8, TNF, GPX1, NOS3, GSTP1, rs1800872, reactive oxygen species, IL6, IL1B, TLR4, SOD3, rs1800896, GSR, CRP, prostate cancer, IL10, SOD2, IL1RN, hOGG1, NOS2, MPO, and SOD1, we explore their roles in disease progression. Using a nested case-control design with paraffin-embedded tissue samples, we genotyped key SNPs and applied conditional logistic regression to assess their relationship with recurrence. Results revealed significant associations between IL10 rs1800872 and rs1800896, CRP, GSTP1, and IL1B, highlighting their influence on recurrence risk. These findings underscore the importance of genetic variations in immune and oxidative pathways in prostate cancer prognosis.

title: Mad2 Overexpression and Oncogene Co-Expression in Breast Cancer Progression
abstract: Overexpression of Mad2 in combination with Kras(G12D or Her2 in mammary glands leads to mitotic checkpoint activation and delayed tumor onset. Malignancies are associated with Kras(G12D and Her2, while Chromosome Instability is positively correlated with Mad2 levels. Despite this, Mad2-positive tumors in Breast Cancer patients exhibit increased karyotype complexity and persistent subclones that outgrow oncogene-dependent cells. Chromosome Instability is also linked to Mad2 expression, highlighting its role in tumor progression. Breast Cancer is associated with Mad2 expression, underscoring its significance in oncogenic pathways.

title: Analysis of Serum Cytokines and Single-Nucleotide Polymorphisms in Erysipelas Patients
abstract: This study examines the relationship between serum cytokine levels and single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in genes associated with erysipelas. Researchers analyzed 71 erysipelas patients and 55 age-matched controls to investigate the interactions between SNPs in SOD1, SOD2, and CAT with the disease's predisposition and cytokine profiles. Female patients exhibited a higher risk of erysipelas, while male patients showed a tendency for facial localization. SNPs such as SOD1 G7958A, SOD2 T2734C, and CAT C262 were linked to infection localization and severity. The T allele of SOD2 T2734C was associated with bullous erysipelas, while the C allele correlated with erythematous forms. G and A alleles of SOD1 G7958A were linked to lower limb and upper body involvement, respectively. Serum cytokines including IL-1beta, CCL11, IL-2Ralpha, CXCL9, TRAIL, PDGF-BB, and CCL4 were associated with symptom manifestation, whereas IL-6, IL-9, IL-10, IL-13, IL-15, IL-17, G-CSF, and VEGF were linked to disease recurrence. Variants of IL-1beta, IL-7, IL-8, IL-17, CCL5, and HGF were connected to the SOD2 T2734C SNP, and variations in PDGF-BB and CCL2 were associated with the CAT C262 T SNP. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: streptococcus infection; G7958; T2734.

title: Genetic Polymorphisms and Hemoglobin Profiles in Thalassemia Patients
abstract: A Ag-globin G->A gene variant is linked to b(0)39 thalassemia globin gene and elevated fetal hemoglobin levels. Background: Enhanced g-globin gene expression and high fetal hemoglobin (HbF) production in b-thalassemia patients are recognized as factors contributing to milder clinical outcomes. Recent research has focused on identifying HbF-associated polymorphisms, such as XmnI, BCL11A, and MYB variants, to better predict transfusion needs and responses to HbF inducers like hydroxyurea. Methods: Ag-globin gene sequencing was conducted on genomic DNA from 75 b-thalassemia patients, including 31 b(0)39/b(0)39, 33 b(0)39/b(+)IVSI-110, 9 b(+)IVSI-110/b(+)IVSI-110, one b(0)IVSI-1/b(+)IVSI-6, and one b(0)39/b(+)IVSI-6. Results: The rs368698783 polymorphism was detected in the 5'UTR region of the Ag-globin gene in b-thalassemia patients, affecting the LYAR (human homologue of mouse Ly-1 antibody reactive clone) binding site 5'-GGTTAT-3'. This Ag(+25 G->A) polymorphism is associated with the Gg-globin-XmnI polymorphism and both are linked to the b(0)39-globin gene, but not the b(+)IVSI-110-globin gene. The Ag(+25 G->A) and Gg-globin-XmnI polymorphisms are associated with high HbF in erythroid precursor cells from b(0)39/b(0)39 patients. Conclusions: We propose that the Gg-globin-XmnI/Ag-globin-(G->A) genotype is frequently linked with b(0)-thalassemia mutations but not b(+)-thalassemia mutations, and this combination may have been selected in the population due to its functional association with high HbF.

title: Warfarin Use in Elderly Patients with Atrial Fibrillation: Hemorrhage and Stroke Outcomes
abstract: This study examines the relationship between warfarin therapy and major hemorrhage or stroke in elderly patients with atrial fibrillation. Among 235 individuals aged 76 and older with atrial fibrillation on warfarin, 530 years of follow-up revealed a 10.0% annual rate of major hemorrhage, with 24 cases classified as life-threatening and five as fatal. The stroke incidence rate was 2.6% annually, highlighting the effectiveness of warfarin in reducing stroke risk while noting the higher prevalence of bleeding events in this frail population.

title: Synaptotagmin-Related Neurodevelopmental and Cerebral Abnormalities
abstract: A disruption of synaptotagmin (SYT14) is associated with neurodevelopmental abnormalities and seizures. We describe genetic and molecular studies of a de novo, balanced translocation t(1;3)(q32.1;q25.1) in a 13-year-old female (DGAP129) presenting with cerebral atrophy, macrocephaly, seizures, and developmental delay. Fluorescence in situ hybridization and Southern blot analysis revealed the disruption of the synaptotagmin gene (SYT14) at the 1q32 breakpoint. Expression of SYT14 in human brain was confirmed via Northern blot. Given that synaptotagmin family proteins mediate calcium signaling in processes like neurotransmission and hormone responsiveness, SYT14 is a candidate gene for the developmental issues in this patient. This is the first reported constitutional rearrangement of SYT14, and further studies on DGAP129 may enhance understanding of SYT14's role in neurodevelopment.

title: Isoproterenol-Induced Dystrophin Loss and Structural Integrity Disruption in Cardiomyocytes
abstract: Isoproterenol administration disrupts sarcolemmal stability in rat cardiomyocytes, leading to primary dystrophin depletion and subsequent myocardial injury. The mechanism involves a mismatch between oxygen supply and demand following coronary hypotension, which exacerbates cardiac hyperactivity. Immunofluorescent analysis revealed that dystrophin is the most vulnerable component of the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex, which links actin to laminin in the extracellular matrix. Beta1-integrin and beta-dystroglycan expressions were significantly reduced after dystrophin loss, correlating with structural degradation. Gamma-sarcoglycan and laminin alpha-2 levels also declined, reflecting the breakdown of sarcomeric integrity. Hypotension was observed alongside these changes, highlighting the interplay between oxygen availability and cardiac dysfunction. The study underscores the critical role of dystrophin in maintaining sarcolemmal stability, with isoproterenol-induced loss contributing to severe, irreversible myocardial injury linked to ischaemic injury.

title: Vitamin E and Haptoglobin Genotype Influence Cardiovascular Disease Risk in Diabetic Patients
abstract: This study examines the impact of antioxidant vitamin E supplementation on cardiovascular disease outcomes in individuals with diabetes mellitus and the haptoglobin 2-2 genotype. Researchers aimed to explore whether antioxidant vitamin E could mitigate cardiovascular risks in this high-risk group. By analyzing data from two clinical trials (HOPE and ICARE), they determined the haptoglobin genotype in diabetic participants and assessed the effect of vitamin E on cardiovascular events, including stroke, myocardial infarction, and cardiovascular death. The results showed a significant reduction in the composite endpoint for individuals with the 2-2 genotype, with vitamin E treatment associated with a lower risk of adverse outcomes. The study also highlights the importance of genotyping in personalized medicine, suggesting that targeting the haptoglobin genotype with antioxidant therapy could improve long-term prognosis for diabetic patients.

title: Alternative Splicing and Mild Phenotype in Cystic Fibrosis Patients with E831X Mutation in CFTR Gene
abstract: Alternative splicing at a NAGNAG acceptor site has been implicated in modifying disease outcomes, particularly in genetic disorders involving premature termination codons (PTCs). In cystic fibrosis, the E831X mutation (2623G > T) in the CFTR gene is associated with variable disease severity. A novel splicing mechanism involving NAGNAG tandem sites was identified, leading to insertions or deletions of three nucleotides. This process generates multiple mRNA isoforms in nasal epithelial cells, contributing to proteome diversity. Experimental evidence demonstrates that alternative splicing can bypass a UAG stop codon, resulting in a milder phenotype. While the E831X mutation is a pathogenic variant in the CFTR gene, no direct functional interaction was observed between the E831X allele and the CFTR protein. These findings highlight the role of splicing mechanisms in modulating disease expression and underscore the importance of genetic counseling for patients with cystic fibrosis.

title: In vivo evaluation of a dual adenosine A2A/A1 receptor antagonist in Parkinson's disease models
abstract: This study investigates the efficacy of a dual adenosine A2A/A1 receptor antagonist in various animal models of Parkinson's disease. The compound demonstrated significant therapeutic potential in mouse models of haloperidol-induced catalepsy and reserpine-induced akinesia, both of which are key phenotypic features of Parkinson's disease. Additionally, it showed promising activity in the rat 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA) lesion model of drug-induced rotation and the MPTP-treated non-human primate model. The adenosine A2A/A1 receptor antagonist was also tested in MPTP-treated models, highlighting its broad applicability across different disease paradigms. These findings underscore the compound's potential as a therapeutic agent for Parkinson's disease, with particular emphasis on its effects in models associated with catalepsy and akinesia. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: Parkinson 's disease.

title: Genetic Mutations and Syndromes in Bone Disorders
abstract: Mutations in PTPN11 are associated with metachondromatosis but not with Ollier disease or Maffucci syndrome. Metachondromatosis (MC) is a rare, autosomal dominant condition characterized by combined exostosis and enchondromatosis. MC is distinct from other multiple exostosis syndromes and is not linked to EXT1 or EXT2, which are responsible for multiple osteochondromas. A study identified heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in PTPN11 in 10 of 17 MC families, including 5 frameshift, 2 nonsense, and 3 splice-site mutations. A 15 kb deletion spanning exon 7 of PTPN11 was found in an additional family. Exostosis, a common feature of MC, is not directly linked to PTPN11. Multiple exostosis is associated with EXT2 and EXT1, which are genes involved in bone development. Analysis of 54 patients with Ollier disease or Maffucci syndrome revealed no PTPN11 mutations. These findings suggest that PTPN11 mutations are a frequent cause of MC, while Ollier disease likely has a different genetic basis.

title: Levodopa-Induced Dyskinesia in Parkinson's Disease: Prevalence and Predictors
abstract: This study examines the prevalence and risk factors for levodopa-induced dyskinesia among patients with Parkinson's disease. Chronic levodopa therapy is commonly associated with motor complications, including dyskinesia, which is positively correlated with levodopa-induced effects. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 120 patients with Parkinson's disease undergoing long-term levodopa treatment. The UPDRS scale was used to assess dyskinesia severity. Results show that 52% of patients exhibited dyskinesia, with higher prevalence in those with longer levodopa therapy duration and higher daily doses. Notably, levodopa-induced dyskinesia is negatively correlated with Parkinson's disease progression, suggesting a complex relationship between treatment effects and disease trajectory. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: Parkinson 's disease.

title: VPAC2 Receptor Deficiency Leads to Enhanced Experimental Autoimmune Encephalomyelitis with Altered Cytokine Profiles and Treg Dysfunction
abstract: Mice lacking the VPAC2 receptor exhibit heightened experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) with increased Th1/Th17 responses and diminished Th2/Treg activity. Vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) and pituitary adenylyl cyclase-activating polypeptide (PACAP) are structurally related neuropeptides expressed in the central and peripheral nervous systems. While VIP and PACAP have demonstrated anti-inflammatory effects in inflammatory disease models, their receptor subtypes (VPAC1, VPAC2, and PAC1) show divergent roles in EAE. In this study, VPAC2-deficient mice showed exacerbated (MOG35 - 55)-induced EAE, marked by intensified clinical and histopathological features, elevated proinflammatory cytokines (TNF-alpha, IL-6, IFN-gamma, and IL-17), and reduced anti-inflammatory cytokines (IL-10, TGFbeta, and IL-4). The abundance and proliferative index of CD4(+)CD25(+)FoxP3(+) Tregs in lymph nodes, thymus, and CNS were significantly reduced. Furthermore, Tregs from VPAC2-deficient mice exhibited impaired suppressive activity in vitro. These findings underscore the protective role of PACAP and the VPAC2 receptor in autoimmune disorders, supporting Treg expansion and maintenance.

title: Alcohol Metabolism and Prostate Cancer Risk: A Genetic Analysis
abstract: Alcohol consumption and its metabolic pathways were examined in relation to prostate cancer progression. Prostate cancer remains a significant health concern in men, and the role of alcohol in disease development is still debated. This study investigated genetic variants in alcohol-metabolizing genes, including Alcohol Dehydrogenases (ADHs) and Aldehyde Dehydrogenases (ALDHs), and their associations with prostate cancer incidence and mortality. Data from 23,868 prostate cancer cases and 23,051 controls across 25 studies were analyzed. Single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in 8 alcohol-metabolizing genes were evaluated for their links to prostate cancer diagnosis and survival. While most variants showed no significant association with cancer diagnosis, four SNPs in two genes were linked to increased prostate cancer mortality. rs1441817, rs12910509, and rs8041922 in ALDH-related genes were associated with reduced mortality, while rs10973794 in ALDH1B1 was linked to higher mortality in low-grade prostate cancer. These findings suggest that alcohol consumption may not influence cancer incidence but could affect disease progression through genetic pathways.

title: A 19-Base Pair Deletion in Dihydrofolate Reductase: A New Risk Factor for Preterm Delivery
abstract: Folate plays a crucial role in cell division, which is essential during fetal development. Dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) is necessary for converting folic acid from supplements and fortified foods into its reduced forms, which are used by the cell. Additionally, DHFR helps convert dihydrofolate, produced by thymidylate synthase during DNA synthesis, into active folates. We aimed to investigate whether a common deletion polymorphism in the DHFR gene is associated with preterm delivery or low birth weight. We analyzed 324 pregnant women from Camden, NJ. Folate intake was calculated based on supplement use and two 24-hour dietary recalls during pregnancy. Genomic DNA was extracted from leukocytes and genotyped. Women with the deletion allele had a significantly higher risk of preterm delivery (adjusted odds ratio: 3.0; 95% CI: 1.0, 8.8; P < 0.05) compared to those without. When combined with low folate intake (<400 μg/day), the risk increased further (AOR: 5.5; 95% CI: 1.5, 20.4; P = 0.01) for preterm delivery and low birth weight (AOR: 8.3; 95% CI: 1.8, 38.6; P = 0.01). The 19-base pair deletion in DHFR may be a risk factor for preterm delivery. In the presence of low dietary folate, this allele may also contribute to low birth weight, indicating a potential gene-environment interaction.

title: Mild glycine encephalopathy in a consanguineous family due to a GLDC splice mutation
abstract: A large consanguineous family with mild glycine encephalopathy was identified, characterized by a novel GLDC splice mutation. Clinical features included hypotonia, abnormal movements, convulsions, and moderate mental retardation, with relative preservation of gross motor function and language skills. Aggression and irritability were prominent. Genetic analysis revealed that all nine affected individuals were homozygous for a translationally silent GLDC exon 22 transversion c.2607C > A, while parents were heterozygous. Lymphoblast GLDC mRNA levels were significantly reduced, with aberrantly spliced cDNA species detected. The mutation was also found in an unrelated patient with a favorable clinical outcome. Glycine encephalopathy was associated with GLDC mutations, and the c.2607C > A mutation was strongly correlated with disease manifestation. AMT and GCSH genes were also analyzed but did not show significant associations with the phenotype. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: c.2607C > A..

title: Consecutive Nonsense Mutations in BMPR1A and Their Association with Juvenile Polyposis and Colon Cancer
abstract: A family was found to have two consecutive nonsense mutations in the BMPR1A gene, leading to juvenile polyposis. We identified a novel germline mutation in BMPR1A within a family exhibiting both juvenile polyposis and colon cancer. This mutation involves two consecutive substitutions (735 - 6 TG > AT) that result in two nonsense mutations (Y245X, G246X), inherited in an autosomal dominant manner on one parental chromosome. The mutation causes protein truncation, and this case represents a new instance of consecutive nonsense mutations in human disease. The association between BMPR1A mutations and juvenile polyposis is significant, while the link between BMPR1A and colon cancer remains consistent. The gene product Y245X shows a positive correlation with juvenile polyposis, and G246X also exhibits a positive correlation with the same condition. Additionally, BMPR1A is associated with both juvenile polyposis and colon cancer, highlighting its role in these diseases.

title: Identification of Genes Modulating Alpha-Synuclein Toxicity in Yeast Models
abstract: A novel screening approach was employed to identify genes that mitigate the toxicity of alpha-synuclein in yeast. The role of alpha-synuclein in neurodegeneration remains poorly understood, prompting investigations into genetic factors that counteract its harmful effects. Using a yeast model, suppressors of alpha-synuclein-induced sensitivity to hydrogen peroxide were discovered. Key genes involved in ubiquitin-dependent protein degradation, vesicle trafficking, and stress response were identified. Among these, ENT3, IDP3, JEM1, ARG2, and HSP82 showed the strongest ability to inhibit reactive oxygen species accumulation in cells expressing alpha-synuclein. However, deletion of these genes exacerbated alpha-synuclein toxicity, indicating their protective role. Notably, four of these genes failed to protect against the toxicity of the A30P and A53 T mutant forms of alpha-synuclein, suggesting distinct pathogenic mechanisms. Overexpression of Ent3p, a clathrin adapter protein, led to the redistribution of alpha-synuclein from the plasma membrane into cytoplasmic vesicles, implicating its involvement in vacuolar degradation. A similar clathrin-associated protein, epsinR, is present in human cells, highlighting potential evolutionary conservation. The findings underscore the importance of these genes in modulating alpha-synuclein toxicity and neurodegeneration, with implications for Parkinson's disease-related pathologies. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: Parkinson 's disease-related.

title: Genetic Analysis of a Taiwanese Family with Oculopharyngeal Muscular Dystrophy
abstract: This study examines a Taiwanese family affected by oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy. Oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy is a late-onset autosomal dominant muscle disorder characterized by a short trinucleotide repeat expansion in the polyadenylate binding-protein nuclear 1 gene. A novel mutation was identified in the PABPN1 gene of this family. The polyalanine tract in the PABPN1 gene was found to be expanded due to an insertion of (GCG)4GCA. Genetic analysis of the family revealed that the normal (GCG)6(GCA)3GCG sequence was replaced by (GCG)6(GCA)(GCG)4(GCA)3GCG. This mutation was associated with the autosomal dominant muscle disorder in the family. The study highlights the molecular mechanism underlying the genetic variation in the PABPN1 gene and its role in the pathogenesis of oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy.

title: Modulation of TGF-beta Isoforms and Receptors in Keloid Scar Fibroblasts by Antisense Oligonucleotides
abstract: The study examines the impact of antisense oligonucleotides on TGF-beta isoforms and their receptors in fibroblasts derived from keloid scars. Keloid scars are characterized by excessive collagen deposition and fibroproliferation, a condition linked to dysregulated TGF-beta signaling. TGF-beta, including isoforms TGF-beta1, TGF-beta2, and TGF-beta3, plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of keloid disease, which is a benign tumor-like lesion in humans. TGF-beta exerts its effects by binding to TGF-beta receptors I and II, leading to the activation of downstream signaling pathways. In this investigation, antisense oligonucleotides were used to suppress TGF-beta1 expression, revealing significant reductions in TGF-beta1 and TGF-beta2 levels in keloid-derived fibroblasts compared to normal fibroblasts. The expression of TGF-beta3 and TGF-betaRII showed contrasting patterns, with TGF-betaRII mRNA levels increasing over time. These findings suggest a complex interplay between TGF-beta isoforms and their receptors, highlighting potential therapeutic targets for keloid disease. The results also indicate that keloid fibroblasts may exhibit altered responses to TGF-beta, potentially due to receptor-level modifications or intracellular signaling disruptions. Understanding these regulatory mechanisms could improve treatment strategies for keloid scars and related fibrotic conditions. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: TGF-beta-isoforms and their receptors I and II.

title: Regulation of Stem Cell Fate by Brat and Pum-Nos in Drosophila Ovary
abstract: Brat plays a critical role in directing stem cell differentiation by modulating the activity of a bistable signaling switch that limits BMP pathways. In Drosophila ovarian germline stem cells (GSCs), maintenance depends on Dpp signaling and the translational repression functions of Pumilio (Pum) and Nanos (Nos). During cell division, Dpp signaling is silenced, and Nos is reduced in one daughter cell, triggering its transition to a differentiating cystoblast (CB). However, the downstream effectors of Pum-Nos remain undefined, and the mechanism of CB loss of Dpp responsiveness is unclear. Here, we demonstrate that Brat acts as a key differentiation factor and target of Pum-Nos regulation. Brat is excluded from GSCs by Pum-Nos but collaborates with Pum in CBs to repress specific mRNAs, including those of Mad and dMyc. The simultaneous regulation of these targets decreases cellular sensitivity to Dpp signaling, leading to the cell's loss of self-renewal capacity. Mathematical analysis reveals the bistable dynamics of the Brat system, highlighting how autoregulation of GSC population arises from Brat's integration of extracellular Dpp signals with intracellular responses.

title: Ginsenosides Modulate Opioid-Induced Hyperalgesia in Mice
abstract: Ginsenosides, including Re, Rg1, and Rb1 ginsenosides, were evaluated for their effects on opioid-induced hyperalgesia (OIH) in mice. OIH, a condition characterized by nociceptive sensitization following opioid withdrawal, can limit the clinical use of opioids and complicate recovery from opioid addiction. In this study, mice were administered morphine subcutaneously for 7 days, and on days 8 and 9, they received Re, Rg1, or Rb1 intragastrically. On day 10, thermal sensitivity and acetic acid-induced writhing tests were conducted. Re (300 mg/kg) inhibited OIH in both tests, while Rg1 and Rb1 failed to prevent OIH. Notably, Rg1 showed a tendency to exacerbate OIH in the acetic acid-induced writhing test. These findings suggest that Re, but not Rg1 or Rb1, may play a role in mitigating OIH. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: Re , Rg1 , and Rb1 ginsenosides.

title: Distinct Roles of CD4+IFN-g+ T Cells in Malaria Infection: IL-10 Production and Exhaustion Markers
abstract: CD4+IFN-g+IL-10 and CD4+IFN-g+ T cells play critical roles in the immune response during Malaria Infection. These cells express high levels of PD-1, Lag-3, and TIGIT, indicating cellular exhaustion. Infection leads to the differentiation of CD4+IFN-g+ T cells into short-lived effector cells, while CD4+IFN-g+IL-10 T cells are associated with IL-10 production. The study shows that Malaria Infection is linked to the expression of CD4+IFN-g+ T cells, but PD-1 and Lag-3 are not directly related in this context. Additionally, TIGIT is expressed on CD4+IFN-g+ T cells during infection, and CD4+IFN-g+IL-10 T cells are associated with the regulation of immune responses. The findings highlight the importance of these markers in understanding the dynamics of immune cell function during repeated malaria infections.

title: PON1 Polymorphisms and Mortality Outcomes
abstract: Variants of the paraoxonase 1 (PON1) enzyme have been linked to survival outcomes in populations with cardiovascular conditions. The 55M/L, 192Q/R, and -107C/T polymorphisms have been examined for their role in susceptibility to coronary heart disease (CHD) and other fatal conditions. A study of 2000 Danish individuals aged 45-95 years revealed no significant differences in genotype distributions across age groups. However, longitudinal analysis showed that 192RR homozygotes had a 38% higher risk of mortality compared to 192QQ homozygotes (HR 1.38, p=0.04). These findings were validated in a separate cohort of 550 individuals, with similar results (HR 1.38, p=0.09). The effect was most notable in women, though no significant association was found between PON1 192Q/R and CHD incidence. Instead, the 192RR genotype was associated with worse survival following CHD events. Additionally, the -107C/T variant showed no clear link to mortality or CHD outcomes. These results suggest that PON1 192RR homozygosity may increase mortality risk in middle-aged women, potentially through severe CHD complications rather than direct disease susceptibility. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: death; ischemic heart disease.

title: Genetic Mutations and Phenotypic Features in 22q11.2 Deletions
abstract: Mutations in the TBX1 gene are implicated in the pathogenesis of 22q11.2 deletions, with specific missense variants such as H194Q contributing to phenotypic overlap. 22q11.2 deletions are associated with a range of clinical features, including Shprintzen syndrome, through genetic mechanisms involving TBX1. While haploinsufficiency of TBX1 is traditionally linked to the syndrome, the presence of H194Q mutations suggests alternative pathways. These mutations may stabilize protein-dimer interactions, leading to functional changes that mimic the effects of deletions. Notably, the relationship between 22q11.2 deletions and TBX1 remains complex, with evidence of opposing mechanisms that may influence disease manifestation.

title: Polymorphism in MLH1 and Risk of Cancer After Methylating Chemotherapy for Hodgkin Lymphoma
abstract: A common polymorphism in the MLH1 gene (rs1800734) may influence the development of cancer following methylating chemotherapy. This study examines the association between MLH1 variants and cancer risk in patients with Hodgkin lymphoma, myeloid leukaemia, and breast cancer. The DNA mismatch repair system, particularly MLH1, plays a critical role in mediating the cytotoxic effects of methylating agents. Loss of MLH1 function is linked to reduced toxicity and increased mutagenic risk. Patients with Hodgkin lymphoma who received methylating chemotherapy showed higher MLH1 variant frequencies in those who developed therapy-related acute myeloid leukaemia compared to those without prior exposure. The rs1800734 variant was overrepresented in t-AML cases, correlating with a significantly increased risk of malignancy. Additionally, the rs1800734 variant demonstrated a positive correlation with cancer development in patients exposed to methylating agents. These findings suggest that MLH1 polymorphisms may modulate cancer risk in specific disease contexts. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: Cytotoxicity.

title: Discovery of Genetic Variants Linked to Systemic Lupus Erythematosus via Advanced Pathway Analysis
abstract: This study explores the genetic underpinnings of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) by analyzing specific gene polymorphisms. Researchers employed a novel pathway-based platform to investigate 1,204 genes associated with SLE. Key findings include a significant association between SLE and the N673S variant in the P-selectin gene (SELP), as well as the C203S variant in the interleukin-1 receptor-associated kinase 1 (IRAK1) gene. These polymorphisms, identified through transmission disequilibrium testing, demonstrate strong statistical significance. Additionally, the TNFRSF6 gene (Fas) and IRF5 show associations with SLE pathogenesis. The study also highlights the role of the C203S variant in IRAK1 and N673S in SELP, which are positively correlated with SLE susceptibility. These results underscore the importance of IRAK1 and SELP in SLE development, offering new insights into the genetic mechanisms of this complex disease.

title: Antithrombin Modulation of Puromycin Aminonucleoside-Induced Nephrotic Syndrome in Rats
abstract: Antithrombin was evaluated for its impact on puromycin aminonucleoside-induced nephrotic syndrome in a rat model. Rats were administered antithrombin (50 or 500 IU/kg/i.v.) daily for 10 days following puromycin aminonucleoside injection (50 mg/kg/i.v.). The treatment significantly reduced hematological abnormalities and renal dysfunction associated with puromycin aminonucleoside. Hyperlipidemia and nephrotic syndrome were also mitigated. Histopathological analysis showed reduced tubular damage and improved renal function in antithrombin-treated rats. Additionally, antithrombin suppressed apoptosis of renal tubular epithelial cells and decreased cytokine levels. These results indicate that thrombin plays a key role in the pathogenesis of puromycin aminonucleoside-induced nephrotic syndrome, suggesting potential clinical applications for antithrombin in treating nephrotic syndrome. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: nephrosis.

title: Neurofibromin 1 Defects and Tumor-Suppressor Pathways in Ovarian Serous Carcinomas
abstract: Neurofibromin 1 (NF1) defects are common in human ovarian serous carcinomas and co-occur with TP53 mutations. Ovarian serous carcinoma (OSC) is the most common and lethal histologic type of ovarian epithelial malignancy. Mutations of TP53 and dysfunction of the Brca1 and/or Brca2 tumor-suppressor proteins have been implicated in the molecular pathogenesis of a large fraction of OSCs, but frequent somatic mutations in other well-established tumor-suppressor genes have not been identified. Using a genome-wide screen of DNA copy number alterations in 36 primary OSCs, we identified two tumors with apparent homozygous deletions of the NF1 gene. Subsequently, 18 ovarian carcinoma-derived cell lines and 41 primary OSCs were evaluated for NF1 alterations. Markedly reduced or absent expression of Nf1 protein was observed in 6 of the 18 cell lines, and using the protein truncation test and sequencing of cDNA and genomic DNA, NF1 mutations resulting in deletion of exons and/or aberrant splicing of NF1 transcripts were detected in 5 of the 6 cell lines with loss of NF1 expression. Similarly, NF1 alterations including homozygous deletions and splicing mutations were identified in 9 (22%) of 41 primary OSCs. As expected, tumors and cell lines with NF1 defects lacked mutations in KRAS or BRAF but showed Ras pathway activation based on immunohistochemical detection of phosphorylated MAPK (primary tumors) or increased levels of GTP-bound Ras (cell lines). The TP53 tumor-suppressor gene was mutated in all OSCs with documented NF1 mutation, suggesting that the pathways regulated by these two tumor-suppressor proteins often cooperate in the development of ovarian carcinomas with serous differentiation.

title: Tranexamic Acid and Postoperative Seizures: A Multivariate Analysis
abstract: This study examines the relationship between tranexamic acid and convulsive seizures following cardiac surgery. With limited contemporary data on postoperative seizures, a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from 11,529 patients undergoing cardiopulmonary bypass between 2004 and 2010 was conducted. Convulsive seizures were defined as transient episodes of disturbed brain function characterized by abnormal involuntary motor movements. Multivariate regression analysis identified independent predictors of postoperative seizures, including age, female sex, redo surgery, calcification of ascending aorta, congestive heart failure, deep hypothermic circulatory arrest, aortic cross-clamp duration, and tranexamic acid. Tranexamic acid was a strong independent predictor of seizures (OR 14.3, 95% CI 5.5-36.7; p<0.001). Patients with convulsive seizures had significantly higher in-hospital mortality rates and longer hospital stays compared to those without seizures. The study highlights the importance of considering tranexamic acid use in patients at risk for postoperative complications, including abnormal involuntary motor movements and postoperative complications. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: postoperative complication.

title: MicroRNA Expression Dynamics in Pancreatic Cancer Progression Using the KrasG12D;Pdx1-Cre Model
abstract: MicroRNA expression profiles during pancreatic cancer development and progression were analyzed in a genetically engineered KrasG12D;Pdx1-Cre mouse model. Differential miRNA expression was observed in various cancers, including pancreatic cancer. Due to limited early-stage tissue samples, stage-specific miRNA alterations during cancer initiation and progression remain poorly characterized. This study investigated global miRNA expression and processing machinery in the KC model. At 25 weeks, miRNA microarray analysis revealed significant downregulation of miR-150, miR-494, miR-138, miR-148a, miR-216a, and miR-217, along with upregulation of miR-146b, miR-205, miR-31, miR-192, and miR-21 compared to controls. Expression of miRNA biosynthetic components such as Dicer, Exportin-5, TRKRA, and TARBP2 was downregulated, while DGCR8 and Ago2 were upregulated.
