Mice with hypotension exhibited significantly longer latencies compared to those with saline, nitroglycerin plus nimodipine, or delayed nitroglycerin. Nimodipine reduced hypotension-induced memory deficits but did not improve memory in the absence of hypotension. Calcium levels remained unchanged across groups, and no significant differences were observed in oxygenation indices. CONCLUSION: Nimodipine counteracts nitroglycerin-induced hypotension-related memory impairment, potentially through calcium homeostasis preservation, as no differences in oxygenation were noted among groups.

title: Efficacy of modafinil in mitigating sleep disturbances in cocaine-dependent individuals
abstract: A randomized controlled trial evaluated the impact of modafinil on sleep patterns and daytime sleepiness in cocaine-dependent individuals. Twenty participants, including chronic cocaine users, were divided into two groups: those receiving modafinil (400 mg daily) and those given a placebo, over a 16-day period. Sleep assessments were conducted on days 1-3, 7-9, and 14-16 to monitor changes across three weeks of abstinence. The Multiple Sleep Latency Test was administered at multiple time points to assess daytime sleepiness. Results indicated that prolonged abstinence from cocaine correlated with deteriorating sleep metrics. Modafinil treatment was associated with reduced nighttime sleep latency and increased slow-wave sleep duration in cocaine-dependent participants. The drug's effects were most pronounced in the third week of abstinence, correlating with improved total sleep time and shorter REM latency. Compared to healthy controls, modafinil normalized sleep architecture in cocaine users. Additionally, modafinil was linked to enhanced daytime sleep latency, though subjective daytime sleepiness remained slightly elevated. These findings suggest that morning dosing of modafinil may help restore sleep function and reduce daytime sleepiness in cocaine users.

title: Synergy between Morphine and CNSB002 in Rat Models of Pain
abstract: This study investigated the combined effects of morphine and CNSB002, a sodium channel blocker with antioxidant properties, in rat models of inflammatory and neuropathic pain. The objective was to evaluate the antihyperalgesic activity of CNSB002 alone and in combination with morphine. Using carrageenan-induced paw inflammation and streptozotocin-induced diabetic neuropathy models, dose-response curves were constructed for intraperitoneal administration of morphine, CNSB002, and their combination. Results showed that the maximum nonsedating doses were 3.2 mg/kg for morphine, 10.0 mg/kg for CNSB002, and 5.0 mg/kg CNSB002 with 3.2 mg/kg morphine. The ED50 values for CNSB002 were higher than maximum doses, but the combination reduced ED50 for morphine. Antinociception was significantly enhanced by co-administration, with reversal of hyperalgesia increasing from 28.0-31.7% to 114.6-56.9% in inflammatory and neuropathic models, respectively. These findings suggest that CNSB002 may augment the antihyperalgesic effects of morphine in pain models, particularly in inflammatory and diabetic neuropathy conditions.

title: Efficacy of Coenzyme Q10 in Mitigating Cisplatin-Induced Nephrotoxicity
abstract: A study was conducted to evaluate the protective effects of Coenzyme Q10 against cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity in mice. Mice were administered cisplatin to induce acute renal injury, and Coenzyme Q10 was given in a specific dose and duration. Coenzyme Q10 significantly reduced blood urea nitrogen and creatinine levels, which were elevated by cisplatin. It also restored antioxidant defenses, including glutathione and superoxide dismutase, and decreased the levels of tumor necrosis factor-alpha, nitric oxide, and platinum ions. Additionally, it prevented the reduction of zinc and selenium in renal tissues. Histopathological analysis showed that Coenzyme Q10 mitigated cisplatin-induced kidney damage. Immunohistochemical findings indicated a decrease in the overexpression of inducible nitric oxide synthase, nuclear factor-kappaB, caspase-3, and p53 in renal tissues. These findings suggest that Coenzyme Q10 could be a potential therapeutic option for preventing acute cisplatin nephrotoxicity. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: lipid.

title: Efficacy and safety of asenapine in a placebo- and haloperidol-controlled trial for schizophrenia
abstract: Asenapine is approved for the acute treatment of schizophrenia or manic episodes in bipolar I disorder. In a double-blind, 6-week trial, 458 patients with schizophrenia were randomly assigned to receive asenapine 5 mg twice daily, asenapine 10 mg twice daily, placebo, or haloperidol 4 mg twice daily. Using last observations carried forward, mean reductions in the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale total score were significantly greater with asenapine 5 mg twice daily (-16.2) and haloperidol (-15.4) compared to placebo (-10.7; both P < 0.05). Mixed model for repeated measures showed greater changes at day 42 with asenapine 5 and 10 mg twice daily (-21.3 and -19.4) and haloperidol (-20.0) than placebo (-14.6; all P < 0.05). On the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale positive subscale, all treatments were superior to placebo. Asenapine 5 mg twice daily was superior to placebo on the negative subscale with MMRM and on the general psychopathology subscale with LOCF and MMRM. Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 44% and 52% of asenapine 5 and 10 mg groups, 57% of haloperidol, and 41% of placebo. Extrapyramidal symptoms were reported in 15% and 18% of asenapine 5 and 10 mg groups, 34% of haloperidol, and 10% of placebo. No more than 5% of patients had clinically significant weight change. Post hoc analyses showed similar efficacy with asenapine and haloperidol, with greater contrasts in adverse events, especially extrapyramidal symptoms. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: haloperidol-controlled; psychotic.

title: Dopamine's Role in Methamphetamine-Induced Neurotoxicity
abstract: Dopamine is not a critical factor in the development of methamphetamine-induced neurotoxicity. Previous studies suggested that dopamine (DA) mediates the toxic effects of methamphetamine (METH) on brain dopaminergic neurons, as interventions altering DA levels modulate toxicity. However, confounding variables related to drug-induced temperature changes have complicated these conclusions. Recent findings indicate that L-dihydroxyphenylalanine can reverse the protective effects of alpha-methyl-para-tyrosine on METH-induced DA neurotoxicity, but this effect is also influenced by temperature changes. Additionally, mice with genetic deficiencies in brain DA exhibit METH neurotoxicity when thermic effects of METH are maintained. Furthermore, mice with unilateral brain DA deficits display METH-induced dopaminergic deficits that are comparable on both sides. These results suggest that DA is not essential for METH-induced dopaminergic neurotoxicity, highlighting the need to investigate mechanisms independent of DA. Dopamine shows a positive correlation with dopaminergic deficits, while alpha-methyl-para-tyrosine exhibits a negative correlation with neurotoxicity. Dopamine also interacts with methamphetamine-induced effects, and L-dihydroxyphenylalanine is associated with alpha-methyl-para-tyrosine in this context. Neurotoxicity and toxicity are distinct but related phenomena in this study.

title: Role of Glutamate-Mediated Mechanisms in the Inferior Colliculus in Modulating Haloperidol-Induced Catalepsy
abstract: Glutamate-mediated signaling through NMDA receptors in the inferior colliculus plays a key role in modulating haloperidol-induced catalepsy. This study investigates the neural circuits in the inferior colliculus, which are uniquely connected to motor control structures, and their relationship to motor behavior. Experiments demonstrate that activation of the inferior colliculus via excitatory amino acid microinjections induces immobility, which is linked to the dopamine receptor blocker haloperidol. The research examines how glutamate-mediated mechanisms in the inferior colliculus interact with haloperidol-induced catalepsy, revealing that intracollicular injections of MK-801 and AP7 significantly reduce cataleptic symptoms, while N-methyl-d-aspartate increases the latency to step down a horizontal bar. These findings highlight the influence of glutamate-mediated pathways on haloperidol-induced catalepsy and their role in regulating motor activity, underscoring the connection between NMDA receptors and dopamine receptor function in this context.

title: Curcumin Modulates Oxidative Stress and Inflammatory Responses in Antiepileptic Drug-Induced Cognitive Impairment
abstract: Curcumin exhibits antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties that may counteract the cognitive and oxidative effects of antiepileptic drugs. Phenobarbitone and carbamazepine, commonly used for epilepsy, are associated with cognitive dysfunction and increased oxidative stress in chronic use. This study evaluated the impact of curcumin on phenobarbitone- and carbamazepine-induced cognitive impairment and oxidative damage in rats. Rats were administered vehicle or drugs for 21 days, followed by behavioral tests and biochemical analyses. Results showed that phenobarbitone and carbamazepine significantly impaired cognitive function and elevated malondialdehyde levels, while reduced glutathione levels were observed. Concurrent curcumin administration prevented cognitive deficits and normalized oxidative markers without altering drug concentrations. These findings suggest curcumin's potential as a safe adjuvant to antiepileptic therapy, mitigating cognitive dysfunction and oxidative damage caused by phenobarbitone and carbamazepine.

title: Efficacy of Crocus sativus Constituents in Mitigating Neurodegenerative Symptoms
abstract: This study investigated the impact of constituents from Crocus sativus L., particularly crocin, on neurodegenerative conditions such as Alzheimer's disease and learning and memory impairment in male rats. The research focused on the effects of crocin, a key component of Crocus sativus L., in conjunction with streptozocin-induced models of sporadic Alzheimer's disease. Male Wistar rats were divided into groups to assess the influence of crocin on cognitive functions, including learning and memory impairment, cognitive deficits, and neurodegenerative diseases. The study utilized passive avoidance and Y-maze tasks to evaluate cognitive performance. Results indicated that crocin treatment significantly reduced learning and memory impairment and cognitive deficits in rats exposed to streptozocin. Additionally, crocin was found to have a positive correlation with improvements in spatial cognition and a negative correlation with the progression of neurodegenerative diseases. Carotenoids were also examined, but no direct association was found with learning and memory impairment, cognitive deficits, or neurodegenerative diseases. Constituents of Crocus sativus L. were shown to have no direct relationship with streptozocin-induced effects, while crocin exhibited a negative correlation with Alzheimer's disease and a positive correlation with neurodegenerative diseases. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: Alzheimer 's disease.

title: Role of Nitric Oxide in Lindane-Induced Convulsions in Rats
abstract: The impact of nitric oxide on convulsions caused by lindane in rodents was investigated. Lindane, an organochloride pesticide and scabicide, induces convulsions primarily through GABA(A) receptor blockade. Nitric oxide (NO), a gaseous neurotransmitter, exhibits conflicting roles in epileptogenesis due to opposing effects of L-arginine, a precursor of NO syntheses (NOS), and L-NAME, an inhibitor of NOS, observed in various epilepsy models. This study aimed to assess NO's effects on behavioral and EEG characteristics of lindane-induced epilepsy in male Wistar rats. Administration of L-arginine (600, 800, and 1000 mg/kg, i.p.) in a dose-dependent manner significantly increased convulsion incidence and severity, shortening latency to first convulsion when combined with lower lindane doses (4 mg/kg, i.p.). Conversely, pretreatment with L-NAME (500, 700, and 900 mg/kg, i.p.) reduced convulsion incidence and severity, prolonging latency to convulsion following higher lindane doses (8 mg/kg, i.p.). EEG analyses revealed increased ictal periods in rats receiving L-arginine before lindane, while L-NAME pretreatment decreased this number. These findings support NO's role as an endogenous convulsant in lindane-induced seizures. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: GABA(A ) receptors.

title: Cytogenetic Effects of Ifosfamide, Mesna, and Their Combination on Rabbit Lymphocytes
abstract: The cytogenetic effects of ifosfamide, mesna, and their combination were evaluated on peripheral rabbit lymphocytes in an in vivo/in vitro study. Ifosfamide, an alkylating nitrogen mustard, is used as an antineoplasmic agent and is known for its strong urotoxic activity, causing hemorrhagic cystitis. Mesna is administered alongside ifosfamide to mitigate this side effect. In vivo experiments involved administering ifosfamide and mesna separately to rabbit lymphocytes, which were then cultured in vitro. Cytogenetic markers such as sister chromatid exchanges (SCEs), proliferation rate index (PRI), and Mitotic Index were measured. Mesna, when combined with ifosfamide, significantly reduced SCE frequencies compared to ifosfamide alone. High concentrations of mesna alone also led to notable decreases in PRI. Mesna effectively counteracts ifosfamide's genotoxicity, though at high doses, it may inhibit the drug's cytostatic effects. Hemorrhagic cystitis was observed in the group receiving ifosfamide without mesna, highlighting the necessity of mesna for reducing this adverse outcome.

title: Crocin Modulates Lipid Metabolism and ERK Pathway in Diazinon-Exposed Rats
abstract: Crocin ameliorates lipid dysregulation in chronic diazinon exposure by regulating the ERK1/2 pathway in rat liver. Diazinon, an organophosphorus insecticide, disrupts lipid homeostasis and induces hyperlipemia, as evidenced by elevated cholesterol and triglyceride levels. Crocin treatment restores ERK1/2 activation and increases low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLr) expression, counteracting diazinon-induced disturbances. This study evaluated the effects of Corn oil, diazinon (15mg/kg/day), and crocin (12.5/25mg/kg) on lipid metabolism in rats, revealing that crocin mitigates hyperlipemia and enhances LDLr transcript levels. Western blotting and qPCR confirmed reduced ERK1/2 phosphorylation and LDLr expression in diazinon-exposed rats, with crocin reversing these changes. The findings suggest that Crocin's protective effect is mediated through ERK pathway modulation and LDLr upregulation, offering potential therapeutic strategies for organophosphorus-induced lipid disorders. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: LDL.

title: Evaluating the Efficacy of Sodium Chloride and Diltiazem in Preventing Contrast-Induced Nephropathy
abstract: This study investigates the protective effects of isotonic sodium chloride, sodium bicarbonate with dextrose, and isotonic sodium chloride combined with diltiazem in preventing contrast-induced nephropathy. Patients undergoing percutaneous coronary angiography received 30-60 mL of iodinated contrast agent, with baseline creatinine levels between 1.1 and 3.1 mg/dL. Participants were divided into three groups: Group 1 received isotonic sodium chloride, Group 2 received a 5% dextrose and sodium bicarbonate solution, and Group 3 received isotonic sodium chloride both before and after contrast injection, along with diltiazem the day before and first two days post-injection. Plasma blood urea nitrogen and creatinine levels were measured on days 2 and 7. Baseline creatinine levels were similar across groups. Of 60 patients, 16 developed acute renal failure on day 2 (26.6%). Group 1 had 5 cases (25%), Group 2 had 6 (30%), and Group 3 had 5 (25%). The study found no significant differences in preventing contrast-induced nephropathy among the three treatments. Contrast-induced nephropathy was positively correlated with acute renal failure, while diltiazem was associated with a reduced risk of nephropathy. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: calcium.

title: Efficacy of Fentanyl and Midazolam in Preventing Etomidate-Induced Myoclonus
abstract: This prospective study evaluated the effectiveness of fentanyl, midazolam, and their combination in preventing etomidate-induced myoclonus. Patients were divided into four groups based on pretreatment regimens: no pretreatment (Group NP), fentanyl 1 μg/kg (Group F), midazolam 0.03 mg/kg (Group M), and a combination of midazolam 0.015 mg/kg + fentanyl 0.5 μg/kg (Group FM). Etomidate was administered 2 minutes after pretreatment, and myoclonic movements were assessed for severity. Pain intensity, hemodynamic stability, and adverse effects were also monitored. Results showed myoclonus incidence rates of 80%, 45%, 75%, and 20% in Groups NP, F, M, and FM, respectively. Fentanyl and the combination demonstrated significantly lower myoclonus occurrence. Additionally, etomidate-induced myoclonus showed a positive correlation with pain severity, while midazolam use was associated with a negative correlation to myoclonus. Fentanyl and midazolam exhibited no direct association in this context.

title: Drug-Drug Interactions and Muscle Toxicity in Hepatitis C Patients
abstract: A 52-year-old man with chronic hepatitis C virus infection was treated with telaprevir, ribavirin, and pegylated interferon. He was also prescribed simvastatin. One month into therapy, he developed muscle toxicity and rhabdomyolysis. Creatine kinase levels reached 62,246 IU/L, prompting discontinuation of all antiviral drugs and simvastatin. The patient's renal function remained stable, and creatine kinase levels decreased to 230 IU/L within 14 days. Telaprevir is suspected as the causative agent in the interaction with simvastatin, attributed to CYP3A4-mediated inhibition of simvastatin clearance. Simvastatin plasma concentrations increased 30-fold, leading to statin-induced muscle toxicity. This case highlights the clinical significance of drug-drug interactions between telaprevir and statins in hepatitis C patients. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: hepatitis C virus infected.

title: Founder Mutations in BRCA1 and BRCA2 in Polish Families with Breast-Ovarian Cancer
abstract: Founder mutations in the BRCA1 gene were identified in 35 of 66 Polish families with breast-ovarian cancer. These families included 26 with both breast and ovarian cancers, 4 with ovarian cancer only, and 36 with breast cancer only. Mutations such as 5382insC and 4153delA were detected, along with BRCA2 abnormalities. BRCA1 abnormalities were found in all four ovarian cancer families and 67% of those with both cancers. The study also identified C61 G mutations and recurrent BRCA1 defects, highlighting the role of these genetic variations in cancer susceptibility. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: breast or ovarian cancer.

title: D90A-SOD1 and Neurodegenerative Disease Linkage
abstract: D90A-SOD1 mutations are associated with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), a neurodegenerative disease. D90A-SOD1 exhibits a unique pattern in recessive, dominant, and sporadic cases, with homozygotes showing extended survival. A rare haplotype links D90A-SOD1 to a cis-acting modifier, suggesting a genetic basis for disease variation. Neurodegenerative disease manifestations vary with D90A-SOD1 inheritance, highlighting its role in ALS pathogenesis.

title: Improved Tetra-Primer PCR for Detecting FGFR3 G380R Mutation in Achondroplasia
abstract: This study presents an improved tetra-primer PCR method for detecting the FGFR3 G380R mutation, which is responsible for achondroplasia, a common form of dwarfism. The assay efficiently identifies both c.1138G>A and c.1138G>C mutations in the FGFR3 gene, enabling accurate genotyping. The method demonstrated high sensitivity, detecting one mutant allele in 100 wild-type alleles. Testing in 50 controls, 3 achondroplasia patients, and 5 amniotic fluids showed complete concordance with PCR-RFLP. This approach offers a cost-effective and user-friendly solution for FGFR3 p.G380R analysis, suitable for low-tech laboratories.

title: Association Between MMP1 Promoter Polymorphism and Lumbar Disc Disease
abstract: This study investigates the association between the -1607 promoter polymorphism of MMP1 and lumbar disc disease (DDD) in Southern Chinese populations. The guanine insertion/deletion (G/D) variant at the -1607 site of the MMP1 gene was linked to altered promoter activity and transcription levels. Genotyping using the Sequenom platform revealed a significant allelic association between the D allele and DDD (p=0.027, OR=1.41). Additionally, the D allele showed a positive correlation with lumbar disc disease, highlighting its potential role in disease progression. The findings support a genetic link between MMP1 polymorphisms and DDD, with implications for targeted therapies. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: guanine insertion/deletion ( G/D ) , the -1607 promoter polymorphism; D allele for the -1607.

title: Regulation of Lung Endothelial Permeability by Prostaglandin A2 via EP4 Receptor
abstract: Prostaglandin A2 (PGA2) modulates vascular endothelial function by activating the EP4 receptor, which enhances endothelial barrier integrity and protects against barrier dysfunction caused by thrombin and lipopolysaccharide (LPS). EP4-mediated effects involve Rap1/Rac1 GTPase activation and protein kinase A targets such as VE-cadherin, p120-catenin, ZO-1, cortactin, and VASP. PGA2 suppresses LPS-induced inflammatory signaling by inhibiting NFkB and reducing EC adhesion molecules like ICAM1 and VCAM1. These protective effects are abolished by EP4 inhibition, highlighting the role of the PGA2-EP4 axis in acute lung injury (ALI) models. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: thrombin receptor-activating.

title: Cardiovascular Complications in Terbutaline-Treated Preterm Labor
abstract: Terbutaline treatment for preterm labor was associated with cardiovascular complications in 8 of 160 patients. Corticosteroid therapy and twin gestations were identified as predisposing factors. The study highlights a negative correlation between terbutaline use and cardiovascular outcomes, while also noting an association with corticosteroid therapy and twin gestations.

title: Genetic Basis of Bernard-Soulier Syndrome in a Compound Heterozygote
abstract: A patient with Bernard-Soulier syndrome (BSS) exhibits compound heterozygosity for a novel nine-nucleotide deletion and the Asn45Ser missense mutation in the glycoprotein IX gene. BSS is an inherited bleeding disorder linked to abnormalities in the platelet glycoprotein (GP) Ib/IX/V complex, which includes von Willebrand factor as a key receptor. The complex comprises subunits encoded by separate genes, with mutations in glycoprotein IX (GPIX) contributing to the disorder. The patient's platelets show reduced expression of GP Ib/IX/V, and genetic analysis confirms the presence of both mutations, highlighting the role of GPIX in BSS pathogenesis. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: glycoprotein ( GP ) Ib/IX/V; changes asparagine 86 for alanine and eliminates amino acids 87 , 88 , and 89 ( arginine , threonine , and proline ); nine-nucleotide deletion starting at position 1952.

title: Synergistic Role of IL-3 and CSF-1 in CD11c+ Macrophage Generation
abstract: This study demonstrates that IL-3 and CSF-1 synergistically promote the generation of CD11c+ IL-10-producing macrophages. CSF-1 enhances IL-3-driven CD11c+ cell expansion and modulates CSF-1/CSF-1R signaling, which is associated with c-Fos-associated monopoiesis. These cells produce high levels of IL-1, IL-6, and TNFa in response to LPS, while exhibiting IL-10-producing characteristics. Both IL-3 and IL-3/CSF-1-derived cells resemble macrophages in morphology and function, lacking classical dendritic cell features.

title: Cys 23-Ser 23 Polymorphism in 5-HT(2C) Receptor and Weight Regulation in Seasonal Affective Disorder
abstract: Researchers investigated the association between a Cys 23-Ser 23 substitution in the 5-HT(2C) receptor gene and weight regulation in females with seasonal affective disorder. The study found that this genetic variation is linked to weight gain when depressed, highlighting the role of the 5-HT(2C) receptor in appetite control. The findings suggest that the Cys 23-Ser 23 polymorphism may influence body weight management in individuals with seasonal affective disorder. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: 5-HT(2C ) receptor.

title: Functional Redundancy and Regulation of Cysteine-Rich Domain-Containing Proteins in Zebrafish Development
abstract: Zebrafish Chordin-like and Chordin proteins function redundantly in dorsoventral axis patterning. Chordin is a cysteine-rich domain-containing protein that modulates TGFbeta-like ligand signaling. Chordin-like 1 and 2 (CHL1 and CHL2) are members of this group, with Chl in zebrafish potentially overlapping CHL1 and CHL2 functions. Chl is a maternal and zygotically expressed protein, showing spatiotemporal overlap with Chordin. Chl dorsalizes embryos upon overexpression and is cleaved by BMP1, which antagonizes its activity. Loss-of-function studies reveal Chl acts as a BMP antagonist, overlapping and redundantly functioning with Chordin in dorsoventral axis formation. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: cysteine-rich domain-containing proteins.

title: Manganese Superoxide Dismutase Polymorphisms and Urolithiasis Risk
abstract: This study investigates the association between manganese superoxide dismutase (Mn-SOD) gene polymorphisms and urolithiasis. A valine (Val) to alanine (Ala) substitution at amino acid 16 in the Mn-SOD gene is linked to an increased risk of urolithiasis. Oxidative stress contributes to stone formation in the renal system. PCR-based genotyping using agarose gels revealed significant differences in Mn-SOD alleles between patients and controls, highlighting the potential of Mn-SOD analysis as a tool for urolithiasis risk assessment. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: valine ( Val ) to alanine ( Ala ) substitution at amino acid 16.

title: Epigenetic Regulation of DOCK8 in Lung and Other Cancers
abstract: Epigenetic regulation of the DOCK8 gene is implicated in the development of lung and other cancers. DOCK8, a gene product involved in cell migration and adhesion, is frequently downregulated in lung cancer, with 87% of primary cases showing reduced expression compared to normal lung tissue. Treatment with 5-Aza-2'-deoxy-cytidine and Trichostatin A restores DOCK8 expression in lung cancer cell lines, suggesting epigenetic mechanisms such as DNA methylation and histone deacetylation are involved. Additionally, homozygous deletions of DOCK8 have been observed in gastric and breast cancer cell lines, highlighting its role in multiple cancers. These findings indicate that both genetic and epigenetic inactivation of DOCK8 contribute to cancer progression.

title: Focal Dermal Hypoplasia Caused by a Novel PORCN Mutation
abstract: Focal dermal hypoplasia (FDH), an X-linked dominant disorder, was diagnosed in a 2-year-old Thai girl with characteristic linear streaks of hypoplastic dermis, depressed features, and dental caries. The condition is linked to a heterozygous G > T substitution at nucleotide c.898 in the PORCN gene, converting a glutamic acid residue (GAA) to a premature termination codon (TAA). This mutation, designated p. E300X, was identified as a de novo change in the PORCN gene, confirming the molecular basis of FDH and its association with skeletal, dental, and cutaneous abnormalities. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: glutamic acid residue ( GAA ) to a premature termination codon ( TAA ).

title: HIV-1 Tat and Indoleamine 2,3 Dioxygenase Activation in Hippocampal Slice Cultures
abstract: HIV-1 Tat activates indoleamine 2,3 dioxygenase in murine organotypic hippocampal slice cultures through p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase-dependent mechanisms. This activation is associated with depressive-like behavior in HIV-1-infected mice, as evidenced by increased TNFa and IL-6 protein levels, and upregulation of the inducible isoform of nitric oxide synthase and serotonin transporter. Tryptophan metabolism is modulated by Tat-induced IDO expression, which is enhanced by IFNg pretreatment. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: SB 202190.

title: Dynamic Regulation of ESCRT-III Assemblies by Vps4 and ATP in Membrane Remodeling
abstract: ESCRT-III assemblies dynamically regulate membrane remodeling during cytokinesis through subunit turnover mediated by Vps4 and ATP. The ESCRT-III complex, which includes subunits like Snf7, undergoes rapid subunit exchange at the midbody, requiring the ATPase Vps4 for functional assembly. In vitro studies show that Vps2/Vps24 subunits form filaments with Snf7, but Vps4 and ATP alleviate growth inhibition. High-speed atomic force microscopy reveals dynamic ESCRT-III spirals, highlighting the role of Vps4 in maintaining membrane shape adaptability.

title: Mechanisms of B-Cell Clonogenicity in HIV-1 p17 Variants
abstract: A single Arginine (R) to Glycine (G) mutation at position 76 in p17R76G confers B-cell clonogenic activity, modulating PTEN/PI3K/Akt signaling to influence apoptosis inhibition (CASP-9, CASP-7, DFF-45, NPM, YWHAZ, Src, PAX2, MAPK8), cell cycle promotion (CDK1, CDK2, CDK8, CHEK1, CHEK2, GSK-3 beta, PAK1, PP2C-alpha), and cancer progression. The mutation impacts protein folding and oligomerization, enabling functional epitopes to elicit B-cell growth signals through unknown receptors in HIV-1-seropositive patients with lymphoma. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: Arginine ( R ) to Glycine ( G ) mutation at position 76; S75X; p17.

title: Calbindin-D28k and Alzheimer's Disease Pathogenesis
abstract: Calbindin-D28k plays a critical role in preventing neuronal death and maintaining calcium homeostasis in Alzheimer's disease models. Depletion of CB leads to significant neuronal loss in the subiculum, increased apoptotic features, and mitochondrial dysfunction. The study shows reduced phosphorylation of mitogen-activated protein kinase and cAMP response element-binding protein, as well as decreased levels of N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors and synaptophysin in CBKOTg mice compared to Tg mice. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: Alzheimer 's disease; calcium-binding; protein/presenilin; N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor 1; amyloid b-peptide; NMDA receptor 2A; PSD-95.

title: Voltage-Dependent Anion Channel 1 in Desminopathy and Mitochondrial Dysfunction
abstract: Voltage-Dependent Anion Channel 1 (VDAC1) plays a role in mitochondrial dysfunction associated with desminopathy. Desminopathies, caused by desmin gene mutations, are protein aggregation myopathies. Mitochondrial dysfunction is an early pathological change in desminopathies. VDAC1 regulates mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization and is involved in apoptosis. Immunofluorescence shows VDAC1 accumulation in desmin-stained areas of desminopathy patients and rat models. Apoptosis-related proteins bax and ATF2 are present in desminopathy, while bcl-2, bcl-xl, and HK2.VDAC1 are not. Desmin and VDAC1 are closely linked in tissue splices of desminopathy patients and models at the protein level.

title: Drug-Induced Long QT Syndrome in Methadone Users: Risk Factors and QT Prolongation
abstract: Methadone, a chemical entity, is associated with long QT syndrome and torsades de pointes, particularly in injection drug users. Hypokalemia and potassium levels are risk factors for QT interval prolongation, which is influenced by cytochrome P-450 3A4 inhibitors. The study found a significant correlation between methadone dose and QTc length, highlighting the role of cytochrome P-450 3A4 in drug metabolism and QT prolongation.

title: Bortezomib and dexamethasone as salvage therapy in patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma
abstract: Bortezomib and dexamethasone were evaluated as salvage therapy for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma. The combination showed significant response rates, with 55% achieving partial response. However, peripheral neuropathy occurred in 78% of patients, leading to treatment discontinuation. Bortezomib and dexamethasone were used in cotreatment, demonstrating positive correlation with survival outcomes, though negative correlation with neuropathy severity.

title: Severe Thyroid Hormone Resistance and Genetic Mutations in TR-β Gene
abstract: A patient with severe thyroid hormone resistance was found to have homozygous or hemizygous mutations in the TR-β gene. The I280S mutation (1123T-->G) was present on both alleles or in a hemizygous form, leading to a severe phenotype. This includes impaired intellectual development, hyperkinetic behavior, tachycardia, and hearing and visual impairment. The condition is associated with resistance to thyroid hormone and may present with thyrotoxicosis or hypothyroidism, highlighting the role of TR-β mutations in these symptoms. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: T3 receptor.

title: ACE Gene Polymorphism and Gastric Cancer Metastasis Correlation
abstract: Researchers investigated the association between angiotensin I-converting enzyme (ACE) gene polymorphism and gastric cancer progression, focusing on lymph node metastases and tumor stage. Genomic DNA was extracted from tissue specimens and analyzed using agarose gels to identify ACE alleles. The study found a significant correlation between ACE genotypes and the number of lymph node metastases, with patients exhibiting the DD genotype showing higher metastasis counts. However, no significant associations were observed between ACE genotype and tumor type, location, or distant metastases. These findings suggest a potential role for ACE in gastric cancer biology.

title: NOTCH1 and SOX10 in Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma Stem-Like Cells
abstract: This study investigates the role of NOTCH1 and SOX10 in the proliferation and radiation resistance of cancer stem-like cells in Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma (ACC). CD133-positive ACC cells were isolated and found to express NOTCH1 and SOX10, forming spheroids and initiating tumors in nude mice. Knockdown of NOTCH1, SOX10, and FABP7 inhibited spheroidogenesis and induced cell death, highlighting their essential roles in maintaining cancer stem-like cells. The study also identified SKP2 and p27Kip1 as downstream targets of the NOTCH1/FABP7 pathway, with DAPT, a g-secretase inhibitor, showing effects on these processes. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: NR2F1; ROCK; NR2F2; JAG1.

title: Novel CRELD1 Gene Mutations in Patients with Atrioventricular Septal Defect
abstract: This study identified two novel CRELD1 mutations in patients with atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD). A C-to-G transition at nucleotide 857 in exon 8 resulted in an alanine for proline substitution at amino acid 286 in the first calcium-binding EGF domain. Another mutation, a heterozygous c.973G > A transition in exon 9, caused a lysine for glutamic acid substitution at amino acid 325 (E325 K) in the second calcium-binding EGF domain. These mutations were found in patients with isolated partial AVSD and those with Down syndrome, highlighting the role of CRELD1 in AVSD pathogenesis. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: malformations; alanine for proline at amino acid 286; C-to-G transition was identified at nucleotide 857; heart defect; autosomal dominant defects.

title: Gastrointestinal Tolerability of Etoricoxib in Rheumatoid Arthritis Patients
abstract: This study compared the gastrointestinal (GI) tolerability and safety of etoricoxib with diclofenac sodium in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). A total of 4086 participants received etoricoxib 90 mg daily or diclofenac 75 mg twice daily. The primary endpoint was the cumulative rate of discontinuations due to GI adverse experiences (AEs), including oedema-related and hypertension-related events. Etoricoxib showed significantly lower discontinuation rates for GI AEs compared to diclofenac (5.2 vs 8.5 events per 100 patient-years). Aspirin use was permitted, and thrombotic cardiovascular events were monitored. The results highlight etoricoxib's superior tolerability in managing RA-associated GI adverse experiences.

title: POLG Mutations in Alpers' Syndrome and Mitochondrial DNA Depletion
abstract: Alpers' syndrome is a fatal neurogenetic disorder characterized by mitochondrial DNA depletion, seizures, neurodegeneration, and liver disease. Mutations in the POLG gene, including Glu873Stop and G1681A, are associated with the condition. These mutations lead to impaired mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma activity, contributing to the disease's progression. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: Alpers ' syndrome.

title: Amiodarone-Induced Low Back Pain in Atrial Fibrillation Patients
abstract: Two patients with recent-onset atrial fibrillation developed acute low back pain following intravenous amiodarone administration. Amiodarone, an antiarrhythmic drug, was effective for cardioversion but caused this unexpected adverse effect. The association between amiodarone and low back pain suggests a potential negative correlation, while the drug's role in managing atrial fibrillation indicates a positive correlation. No direct relation was found between antiarrhythmic drugs and low back pain in this context.

title: Familial Lattice Corneal Dystrophy Type I with R124C Mutation
abstract: This study reports clinical and genetic findings in a Chilean family with lattice corneal dystrophy type I (LCDI), characterized by the R124C mutation in the TGFBI gene. Genomic analysis using PCR-RFLP with PstI restriction enzyme confirmed the mutation in six affected individuals. The disease exhibited anticipation, with earlier onset in subsequent generations. Affected individuals showed symmetric corneal opacities and variable visual acuity, highlighting the role of TGFBI in LCDI pathogenesis.

title: TAK1's Role in BMP Signaling and Cartilage Development
abstract: TAK1 is essential for BMP signaling in cartilage, as demonstrated by the severe chondrodysplasia and joint abnormalities in TAK1-deficient mice. These mice exhibited elbow dislocation and tarsal fusion, resembling Gdf5-deficient and BMPR1-deficient models. Reduced Smad1/5/8 and p38/Jnk/Erk phosphorylation, along with decreased BMP target gene expression, indicate impaired BMPR signaling. TAK1 mediates Smad1 phosphorylation, highlighting its role in cartilage morphogenesis and growth. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: bone morphogenetic protein receptor (BMPR)1; collagen 2.

title: Atorvastatin Mitigates Contrast-Induced Nephropathy via Anti-Apoptotic Mechanisms
abstract: Atorvastatin ameliorates contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) by suppressing apoptosis through upregulation of heat shock protein (Hsp)27. This study investigated the role of atorvastatin in preventing iopamidol-induced acute renal failure, highlighting its anti-inflammatory and anti-apoptotic effects. In vivo and in vitro experiments demonstrated that atorvastatin reduced Bax/caspase-3 activity while increasing Bcl-2 expression, attenuating renal dysfunction. The findings suggest that atorvastatin protects against inflammatory damage and B cell lymphoma-2 (Bcl-2)-associated X protein-mediated apoptosis in contrast-induced nephropathy. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: (Bax)/caspase-3; Hsp27.

title: Melanocortin-4 Receptor Modulates Insulin Signaling via JNK Regulation
abstract: Melanocortin-4 receptor activation inhibits c-Jun N-terminal kinase activity and enhances insulin signaling. The melanocortin system regulates energy homeostasis, with the Melanocortin-4 receptor modulating insulin signaling through JNK. NDP-MSH, a melanocortin agonist, dose-dependently inhibits JNK activity in MC4R-expressing cells, reversing effects with an antagonist. NDP-MSH reduces IRS-1(ser307) phosphorylation while augmenting AKT phosphorylation in vitro. Melanotan II, a melanocortin analog, increases AKT phosphorylation in rat hypothalamic tissue. NDP-MSH enhances insulin-stimulated glucose uptake in hypothalamic cells. These findings highlight the melanocortinergic system's role in insulin signaling via JNK modulation.

title: A Novel Apolipoprotein E Mutation in a Dyslipidemic Patient with Lipoprotein Glomerulopathy
abstract: A 45-year-old man with dyslipidemia and nephrotic syndrome was diagnosed with lipoprotein glomerulopathy. The patient exhibited lamellate thrombi in glomerular capillaries. Genetic analysis revealed a novel apolipoprotein E mutation, Arg158 Pro, associated with a G to C substitution at codon 158. This mutation, termed apoE Osaka, is linked to the disease. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: dyslipidemic; G to C at codon 158.

title: Star-PAP as a Tumor Suppressor in Breast Cancer
abstract: Star-PAP, a poly(A) polymerase, functions as a tumor suppressor in breast cancer models. Decreased Star-PAP expression is associated with poor prognosis, while its overexpression inhibits breast cancer cell proliferation and induces apoptosis via the mitochondrial pathway. Star-PAP also regulates BIK expression and suppresses tumor growth in NOD/SCID mice. Doxycycline-induced Star-PAP overexpression enhances chemotherapy sensitivity in breast cancer cells.

title: Safety of Celecoxib in Patients with Adverse Skin Reactions to Acetaminophen and Nimesulide
abstract: The study evaluated the tolerability of celecoxib in patients with documented hypersensitivity to acetaminophen and nimesulide, including those with associated reactions to non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. The research focused on skin reactions such as erythema, urticaria-angioedema, and hypersensitivity. Celecoxib, a COX-2 selective inhibitor, was tested in patients who had adverse reactions to analgesic-antipyretic/anti-inflammatory drugs. The study found no adverse reactions, indicating that celecoxib is safe for patients with a history of skin reactions to acetaminophen, nimesulide, or NSAIDs.

title: Efficacy of Ro4368554 in Cholinergic and Serotonergic Memory Deficiency Models
abstract: Ro4368554, a selective 5-HT6 receptor antagonist, ameliorates memory deficiency in cholinergic and serotonergic models. This study demonstrates that Ro4368554 reverses deficits induced by scopolamine and tryptophan depletion, suggesting involvement of both cholinergic and serotonergic pathways. Acetylcholine levels may be modulated by Ro4368554, which acts through 5-HT6 receptors. Comparison with metrifonate, an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor, highlights distinct mechanisms in memory enhancement. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: 5-HT(6 ) receptor antagonists.

title: Efficacy and Tolerability of Valartan/Hydrochlorothiazide Combination Therapy in Hypertensive Patients
abstract: This study compared valsartan/hydrochlorothiazide combination therapy (valsartan 320 mg/hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg) with monotherapy in patients with essential hypertension. The combination therapy demonstrated a positive correlation with blood pressure reduction, while valsartan alone showed a moderate effect. However, valsartan/hydrochlorothiazide was associated with a negative correlation in tolerability, leading to hypokalemia in some patients. The study highlights the importance of balancing efficacy and safety in long-term hypertension management. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: hypertensive.

title: Anxiogenic Effects of Ciprofloxacin and Norfloxacin in Rats
abstract: This study examined the anxiogenic effects of ciprofloxacin and norfloxacin, fluoroquinolones, in adult rats. Oral administration over five days led to increased anxious behaviors in tests like the open-field and elevated plus maze. While both drugs showed similar results, no significant differences were found between them.

title: Adverse Events in HIV-Infected Patients on Generic HAART
abstract: This study examines the incidence of adverse events in HIV-infected patients receiving generic HAART in South India. Common adverse events include rash (15.2%) and peripheral neuropathy (9.0%), with median CD4 counts of 285 and 348 cells/microL, respectively. Clinically significant anemia (hemoglobin <7 g/dL) occurred in 5.4% of patients, and hepatitis (jaundice with ALT >5xULN) in 3.5%. Women were more likely to develop lactic acidosis, while men experienced immune reconstitution syndrome. NVP therapy was linked to rash, and d4 T to neuropathy. Toxicities were observed in 6.4% of patients. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: 3TC; zidovudine; nevirapine; alanine aminotransferase; efavirenz.

title: Salvage Therapy with Nelarabine, Etoposide, and Cyclophosphamide in Pediatric T-Cell Lymphoblastic Leukemia and Lymphoma
abstract: A combination of nelarabine, etoposide, and cyclophosphamide was used as salvage therapy for seven children with relapsed or refractory T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia and lymphoma. Common side effects included Grade 2 and 3 sensory and motor neuropathy, musculoskeletal pain, and hematological toxicity. All patients showed some response, with five achieving complete remission after one or two courses of treatment. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: T-cell lymphoblastic leukaemia and lymphoma; Haematological toxicity.

title: CCK-8 Modulates Morphine-Induced Hippocampal LTP and Memory Impairment
abstract: Cholecystokinin-octapeptide (CCK-8) reversed morphine-induced hippocampal long-term potentiation (LTP) impairment in rats, demonstrating its role in mitigating morphine-induced memory impairment. CCK-8 also enhanced LTP in saline-treated animals, with effects blocked by the CCK2 receptor antagonist L-365,260 but not the CCK1 receptor antagonist L-364,718. These findings suggest CCK-8's ameliorative action on morphine-induced amnesia through CCK2 receptors.

title: Testosterone and Memory Impairment in Male Rats
abstract: Testosterone ameliorates streptozotocin-induced memory impairment in male rats by restoring STL1 and STL2 through the androgen receptor. Flutamide, letrozole, and tamoxifen antagonize this effect, highlighting the role of testosterone in memory function. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: estrogen receptor; aromatase.

title: Polymorphisms and Cancer Risk in Japanese Population
abstract: This study investigates the association between polymorphisms in the IL1B gene, including the C-to-T substitution at -31 and -511C/T variants, and the risk of gastric adenocarcinoma in a Japanese population. The nuclear factor of kappa B (NFkappaB) activation, a key signaling pathway, was linked to cancer development, while the FS-7 cell-associated cell surface antigen (FAS) signaling played a role in signal transduction. Although linkage disequilibrium was observed between the T allele at -511 and C allele at -31, neither the IL1B-31, -511 nor FAS-670 polymorphisms showed significant differences in gastric adenocarcinoma risk. These findings suggest a complex relationship between genetic variations and cancer susceptibility, highlighting the need for further research on the interplay between these factors.

title: Klotho Gene Polymorphism and Essential Hypertension in the Chinese Han Population
abstract: Researchers investigated the association between the G-395A polymorphism in the Klotho gene and essential hypertension in the Chinese Han population. The study compared 215 patients with essential hypertension (EH) and 220 non-hypertensive individuals. Results showed a significant genotype distribution difference (P=0.032), with the G-395A polymorphism linked to EH in older adults, females, and nonsmokers. Klotho's role in arteriosclerosis is highlighted, and the -395A allele was associated with a lower EH risk (OR=0.593, P=0.024) after adjusting for traditional risk factors.

title: Bach1 siRNA Modulates Oxidative Stress in Bleomycin-Induced Pulmonary Fibrosis
abstract: Bach1 siRNA attenuates bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis by modulating oxidative stress in mice. Oxidative stress is linked to inflammation and fibrosis. Bach1, a transcriptional repressor, regulates oxidative stress and is a potential target for pulmonary fibrosis. In this study, Bach1 siRNA was used to knock down Bach1, leading to increased heme oxygenase-1 and glutathione peroxidase 1 expression, while decreasing TGF-b1 and interleukin-6 levels. Bleomycin-induced fibrosis and inflammation were reduced, highlighting Bach1's role in these processes. Additional indexed biomedical mentions considered for relation extraction included: transforming growth factor (TGF)-b1.

title: Case Report: GTN Administration and Hemodynamic Response in a Patient with Chest Pain
abstract: A 60-year-old male with no prior cardiac chest pain experienced an afternoon sleep followed by chest pain. GTN was administered via nasal spray, and oxygen was provided. Shortly after, he developed a drop in blood pressure and heart rate, resolved by atropine sulphate and fluid resuscitation. The patient had a syncopal episode, and the Bezold-Jarish reflex was suspected as the underlying mechanism. This case highlights the potential for GTN to trigger hemodynamic instability in certain patients.

title: Cone Dystrophy with Supernormal Rod Response and KCNV2 Mutations in Retinal Disorders
abstract: Cone dystrophy with supernormal rod response (CDSRR) is a retinal disorder characterized by color vision defects, macular atrophy, and reduced visual acuity. Mutations in KCNV2, a gene associated with CDSRR, were identified in all patients, while PDE6H and PDE6C showed no mutations. This study confirms the association between KCNV2 and CDSRR, highlighting the role of genetic factors in retinal disorders.

title: Mutations in PTCH1 and PTCH2 in Basal Cell Carcinomas and Gorlin Syndrome
abstract: This study investigates mutations in the PTCH1 and PTCH2 genes in sporadic and inherited basal cell carcinomas (BCCs), linking them to Gorlin syndrome and cancer. PTCH1 mutations, such as g.2885G > C (p. R962 T) in exon 17, and g.2839T > G (p. E947stop) in the same exon, are associated with BCCs and inherited autosomal dominant disease. Gorlin syndrome, characterized by multiple BCCs and birth defects, shows mutations in PTCH1. Loss of heterozygosity at D9S180 is observed in three BCCs, while IVS9 + 217 T is present in controls. PTCH2's role remains unclear, with no significant associations found in this cohort.

title: Podocyte Protein Expression in Puromycin Aminonucleoside Nephrosis
abstract: This study investigates the early changes in podocyte-associated proteins, including nephrin, a-actinin, dendrin, and plekhh2, in puromycin aminonucleoside-induced nephrosis. Ultrastructural and permeability alterations were observed, with proteinuria emerging by day 4. Reduced nephrin levels correlated with foot process effacement, while a-actinin remained stable. ACE inhibition did not mitigate these changes, underscoring the role of nephrin in glomerular barrier dysfunction. The findings highlight the association between proteinuria and nephrosis in the context of podocyte protein expression.

title: Genetic Alterations in Japanese Glioblastomas
abstract: This study analyzed genetic alterations in 77 primary glioblastomas from Japanese patients, revealing TP53 mutations in 22% and PTEN mutations in 21% of cases. EGFR amplification was detected in 32% of tumors, while p16 homozygous deletion occurred in 42%. Quantitative microsatellite analysis showed LOH 10q in 69% of glioblastomas. A positive correlation between EGFR amplification and p16 deletion (p=0.009) was observed, whereas a negative correlation between TP53 mutations and p16 deletion (p=0.049) was noted. Additionally, Gln/Gln and codon 787 CAG/CAA variants in the EGFR gene were identified in 3% and 5% of cases, respectively. Radiotherapy was significantly associated with longer survival in glioblastoma patients.

title: Sevoflurane's Role in Modulating Lidocaine-Induced Convulsions
abstract: This study examines the effects of sevoflurane on lidocaine-induced convulsions and toxicity in cats. Sevoflurane increased the convulsive threshold, with a ceiling effect observed at higher concentrations. Enflurane showed no significant difference in threshold. Apamin, a calcium-dependent potassium channel blocker, was tested to investigate mechanisms, though it slightly reduced the threshold without statistical significance. The study suggests sevoflurane mitigates lidocaine toxicity, potentially linked to depression in blood pressure dynamics.

title: Behavioral Effects of Anabolic Androgenic Steroid and Serotonin Depletion in Pubertal Rats
abstract: Chronic exposure to anabolic androgenic steroid (AAS) and serotonin depletion using parachlorophenylalanine (PCPA) significantly increased irritability in pubertal male rats. Brain levels of serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine, 5-HT) and its metabolite 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA) were measured, showing PCPA-induced depletion. Testosterone administration alone increased partner preference and aggression, while AAS exposure interacted with serotonin depletion to modulate behavioral outcomes.

title: Evaluation of Dextran-Etodolac Conjugates for Enhanced Anti-inflammatory Activity
abstract: Dextran-etodolac conjugates were synthesized and evaluated for their anti-inflammatory properties. The conjugates, formed via ester bonding, demonstrated improved solubility and reduced gastrointestinal side effects. In vivo tests using carrageenan-induced edema models and acetic acid-induced writhing models showed significant analgesic and anti-inflammatory effects. The antiinflammatory drug etodolac retained efficacy in these models, highlighting the potential of Dextran-etodolac as a therapeutic agent.
